===== https://testing.polyester.com/docs/api-docs/rest/POST/v1/auth/address-book-entries/address_book_entry_id:copy =====

AddressBookService Copy Address Book Entry Copy one address-book entry into another visible root or subaccount book. Interactive callers with enrolled MFA need recent assurance; API keys need MANAGE_ADDRESS_BOOK.    Copy URL        Method  POST   Path /v1/auth/address-book-entries/{address_book_entry_id}:copy    Visibility Authentication required    MFA Requirement Conditionally required   POST /v1/auth/address-book-entries/{address_book_entry_id}:copy       Send  Request  Development    cURL         curl --request POST \ \
  --url 'https://api-devnet.polyester.ai/v1/auth/address-book-entries/1:copy' \
  --header 'Accept: */*' \
  --header 'X-API-KEY-ID: YOUR_API_KEY_ID' \
  --header 'X-API-TIMESTAMP: YOUR_API_TIMESTAMP' \
  --header 'X-API-SIGNATURE: YOUR_API_SIGNATURE' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "targetSubaccountId": "6789012345678"
}'     Responses        {
  "entry": {
    "addressBookEntryId": "1",
    "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "external": {
      "address": "0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333",
      "polychainChainId": 1
    },
    "kind": "EXTERNAL_CHAIN",
    "label": "Treasury Wallet",
    "note": "Primary treasury destination.",
    "revision": "1",
    "scope": {
      "rootAccountId": "7563897446546",
      "scopeType": "ROOT",
      "subaccountId": "37HAHbBRCeY"
    },
    "tags": [
      {
        "color": "#7C3AED",
        "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "name": "Treasury",
        "scope": {
          "rootAccountId": "7563897446546",
          "scopeType": "ROOT",
          "subaccountId": "37bbZLLApNf"
        },
        "tagId": "1",
        "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}        Authorization   x-api-key  string  required    Samples use X-API-KEY-ID, X-API-TIMESTAMP, X-API-SIGNATURE.  Default key     Headers   Accept  string  header    Requested response media type.  */*  x-polyester-mock  boolean  default: false   Enable mocked API responses for this request.     Path parameters  Example  address_book_entry_id  string (int64)   required    > 0      Address-book entry id to copy.         Request body     Form  JSON      Example    targetSubaccountId  string (int64)    Optional destination subaccount. Omit to copy into the root account address book.        Response     Form  JSON        entry  object    Newly copied address book entry.  11 fields     addressBookEntryId  string (fixed64)    Stable public id of the saved address-book entry.  Example 1   scope  object    Address book that owns this entry.  3 fields     scopeType  enum    Address-book scope type.  SCOPE_ROOT  SCOPE_SUBACCOUNT  Example ROOT   rootAccountId  string (fixed64)    Root account that owns this address book.  Example 7563897446546   subaccountId  string (fixed64)    Subaccount for subaccount-scoped books. Empty for root account books.  Example 37HAHbBRCeY   kind  enum    Type of saved destination.  EXTERNAL_CHAIN  INTERNAL_ACCOUNT  Example EXTERNAL_CHAIN   label  string    User-defined display label.  Example Treasury Wallet   note  string    Optional user-defined note.  Example Primary treasury destination.   createdAt  string (date-time)    Time this entry was created, as a UTC timestamp.  Example 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z   updatedAt  string (date-time)    Time this entry was last updated, as a UTC timestamp.  Example 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z   external  object    External chain withdraw destination.  2 fields     polychainChainId  integer (int32)    External network identifier for the destination address.  Example 1   address  string    Destination address on the selected external network.  Example 0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333   internal  object    Internal account transfer destination.  6 fields     rootAccountId  string (fixed64)    Root account that owns the target internal account.     targetAccountId  string (fixed64)    Target account or subaccount public id.     targetScopeType  enum    Whether target_account_id identifies a root account or a subaccount.  SCOPE_ROOT  SCOPE_SUBACCOUNT     smartAccountAddress  string    Smart account address for the internal transfer destination.     rootUsername  string    Username for the destination root account, when available.     subaccountLabel  string    Label for the destination subaccount, when the destination is a subaccount.     tags  object[]    Tags currently attached to this entry.  6 fields     tagId  string (fixed64)    Stable public id of the tag.  Example 1   scope  object    Address book scope where this tag exists.  3 fields     scopeType  enum    Address-book scope type.  SCOPE_ROOT  SCOPE_SUBACCOUNT  Example ROOT   rootAccountId  string (fixed64)    Root account that owns this address book.  Example 7563897446546   subaccountId  string (fixed64)    Subaccount for subaccount-scoped books. Empty for root account books.  Example 37bbZLLApNf   name  string    Human-readable tag name.  Example Treasury   color  string (color)    Optional UI color token for this tag.  Example #7C3AED   createdAt  string (date-time)    Time the tag was created, as a UTC timestamp.  Example 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z   updatedAt  string (date-time)    Time this tag was last updated, as a UTC timestamp.  Example 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z   revision  string (uint64)    Monotonic resource revision used for conditional updates. You get one place to use Assets from supported chains. Deposit through one chain, then trade, lend, borrow, or withdraw through another supported route . Decentralized finance (DeFi) has had this problem for years. The same Asset is split across blockchains, exchanges, and lending markets that can't share liquidity. Polyester combines those markets, so the chain you start on doesn't limit what you can do next.       Core features   Permissionless and non-custodial Polyester does not require KYC checks. Your owner wallet  stays in control of your account and private keys.  Advanced spot trading Dedicated order books and a spot interface give you execution tools, market data, and order controls.  High-performance matching PolyEngine  matches up to 1 million transactions per second, with 1 ms 99th percentile (P99) latency.   Broad chain support Polyester currently supports 16  networks and 15  Unified Assets , including:    Arbitrum Sepolia     Avalanche C Fuji     Base Sepolia     Bitcoin Cash Testnet     Bitcoin Testnet     BNB Smart Chain Testnet     Dogecoin Testnet     Ethereum Classic Testnet     Ethereum Sepolia     HyperEVM Testnet     Litecoin Testnet     Polygon Amoy     Ripple Testnet     Robinhood Testnet     Solana Devnet     Tron Nile   9 More 8 More  See Supported Assets for every listed chain and Asset.   Unified Assets Compatible versions of the same Asset from multiple chains become one Unified Asset. You can trade, lend, or borrow that Asset in one interface.   Capital-efficient lending and borrowing Use supported Assets from any connected chain as collateral. Those Assets can keep working while you borrow.  Cross-account collateral and permissions Assign members, roles, and application programming interface (API) keys across a Master Account  and its Subaccounts . Eligible accounts can share collateral to set access, liquidity, and risk.   Customizable workspace You can arrange charts, order books, order entry, and account data around the markets you use.  Institutional APIs Institutions can integrate through Financial Information eXchange (FIX), WebSocket, and Simple Binary Encoding (SBE). Other APIs are also available.  Developer and AI integrations Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and software development kits (SDKs) connect developers and AI agents to Polyester markets. Developers and agents can then build on that liquidity.  Together, these features make Polyester the ultimate liquidity hub across supported chains and Assets. Polyester brings together unified liquidity with a high-performance chain, advanced exchange infrastructure, and open integrations built for the next generation of DeFi. Deposit and withdraw Each Master Account and Subaccount has chain-specific deposit addresses. Zipper  verifies the source-chain transaction and creates a 1:1-backed Zipped Asset  on Polyester Chain. The Funding Account  credits the matching Unified Asset.   Deposit Funds  Send a supported Asset from an external wallet. A withdrawal uses an available Zipped Asset route. Zipper then returns the native Asset to the external address. What you can move depends on current listings, routes, fees, and confirmation requirements.   Withdraw Funds  Send a balance out to an external wallet. Spot trading Polyester spot trading lets you trade supported Asset Pairs through dedicated order books with institutional-grade latency. Most decentralized exchanges begin with the Assets already available on one chain. Polyester is built to bring Assets from both EVM and non-EVM chains into the same exchange, including Assets that rarely meet in one native decentralized venue.  Spot trading overview  Order books, order types, and how execution works. The Unified Trading Account  brings deposited balances into dedicated spot order books. Equivalent versions of the same Asset share one trading balance, removing the need for a different exchange or balance for every source chain.
This creates a path for markets that are difficult to serve in a chain-specific DEX. Every Pair remains its own market with its own order book. Polyester unifies access to liquidity, not unrelated Assets or prices.  Example: Non-EVM and EVM Assets in one venue   When supported, Assets arriving from    Bitcoin ,    XRP ,    Dogecoin , and    Litecoin  can trade in the same ecosystem as Assets arriving from    Ethereum ,    Solana ,    Base ,    Avalanche , and other chains. Spot VIP tiers Your VIP tier sets the maker  and taker  rates you pay on spot trades: Higher tiers receive lower rates See the current rates on the VIP fee schedule Bridge and swap across chains Unified Asset balances connect supported chain routes. You can move the same Asset between chains, or trade it for a different Asset before you withdraw. Bridge. Deposit through one supported chain and withdraw the same Asset natively through another. No trade is required.  Example: Bridge USDC from Ethereum to Solana   You deposit    USDC on    Ethereum . Polyester credits one    USDC Unified Asset. You can then withdraw native    USDC on    Solana . No trade is required. Swap. Deposit through one supported chain, trade on a spot book, then withdraw a different Asset.  Example: Swap BTC for USDT   Native    BTC can enter through the    Bitcoin  route, trade for    USDT, and leave through a supported    USDT route on another chain. For a same-Asset transfer, Polyester keeps the source route and its 1:1 backing, then uses available inventory on the destination route to fill the withdrawal. Shared Unified Asset balances let liquidity across routes serve that transfer. You do not need a separate pool for every pair of chains. Availability depends on current listings, supported deposit and withdrawal routes, destination inventory, fees, minimums, confirmation requirements, and route health. A cross-Asset swap also needs an available Pair and enough order-book liquidity.   Quick Swap  Convert one Asset into another and deliver it to a chosen wallet. Lend and borrow Polyester gives lenders and borrowers access to liquidity gathered from every supported route for an Asset, rather than a single chain-specific pool. Chain-specific lending platforms often divide one asset into separate markets. USDT on Ethereum may sit in a different pool from USDT on Solana, even though both represent the same economic asset. Each pool has its own supply, demand, utilization, and rates. Polyester brings supported versions of the same asset into one Unified Asset balance before that balance reaches the lending market. A USDT deposit from Ethereum and a USDT deposit from Solana can therefore participate in the same USDT lending market rather than competing in isolated chain-specific pools. Polyester's portfolio-aware risk engine takes this capital efficiency further. Eligible Assets in your Unified Trading Account continue to contribute collateral value while they are committed to open orders, so placing an Asset on the book does not make that capital unproductive.   Example: Use BTC as productive collateral for market making  A market maker  quoting the       BTC/USDT   market can use one original collateral position to support liquidity on both sides of the order book: Sell side. Place deposited    BTC in resting sell orders. Collateral. Eligible    BTC committed to those open orders continues to contribute collateral value, allowing the market maker to borrow    USDT. Buy side. Place the borrowed    USDT in resting buy orders. The original    BTC collateral can therefore support sell-side inventory and buy-side liquidity at the same time. By evaluating eligible balances and open orders together, Polyester keeps market-making capital productive across trading and borrowing instead of requiring it to sit idle in separate accounts. If you lend, you gain access to demand gathered around the Asset instead of one route. If you borrow, you gain access to supply gathered from every supported route. For the market as a whole, liquidity can become deeper and more useful because it is no longer divided by chain. Unified liquidity Polyester brings liquidity from supported chains into one place, giving every market access to deeper, more useful liquidity. Polyester turns chains into connected routes around a shared exchange rather than separate destinations with separate liquidity. A better trading experience. You can access more supported Assets in one set of spot markets. A better bridging experience. You can deposit the same Asset through one supported chain and withdraw it through another. A better cross-chain swap experience. You can deposit, trade, and withdraw through one path across otherwise disconnected ecosystems. A better lending experience. You can lend or borrow equivalent Assets through one market instead of multiple chain-specific pools. Underneath that experience, Polyester keeps the system verifiable. Zipper preserves route-specific, 1:1 backing for Assets brought onto Polyester Chain. The Funding Account records unified on-chain balances. PolyEngine provides low-latency order matching while account balances, active orders, and trading strategies remain private. Your non-custodial owner wallet controls the Polyester smart wallet associated with your Master Account and Subaccounts. Polyester does not hold your private keys or become the owner of your account.   Supported Assets  Current Asset and chain routes, plus fees and minimums. These concepts follow an Asset from its source chain into Polyester, through your account, and onto an order book. Core Systems Polyester Chain Polyester Chain  is Polyester's EVM-compatible Layer 1. It is the on-chain foundation of the Polyester Exchange and Zipper , where Zipped Assets , Safe smart accounts , Funding Account  balances, and the Trading Gateway and Zipper contracts live. Validators verify every transaction and agree on each new block. This creates a shared, publicly auditable record of Asset supplies, balances, account controls, and protocol activity that you can view through Polyester Scan .   Polyester Chain  How the chain, accounts, and on-chain balances work. Zipper Zipper connects supported external chains to Polyester. It wraps ("zips") external Assets into tokens on Polyester Chain and unwraps ("unzips") them for supported Withdrawals. Every Zipped Asset stays tied to its exact Asset and source chain. Zipper validates Deposits and Withdrawals while keeping the supply, backing, and Withdrawal path for each route  separate. Zipped Assets A Zipped Asset is an ERC-20 token on Polyester Chain that represents an Asset from an external chain. Its on-chain supply is backed 1:1 by the equivalent Asset held in that route's vault  on the original source chain.   Example: Separate zUSDT routes  If 100    USDT is deposited through    Ethereum  and 50    USDT through    Solana , Polyester creates 100    Ethereum     zUSDT and 50    Solana     zUSDT. These are independent Zipped Assets with separate supplies and backing. The Asset held in the vault on the original source chain and the corresponding Zipped Asset supply on Polyester Chain are both publicly auditable. Each route remains independent, so its supply, backing, and Withdrawal path can be verified separately.   Zipper  How source-chain Assets become Zipped Assets and Unified Assets. PolyEngine PolyEngine  powers Polyester's order-book trading, settlement, and lending liquidations. It maintains order books, reserves balances, matches Orders, settles Fills, and provides API connectivity for market makers , high-frequency traders, AI agents, and other services. Each spot Pair can process up to 500,000 transactions per second through PolyEngine, with end-to-end matching latency below one millisecond. This gives traders institutional-grade execution speed, while PolyEngine's reservation, settlement, and liquidation controls keep balances, trades, and lending positions consistent throughout their lifecycle.   PolyEngine  Order matching, settlement, and API connectivity. Polyester Scan Polyester Scan is Polyester's blockchain Explorer. Use it to view public records for blocks, Transactions, contracts, Zipped Assets, and Deposit and Withdrawal Flows . Polyester Scan focuses on public chain evidence. Private credentials, account balances, active Orders, Fill attribution, and the internal trading ledger remain outside the public Explorer.   Polyester Scan  Public records for blocks, Transactions, and Flows. Accounts and Balances Smart Wallet Your smart wallet is the on-chain account controlled by your connected or embedded owner wallet . It authorizes account activity on Polyester Chain while your owner wallet remains in control of your private keys. The smart wallet establishes who can act on the account. Zipper custody paths and Polyester application contracts separately hold or account for Assets as they move through supported products. Polyester sponsors the gas fees for current user-facing activity on Polyester Chain, so you can authorize on-chain actions without holding its native gas Asset. This gas abstraction  applies to Polyester Chain. External chains still charge their own transaction fees.   Smart wallet  The on-chain account your owner wallet controls.   Gas abstraction  How Polyester sponsors gas on Polyester Chain. Funding Account The Funding Account is where you manage on-chain balances for Deposits, Withdrawals, internal transfers, and transfers to Trading. When a supported Deposit arrives, Polyester keeps the Zipped Asset as backing and credits the matching Unified Asset  balance to Funding.   Zipper credits deposits directly to your Polyester Funding or Trading Account under your smart wallet's control. You never need to receive or hold Zipped Assets in MetaMask, Phantom, or another external wallet. Assets remain outside the lending liquidation engine while they are in Funding, so they cannot be liquidated or used as collateral for margin trading. Transfer a balance to the Unified Trading Account  when you want to use it for an Order.   Funding Account  On-chain balances for deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Unified Assets A Unified Asset combines supported versions of the same Asset into one Funding or Trading balance. Polyester explicitly assigns eligible Zipped Asset routes to the same Unified Asset, so a matching ticker or wrapped variant alone does not combine them. A Unified Asset is an on-chain accounting record rather than an ERC-20 token. It is publicly auditable, while every Zipped Asset beneath it keeps its own token supply and 1:1 vault backing.   Unified Assets  On-chain balances for deposits, withdrawals, and transfers.   Example: Combine zUSDT into one balance  A user's 100    Ethereum     zUSDT and 50    Solana     zUSDT appear as one 150    uUSDT balance for Funding and Trading. Polyester still tracks each    zUSDT supply and its source-chain backing separately. Unified Trading Account The Unified Trading Account holds the private balances you use for trading. When you transfer a balance from Funding to Trading, PolyEngine can use it to create and settle Orders for that Asset. Each Trading balance shows a total, available, and reserved amount. Active Orders and other pending activity can reserve part of the balance until they Fill, are canceled, or reach another final state.   Unified Trading Account  Private balances used to place and settle Orders. Master Accounts and Subaccounts A Master Account  is your top-level Polyester account. It controls account-wide settings, security, the VIP tier, and every Subaccount  created beneath it. All Subaccounts share the Master Account's VIP tier. A Subaccount gives you a separate environment for balances, members, policies, activity, and API keys . Each Subaccount has its own Funding and Trading balances. Switching the active account changes which balances, Orders, and permissions you are managing.   Subaccounts  Separate balances, members, and API keys under a Master Account. Trading Pair A Pair is one market between two Assets: a base Asset  and a quote Asset . Every Pair has its own order book where those Assets can be bought and sold. The source chain does not change the Pair. Supported versions of each Asset trade through the same Unified Asset balance and order book.   Example: ETH/USDT across multiple source chains  The       ETH/USDT   Pair trades    uETH against    uUSDT.    ETH deposited from    Base  or    Arbitrum  becomes part of the same    uETH Trading balance, while    USDT deposited from    Ethereum  or    Solana  becomes part of the same    uUSDT balance. Polyester uses one       ETH/USDT   order book, not a separate Pair for each source chain. Order Book An order book lists the buy and sell Orders available for one Pair. Polyester uses price-time priority: the best price comes first, and earlier Orders take priority when multiple Orders have the same price. PolyEngine maintains a separate order book for every Pair. Its liquidity comes from balances held in Polyester Unified Trading Accounts rather than an external DEX, AMM, bridge pool, exchange, or third-party solver. How These Concepts Fit Together Follow an Asset through Polyester from Deposit to Withdrawal: Your smart wallet authorizes the account on Polyester Chain. Zipper brings a supported Asset into Polyester from its source chain. The Deposit creates a source-chain-specific Zipped Asset backed 1:1 by the original Asset. The Funding Account combines eligible Zipped Assets into one Unified Asset balance. Moving that balance to the Unified Trading Account makes it available to PolyEngine. PolyEngine accepts and matches Orders on the Pair's order book. Fills update private Trading records, while Market Trades publish completed exchange activity. Move funds back to the Funding Account before making a supported external Withdrawal. Polyester Scan shows the public chain and cross-chain Flow records for the journey. Next Steps  Create Your Account  Choose how to sign in, create your non-custodial Master Account, and protect the wallet that controls it. Secure Your Account  Protect your owner credential, add MFA, save recovery codes, and configure withdrawal and transfer whitelists. First Deposit & Trade  Deposit an Asset, make it available in Trading, and place your first spot Order.          Previous What is Polyester? You can create an embedded wallet with Google or email, or connect a wallet you already control through MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, or WalletConnect. Overview The wallet address becomes the owner credential for your account. Your first successful sign-in creates a Master Account , and the same owner wallet opens it on future visits. Every Master Account and Subaccount  also receives its own Safe smart account  on Polyester Chain . The owner wallet controls that smart account, so protecting the wallet protects access to your Polyester account and funds. Polyester does not create a separate username and password. You can add a username from Profile when that field is available, but it is display information rather than a sign-in credential.   Polyester never holds your private keys. Only your owner wallet can open the account and authorize its activity. Create your account The options on the Create Account screen work for both account creation and future sign-ins. Choose a method you can protect and recover over the long term. Each path creates or opens the Master Account tied to that owner wallet.        Google or email Browser wallet WalletConnect   Google or email   Embedded wallet Google and email create an embedded non-custodial owner wallet through Turnkey. Your Google identity or email is how you return to that wallet. Use the same identity every time. A different Google account or email address can create or open a different Polyester account.  1 Choose Google or Email Select Google or Email on the Create Account screen. Both options create an embedded non-custodial owner wallet through Turnkey.  Connect with Google        2 Verify the identity Continue with Google or enter the verification code sent to your email address. 3 Open your Master Account Polyester creates the Master Account and opens it with the embedded owner wallet. Turnkey stores the embedded wallet's private key in encrypted form and decrypts it only inside secure enclaves for authorized signing. Polyester does not receive the raw private key during account use. You can export the private key through the Polyester interface. The key is revealed only during that export, and Polyester is not notified when you request it.  Keep exported private keys safe Store an exported private key securely and never share it. Anyone with the key may be able to control the wallet and its Polyester account.   Browser wallet Use MetaMask, Rabby, or Phantom if you already control a browser wallet. The active address becomes the owner credential for your Master Account. Private keys and recovery stay inside the selected wallet. Return with the same wallet and address.  1 Choose a wallet Select MetaMask, Rabby, or Phantom on the Create Account screen.  Connect a wallet  2 Confirm the address Unlock the wallet and confirm that the address you want to use is active. 3 Sign in Review and sign the authentication message to prove that you control the address. Polyester then creates or opens the Master Account tied to that wallet.       The authentication signature proves control of the wallet address. It does not transfer an Asset, approve spending, or require a seed phrase or private key. Signing in is an off-chain action and costs no gas. It also does not deploy the Safe smart account. Polyester deploys the Safe with the account's first Deposit on Polyester Chain. WalletConnect   Desktop or mobile WalletConnect connects another compatible desktop or mobile wallet. Approve the connection in that wallet, then sign in with its active address. Private keys stay in the wallet you connect.  1 Choose WalletConnect Select WalletConnect on the Create Account screen.  Connect with WalletConnect  2 Approve the connection Pick the desktop or mobile wallet and approve the WalletConnect request there.       3 Sign in Review and sign the authentication message in the connected wallet. Polyester then creates or opens the Master Account tied to that address. The authentication signature proves control of the wallet address. It does not transfer an Asset, approve spending, or require a seed phrase or private key. Signing in is an off-chain action and costs no gas. It also does not deploy the Safe smart account. Polyester deploys the Safe with the account's first Deposit on Polyester Chain. Confirm your Master Account Account creation is complete when Polyester opens your Master Account. The account menu shows the current owner identity and Safe smart account, so you can confirm which account is active.  1 Open the account menu View the authenticated Master Account and the identity used to sign in.       2 View the smart account address This address identifies the account's activity on Polyester Chain. 3 Confirm the account Compare the identity and smart account address with your records before making a Deposit.  Missing balances can mean the wrong account If the expected balances are missing, stop before depositing again. Sign out and return with the exact wallet address, Google identity, or email address used to create the Master Account. Protect your owner wallet The owner wallet controls your Master Account and authorizes its chain-visible activity. Polyester does not hold its private keys and cannot replace the wallet's own recovery method. Sign-in path Where the private key is protected What the user must protect MetaMask, Rabby, or Phantom Inside the selected wallet The wallet, device access, and its recovery keysWalletConnect Inside the wallet connected through WalletConnect The connected wallet, device access, and its recovery keysGoogle or email Stored as an encrypted private key by Turnkey and used inside secure enclaves The exact Google identity or mailbox and its recovery methods    Add MFA and recovery methods before funding the account. Polyester MFA  protects sensitive account actions, but it does not replace the owner wallet or its recovery method. Your original owner credential remains tied to the Master Account. Polyester does not currently provide a general flow to link another sign-in method, replace or unlink the owner credential, or close or delete the Master Account. Protect and reuse the exact method selected during account creation.  Keep recovery keys private Polyester support will never ask for a seed phrase, private key, email verification code, or MFA recovery code. Anyone who obtains these recovery keys may be able to control the account.   Access and security  MFA, sessions, API keys, and withdrawal allowlists for the account you just created. FAQ   Which wallets can I use to create an account?  The Create Account screen supports MetaMask, Rabby, and Phantom directly. WalletConnect can connect another compatible desktop or mobile wallet. The selected wallet address becomes the owner credential for the Master Account.   Who creates the wallet when I use Google or email?  Turnkey creates and secures the embedded non-custodial owner wallet. Google verifies the selected Google identity, while email verifies access to the selected mailbox. Polyester uses the resulting wallet to create or reopen the Master Account.   Where are my private keys stored?  With MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, or WalletConnect, the private keys remain in the connected wallet. With Google or email, Turnkey stores the encrypted private key and decrypts it only inside secure enclaves for authorized signing. Polyester does not receive the raw private key in either path.   Does every account get a smart account?  Yes. Every Master Account and Subaccount receives its own Safe smart account. The Safe identifies the account on Polyester Chain, while the owner credential controls it.   Why did signing in show an account with no balances?  A different wallet address, Google identity, or email address can open a different Polyester account. Sign out, return with the identity used during account creation, and confirm the smart account address before taking another action.   Can I add another sign-in method to the same Master Account?  Not currently. Another wallet address, Google identity, or email address may open a different Master Account rather than link to the existing one.   What happens if I lose access to my sign-in method?  Recovery depends on the owner wallet. Use the wallet's recovery process for an external wallet, or recover the linked Google identity or mailbox for an embedded wallet. If access to an embedded wallet's provider is permanently lost and its private key was not exported beforehand, Polyester cannot replace that owner. MFA and recovery codes do not change Safe ownership. Next Steps  Secure Your Account  Protect your owner credential, add MFA, save recovery codes, and configure withdrawal and transfer whitelists. The owner wallet  controls your account, MFA  verifies sensitive actions, and on-chain whitelists restrict where Assets can be sent. Each layer protects something different, so the strongest setup uses all three. Start with the owner wallet. Polyester cannot replace its private keys or transfer ownership to a new sign-in method if you lose access. The safeguards inside Polyester strengthen that foundation, but they do not replace it.  Never share account secrets Polyester support will never ask for your seed phrase, private key, verification code, MFA code, recovery code, or API private signing key. Anyone who obtains this information may be able to control your account. Protect the wallet that owns your account The sign-in method you selected during account creation is the owner credential for your Master Account . It controls the account's Safe smart account  on Polyester Chain .        Google Email MetaMask Phantom Rabby WalletConnect  Google This Google identity unlocks a Turnkey embedded wallet that owns your Master Account. That wallet controls the account's Safe on Polyester Chain.   Embedded wallet Protect the exact Google account used at sign-in. Keep Google recovery current, including a backup email, phone number, or passkey. If you exported the Turnkey private key, store it offline and never send it to support. MFA cannot replace this identity if you lose it. Secure your Google Account MFA inside Polyester cannot recover or replace the owner wallet. Losing the wallet, Google identity, or email address may permanently remove your ability to control the account.   Sign-in and ownership  How your wallet, Google account, or email connects to your Polyester account. Add MFA MFA adds a separate verification check to sensitive actions started from an interactive Polyester session. You can enroll a passkey, an authenticator app, or both. A passkey can use Face ID, Touch ID, or a compatible hardware key. An authenticator app generates a rotating six-digit code. Polyester can require fresh MFA when you: Withdraw Assets or send an internal transfer. Weaken a whitelist requirement or change an approved destination. Create, disable, or revoke an API key . Remove an MFA method or regenerate recovery codes. Open Security, choose Add a passkey or Add an authenticator app, and follow the verification prompt. Give each method a recognizable name so you can identify the device or app later. When setup is complete, confirm that it appears under Multi-Factor Authentication. MFA confirms that you approved an action. It does not decide whether a destination is trusted, replace your owner wallet, or apply an on-chain restriction. Polyester may also request a fresh verification for a high-risk action even when your current session has already completed MFA.   MFA and recovery  Add a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes available if you lose a method. Save your recovery codes Your first MFA enrollment provides a set of single-use recovery codes. Store them somewhere private and separate from the device you normally use to sign in. Before completing setup, make sure you can recover the saved copy. Recovery codes restore access when an MFA method is unavailable. They do not replace the owner wallet, Google identity, or email address that controls the account. Regenerating the set invalidates every previous code, so discard any older copies.  Keep a backup method Polyester prevents you from removing your final MFA method. Add and verify a replacement before retiring a device or authenticator app. Restrict withdrawals and transfers On-chain whitelists restrict the destinations your Funding Account  can send Assets to. They remain effective after you complete MFA because they are enforced by the account itself. External withdrawal whitelist: Allows Withdrawals only to approved addresses on external chains. Internal transfer whitelist: Allows internal transfers only to approved Polyester accounts. These controls are independent and off by default. Enable them separately for each Master Account or Subaccount  you want to protect. Subaccounts do not inherit whitelist settings from the Master Account. Saving a destination in the Address Book gives it a reusable label, but does not approve it. Add the destination to the correct whitelist before enabling the requirement. Verify every address or Polyester account through another trusted channel first. Adding or removing an approved destination, or disabling a whitelist requirement, requires fresh verification and GuardSigner  approval. If the Security page shows a missing GuardSigner, select Set up. If the account is waiting for on-chain initialization, select Initialize and wait until its status is Ready. MFA and whitelists serve different purposes. MFA verifies your approval. A whitelist limits where the Funding Account can send Assets, even after your identity has been verified. Deposit routing is separate The Default Deposit Destination setting controls whether accepted Deposits credit your Funding Account or Unified Trading Account . It is not a whitelist and does not approve a Withdrawal address. An external Withdrawal still follows the Funding Account and Zipper  security path regardless of where the Deposit was first credited.   Address Book and whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. Review your security before adding funds Confirm that every enrolled MFA method has a recognizable name. Store recovery codes separately from your primary device. Make sure your owner wallet, Google identity, or email address has a working recovery method. Review saved destinations and enable the appropriate whitelist requirements. Remember that signing out affects only the current browser. Polyester does not currently provide cross-device session management or individual remote session revocation. Review these settings again whenever a device, owner identity, team member, API key, or trusted destination changes. If you suspect a compromise Respond from a trusted device and secure the owner identity first. Lock down the connected wallet, Google identity, or mailbox through its verified provider before routine account cleanup.  1 Secure the owner identity Lock down the connected wallet, Google identity, or mailbox through its verified provider. If the owner credential may be exposed, securing it is the first priority.   Polyester does not currently provide a Master Account emergency freeze. A Subaccount freeze, policy halt, or API-key revocation protects only that specific resource. 2 Revoke unfamiliar access Sign out of every accessible browser and disable exposed or unfamiliar API keys. Polyester does not currently support cross-device session management or individual remote session revocation. 3 Review every account scope Check Subaccount members, roles, permissions, trusted destinations, whitelists, recent activity, and open Orders. Send Assets only to verified destinations that you control.   Cancel unfamiliar open Orders to release any Assets held in reserved Trading balances before you try to move them. 4 Preserve evidence Record timestamps, account identifiers, session details, and transaction IDs before contacting official support. Never include private keys, seed phrases, MFA codes, or recovery codes.  Sessions and alerts  Manage account sessions and respond to unfamiliar activity. FAQ   Why do I need MFA if my wallet is already secure?  The owner wallet controls your smart account. MFA separately verifies sensitive actions performed in an interactive Polyester session. One layer does not replace the other.   Should I choose a passkey or an authenticator app?  Choose a method you can keep available on trusted devices. A passkey can use device biometrics or a hardware security key when supported. An authenticator app generates time-based six-digit codes. Enrolling both gives you a backup if one becomes unavailable.   What happens if I lose an MFA method?  Use another enrolled method or one unused recovery code. After restoring access, add a replacement method and regenerate your recovery codes if their storage may have been exposed.   Can Polyester recover my owner wallet or bypass MFA?  Polyester cannot recreate a non-custodial wallet's private keys, bypass the credential that owns your smart account, or replace a permanently lost embedded owner wallet through MFA. Recovery depends on the wallet provider, linked Google identity or mailbox, another enrolled MFA method, or recovery keys that already exist.   Should I export the Turnkey wallet's private key?  Export is not required to use Polyester. An export reveals the private key that controls the embedded owner wallet, so use it only for a deliberate backup or migration. Keep it offline and never send it to support.   Does saving an Address Book entry automatically allow transfers?  No. The Address Book saves destination information for convenience. External withdrawal and internal transfer whitelists separately determine which destinations are permitted when their requirements are active.   Does MFA replace an on-chain whitelist?  No. MFA verifies who approved a protected action. Whitelists enforce where Assets may move. A Withdrawal can require valid MFA and still be restricted to an approved address. ALPHA Markets Trade    More    Search /   Deposit Assets     @ForkOwl           Open menu     ALPHA   @ForkOwl   More Options  Funding Transfer Withdraw Deposit Profile Ledger Settings    Markets Trade Search Orders Dashboard    User Docs  Developer Docs  SDK  API Docs         Discord         Start Here   What is Polyester?   Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Start Here /First Deposit & Trade   First Deposit & Trade  07/27    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    Your first trade starts with an Asset you already hold. Deposit that Asset into Polyester, make the balance available in Trading, find a market that exchanges it for the Asset you want, and place an Order. After the Order fills, the Asset you received appears in your Unified Trading Account . Before you deposit Confirm these first: Create an account so Polyester can assign a deposit address Secure your account so the owner wallet  and MFA  are in place Confirm the selected Master Account  or Subaccount  so the credited balance appears there Hold a supported Asset on the network you'll send from Deposit, trade, and check your new balance This journey works whether your completed Deposit credits Funding first or goes directly to Unified Trading.  1 Deposit an Asset Open Deposit, select the Asset, and choose the network where it currently exists. Copy the address directly from Polyester and send the Asset from your source wallet or exchange. Include the exact memo or destination tag when one is shown.   Each account gets one deposit address per supported chain, not per Asset. Supported EVM networks share that EVM address. The wrong network, address, or memo can prevent a Deposit from crediting. Verify before sending.       Wait for the required source-chain confirmations. If the completed Deposit appears in Funding, open Transfer and move the amount you want to trade into Unified Trading. If it already appears as an available Trading balance, continue to the next step.   Your Default Deposit Destination can be Funding or Unified Trading. You can review this setting under Deposit Routing on Security.   Deposit Funds  Learn more about depositing funds.   Internal Transfers  Learn more about internal transfers. 2 Find a market for the deposited Asset Open Spot Markets and search for the ticker you deposited. Choose a Pair that contains both the Asset you have and the Asset you want to receive.         The first ticker is the Base Asset . The second is the Quote Asset . In       BTC/USDT  , selling    BTC gives you    USDT, while buying    BTC spends    USDT.   Trading Screen  Learn more about the trading screen. 3 Choose Buy or Sell and place the Order Choose Sell when you hold the Base Asset and want the Quote Asset. Choose Buy when you hold the Quote Asset and want the Base Asset. Confirm the active account, enter the amount, select a Market or Limit Order, review the estimated total and fees, then place the Order.        Market or Limit? A Market Order prioritizes immediate execution within its protections. A Limit Order lets you control the worst execution price, but it may remain open until the market reaches that price.   Example: Buy BTC with a Limit Order  You hold    USDT in Unified Trading and want    BTC. Open the       BTC/USDT   market.    USDT is the Quote Asset you spend, and    BTC is the Base Asset you want to receive. Select Buy, choose a Limit Order, enter the amount of    BTC, and set a Limit Price. Review the Order and place it. When it fills, the spent    USDT decreases and the received    BTC appears in the same Unified Trading Account. A filled Limit Buy shows Fill Progress at 100%, with no remaining quantity. Open the order to see the Limit Price, filled value, and the trades that completed it. If a Limit Order remains open, the unfilled quantity stays reserved. Cancel the remaining Order if you want to release that balance back to Unified Trading.   Order Form  Learn more about the order form. 4 Check the Asset you received After the Order fills, open your Unified Trading balance and confirm that the Asset you received is available. Open Orders shows any quantity still waiting to trade. Order History and Fills show what executed, including the quantity and price.         An accepted Order is not always a completed trade. If a Limit Order is still open or partially filled, some of its balance remains reserved until it fills or you cancel it. The received Asset can support another eligible Order or be transferred back to Funding when it is available and not reserved.   Manage Orders  Learn more about managing orders. Once the received Asset appears in your Unified Trading balance, you can use it in another eligible Order or transfer it to Funding for a supported withdrawal.   Withdraw Funds  Learn more about withdrawing funds. FAQ   Does every Deposit have to go through Funding first?  No. Deposit Routing can credit a completed Deposit to Funding or Unified Trading by default. The setting belongs to the active Master Account or Subaccount. If the balance is already available in Trading, skip the internal transfer.   Why is my Deposit not available immediately?  The source-chain transaction must meet the route 's confirmation requirement before Polyester can credit the balance. Its progress and estimated arrival time appear in the deposit record after the transaction is detected.   Should my first trade use a Market or Limit Order?  Choose based on the result you want. A Market Order prioritizes immediate execution within its configured protections, but it can fill at more than one price. A Limit Order controls the worst execution price, but it may remain partially filled or open.   Does an Order confirmation mean the trade is complete?  It means Polyester accepted the Order. Open Orders, Order History, and Fills show whether it is waiting, partially filled, completed, or cancelled.   Where does the Asset received from a trade appear?  The received Asset appears in the same Unified Trading Account. It can support another eligible Order or be returned to Funding when the balance is available and not reserved. Related Topics  What is Polyester?  How Polyester unifies Assets from supported chains for trading, lending, bridging, and swaps. Key Concepts  Learn how Polyester moves Assets across chains, keeps balances on-chain, and processes order-book trades. Create Your Account  Choose how to sign in, create your non-custodial Master Account, and protect the wallet that controls it. Secure Your Account  Protect your owner credential, add MFA, save recovery codes, and configure withdrawal and transfer whitelists. It is an accounting identity, not an ERC-20 in your external wallet. You trade, transfer, and withdraw against that one balance. Why Unified Assets exist The problem Decentralized finance (DeFi) has had this problem for years. The same Asset is split across blockchains, exchanges, and lending markets that can't share liquidity. Without unification, Ethereum USDT and Solana USDT sit as separate piles. You decide which pile to trade from and which pile to withdraw from. The solution Polyester maps compatible deposit routes  to one Unified Asset. Funding shows one balance. Behind it, Zipper  keeps a separate Zipped Asset  for each Network so each route keeps its own backing and withdrawal path. Unification is configured per route. Matching tickers alone do not merge balances. See Supported Assets for the mapped routes.  Example: three USDT deposits become 150 Unified USDT   You deposit 50    USDT from    Ethereum , 50 from    Solana , and 50 from    Base . Polyester credits your account with one Unified Asset: 150    USDT. Behind that credit, Zipper holds a separate Zipped USDT for each Network. What that means in practice: You can trade 150    USDT for    BTC You can transfer 150    USDT to another Polyester account You can withdraw 150 as Ethereum    USDT You do not pick which Network you deposited from in Funding cbBTC on    Base  and native    BTC from the    Bitcoin Network  stay separate Unified Assets. Polyester only merges routes it maps as equivalent. Unified Asset Flow Deposits from each source Network are zipped into Network-specific backing, then unified into one balance. That single Unified Asset is what you trade across all markets.   Overview Example    How chain-specific deposits become Unified Assets How a deposit becomes a Unified Asset You send the External Asset once. Zipper runs the Deposit Flow . Polyester credits the Unified Asset when the Flow completes. You do not wrap or hold the Zipped Asset yourself.   Deposit Funds  Learn more about depositing funds. Where you use the Unified Asset The same Unified Asset can sit in Funding or Unified Trading. Location What you use it for Funding Account  Transfers and withdrawals; Zipped Asset backing stays hereUnified Trading Account  Orders, Fills, fees, Lending, and eligible collateral    Default Deposit Destination chooses where new credits appear first. Open Settings > Security to set Funding or Unified Trading. Moving between Funding and Trading does not create another Zipped Asset. It only changes which account area can use the balance. What you can do next Once credited, you can: Trade after the balance is in Unified Trading Transfer to another eligible Polyester account Withdraw to an external wallet on a supported destination Network You can withdraw on a different Network than you deposited from when Polyester supports an equivalent destination route for that Unified Asset. Route availability, inventory, fee, and minimums still apply.   Funding and Trading balances are Unified Assets. Flow and Scan records that show a Zipped Asset are showing the Network-specific backing behind that credit. FAQ   Do I need to wrap or zip before I deposit?  No. Send the supported External Asset with the current Deposit instructions. Zipper creates the Zipped Asset and Polyester credits the Unified Asset during the Deposit Flow.   Why do I see one USDT balance after depositing from two Networks?  Polyester mapped those deposit routes to the same Unified Asset. The Zipped Asset supplies and withdrawal routes remain separate even though Funding shows one balance.   Can I withdraw on a different Network than I deposited from?  Yes, when Polyester supports an equivalent destination route for the same Unified Asset and the receiving wallet supports that Asset and Network. Related Topics  Supported Assets  Deposit and withdraw Unified Assets on supported networks. Expand a row for fees, minimums, and confirmation time. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. Deposit Funds  Deposit a supported Asset from an external Network and confirm where Polyester credits it. Withdraw Funds  Withdraw an available Polyester balance to an external wallet on a supported chain. Internal Transfers  Move an available balance between Polyester accounts or balance areas. Field Meaning Source address The asset contract on the external chain, or Native when no contract is required.Zipped Asset  address The Polyester Chain  contract for that asset-and-chain route.Network fee The fee currently listed for the route.Deposit minimum and withdrawal minimum The smallest listed amount for each action.Confirmations required The minimum number of block confirmations listed for the route.Average deposit time An estimate based on the route's confirmation requirement.    Assets with the same symbol are combined only when Polyester maps them to the same Unified Asset. Timing is an estimate and can vary with chain conditions. Related Topics  Unified Assets  Learn how Polyester turns chain-specific deposits into one account balance you can trade, transfer, or withdraw. Funding Account  Learn how the Funding Account keeps on-chain balances ready to deposit, transfer, trade, or withdraw. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. Deposit Funds  Deposit a supported Asset from an external Network and confirm where Polyester credits it. Withdraw Funds  Withdraw an available Polyester balance to an external wallet on a supported chain. Internal Transfers  Move an available balance between Polyester accounts or balance areas. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Funds /Funding Account   Funding Account  07/27    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    The Funding Account  is where you manage Assets before they enter Trading and after they leave it. It receives deposits, holds available balances, and supports transfers and withdrawals on Polyester Chain . Each Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own Funding Account. Switching the active account changes the balances and activity you see, so check the selected account first if an expected Asset appears to be missing.       What the Funding Account does Funding keeps the movement of Assets simple while preserving the on-chain records underneath each balance. Holds balances on-chain. Funding Account balances and their activity are recorded on Polyester Chain. Combines Zipped Assets  into Unified Assets . Compatible Zipped Assets contribute to one Unified Asset balance, even when they entered through different source chains. Keeps accounts separate. Every Master Account and Subaccount has its own balances, history, and security controls. Keeps Assets outside Lending risk. Assets in Funding do not count as collateral and are not exposed to liquidation. After you transfer an eligible Asset to Trading and use it as collateral, it can support borrowing and may be liquidated if the account no longer meets its margin requirements. How Assets reach Funding When you make a deposit, Polyester handles the cross-chain steps as part of one connected flow:  1 Deposit an Asset Send the Asset using the address, network, and memo or destination tag shown by Polyester.   Deposit Funds  Learn more about depositing funds. 2 Zipper verifies the deposit After the required source-chain confirmations, Zipper  creates the matching source-chain-specific Zipped Asset on Polyester Chain. 3 Zipper sends the Asset to Funding Zipper automatically sends the Zipped Asset to Funding, where it remains as on-chain backing and Polyester credits the matching Unified Asset balance. 4 Choose what happens next Keep the balance in Funding, transfer it, move it to Trading, or withdraw it through an available destination route . Polyester automatically handles zipping and unzipping as part of deposits and withdrawals. You choose the Asset, chain, amount, and destination when required; there is no separate wrapping step to manage.   You never need to hold or manage a Zipped Asset in MetaMask, Phantom, or another external wallet. Zipper sends it directly to the Funding Account controlled by your smart wallet, and Polyester credits the matching Unified Asset balance.   Example: Combine Ethereum and Solana USDT in Funding  Suppose your account receives 100    USDT through    Ethereum  and 50    USDT through    Solana . Zipper creates 100 Ethereum zUSDT and 50 Solana zUSDT. Funding will display them as one 150    USDT Unified Asset balance because Polyester explicitly maps both routes to the same Asset. The two Zipped Asset supplies remain separate. Each keeps its own source-chain backing and withdrawal route even though the Funding Account presents one balance for everyday use. By contrast, Coinbase BTC (cbBTC) on    Base  and native    BTC from the    Bitcoin Network  remain separate Assets and appear as separate balances. Polyester does not merge Assets simply because one is designed to track the value of another. Unification is based on Polyester's configured route mapping, not on a matching ticker. A native, wrapped, or externally bridged token only joins a Unified Asset when Polyester explicitly recognizes that route as an equivalent Asset. Read your balance       The Assets table shows the Unified Asset balances held in the selected Funding Account. Use Balance to see how much of each Unified Asset is available, and use Equity and Allocation to understand its estimated value within the account. Field What it tells you Total Equity The estimated current value of all Funding balances in the selected account, calculated from their Index Prices .Balance History How that estimated value changed during the selected period. Index Price changes can move the chart without moving an Asset.Balance The quantity of the Unified Asset held in Funding.Equity The estimated current value of that Asset balance, calculated from its Index Price.Allocation The Asset's share of the total displayed Funding equity.Actions The deposit, withdrawal, or transfer actions currently available for that Asset.      Balance and Equity answer different questions. Balance tells you how much of an Asset the account holds. Equity estimates what that balance is worth using the Asset's Index Price. The Index Price normalizes prices from leading centralized and decentralized exchanges, then weights them by trading volume to produce one reference price. Equity can therefore change with the broader market even when the Asset quantity stays the same. Move Assets from Funding An available Funding balance can move in four ways: Deposit an Asset. Bring a supported Asset into the selected account from an external chain. Transfer to another Polyester account. Send an available balance to another eligible account without creating a new Zipped Asset or changing its external backing. Transfer to Trading. Make a balance available for spot Orders and eligible Lending activity. Withdraw an Asset. Send a balance to an available Asset route and destination chain. Deposits and withdrawals cross between Polyester and an external chain through Zipper. Transfers between Funding, Trading, and other Polyester accounts stay inside Polyester. Transfer between Funding and Trading Use Transfer to make an available Funding balance usable for trading, Lending, borrowing, or margin. Reverse the direction when an unused Trading balance should return to Funding.  1 Open Transfer Keep Between My Accounts selected and review any values already shown in the form.       2 Choose the source and destination Select Funding as the source and Unified Trading as the destination to move an Asset into Trading. Reverse them to return an available Trading balance to Funding. Use the same Master Account or Subaccount on both sides. 3 Choose the Asset and amount Select an Asset held by the source account and enter an amount within its Available Balance. 4 Review and transfer Confirm the account, direction, Asset, and amount, then select Transfer once. Wait for Transfer History and both balances to show the result before using the balance or trying again.  Learn the difference between funding and trading.   Funding and Trading can show the same Unified Asset, but they serve different purposes. Funding is the on-chain balance area for deposits, transfers, and withdrawals. Trading is the private, low-latency balance area used by Orders, reservations, Fills, fees, and Lending. Compare Funding Account Trading Account Purpose Deposits, withdrawals, and transfers Trading, Lending, borrowing, and marginRecorded on Polyester Chain PolyEngine  LedgerPublicly seen Yes NoLending Not supported Supported for eligible Assets    Moving an Asset into Trading does not bridge it, change its owner, create another Zipped Asset, or move the underlying Zipped Asset out of Funding. It changes which part of the same Polyester account can use the corresponding Unified Asset balance. Funding-to-Trading transfers settle as one Polyester Chain transaction and normally appear in Trading almost immediately. Once the transfer completes, the updated Trading balance is ready to use. Funding and Lending Assets held in Funding are outside the Lending risk engine. They do not count as collateral, increase borrowing power, affect account health, or become available for liquidation. To use an eligible Asset as Lending collateral, transfer it to the Unified Trading Account . Until then, the balance remains available in Funding for transfers and withdrawals. Secure Your Funding Account Security controls apply to the active Master Account or Subaccount. MFA  can confirm protected actions, while on-chain whitelists can limit where Assets are allowed to move. The external withdrawal whitelist restricts withdrawals to approved external addresses when enabled. The internal transfer whitelist restricts transfers to approved Polyester accounts when enabled. MFA confirms the person approving a protected action. It does not replace either whitelist. Use Address Book & Whitelists to manage approved destinations. Read Secure Your Account for an overview of MFA, the Guard Signer, and your owner credential. FAQ   Does every deposit appear in Funding first?  Every deposit creates a Zipped Asset that remains in Funding as on-chain backing. Settings > Security lets the active account use Deposit Routing to choose whether the matching Unified Asset balance is first credited to Funding or Unified Trading.   Why do deposits from different chains appear as one balance?  Polyester explicitly maps their routes to the same Unified Asset. For example, Ethereum zUSDT and Solana zUSDT can contribute to one USDT Funding balance while their supplies and source-chain backing remain separate. A matching ticker by itself is not enough.   Can an open Order use my Funding balance?  No. Orders use the Unified Trading Account. Transfer the amount you want to trade from Funding to Trading first, unless Deposit Routing already credited that Unified Asset balance directly to Trading.   Does my Funding balance count as Lending collateral?  No. Assets in Funding do not increase borrowing power, enter the collateral balance, affect Lending health, or become available for liquidation. Transfer an eligible Asset to Unified Trading before using it as collateral.   Can I withdraw to a different chain than the one I deposited from?  Yes, when an equivalent destination route is supported and has sufficient inventory. Availability also depends on current policy, minimums, fees, account permissions, and security requirements.   Why did Total Equity change when my Balance did not?  Equity uses the Asset's Index Price. When that reference price changes, Equity, Total Equity, Allocation, and Balance History can change while the Asset quantity stays the same.   Is the Funding Account the same as my smart wallet?  No. Your smart wallet is the on-chain account controlled by your owner wallet . Funding is the application contract and balance layer that the smart wallet controls for Zipped Assets, Unified Asset balances, and protected Asset movements. Related Topics  Unified Assets  Learn how Polyester turns chain-specific deposits into one account balance you can trade, transfer, or withdraw. Supported Assets  Deposit and withdraw Unified Assets on supported networks. Expand a row for fees, minimums, and confirmation time. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. Deposit Funds  Deposit a supported Asset from an external Network and confirm where Polyester credits it. Withdraw Funds  Withdraw an available Polyester balance to an external wallet on a supported chain. Internal Transfers  Move an available balance between Polyester accounts or balance areas. It maintains private, low-latency Unified Asset  balances for Orders, Fills, collateral, borrowing, margin, and transfers. Each Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own Trading Account, balances, Orders, and activity. Switching the active account changes what you see and what you can use, so check the selected account first if an expected balance or Order appears to be missing.       What the Trading Account does Trading keeps the balances used by PolyEngine  separate from the on-chain balances held in Funding. Makes Assets available for trading. Available balances can support new spot Orders on Polyester's order books. Keeps Trading activity private. Your balances, Orders, Fills, and strategies are visible only to your account. Separates available and reserved amounts. Trading shows what the account holds, what is free to use, and what is already committed. Supports Lending and margin. Eligible Assets can contribute collateral value, support borrowing, or be supplied through Lending. Keeps accounts separate. Every Master Account and Subaccount has its own Trading balances and activity. How Trading balances work Three quantities describe each Unified Asset balance: Total Balance is the complete amount of the Asset held in Trading. Available Balance is the amount free for a new Order, Lending action, transfer, or withdrawal. Reserved Balance is the amount already committed to an active Order, loan, withdrawal, transfer, or another pending action. Polyester updates Available and Reserved Balance automatically as activity begins and ends. When an action commits an amount, that amount becomes Reserved. Any unused amount returns to Available when the action fills, is canceled, completes, or reaches another final state.   Only Available Balance can support a new Order, Lending action, transfer, or withdrawal. Reserved Balance is still part of Total Balance, but it cannot be used again until the existing commitment releases it.  Example: Reserve BTC in an open Order   Suppose your Trading Account holds a Total Balance of 1    BTC. You place a sell Order for 0.4    BTC on the       BTC/USDT   order book. While the Order is open, the 0.4    BTC committed to it appears as Reserved Balance. The remaining 0.6    BTC stays Available for another eligible action. If you cancel the unfilled Order, the reserved amount returns to Available Balance. If the Order fills, Polyester settles the sold    BTC and credits the    USDT received from the trade. Read your balance       The Assets table shows the private Unified Asset balances held in the selected Trading Account. Total Balance shows the full amount held in Trading, while Available Balance shows what the account can use for a new action right now. Open a Total Balance to see its Reserved Balance, or choose an available action when you are ready to trade or transfer the Asset. Field What it tells you Total Equity The estimated current value of all Trading balances in the selected account, calculated from their Index Prices .Balance History How that estimated value changed during the selected period. Index Price changes can move the chart without an Order or transfer.Allocation The Asset's share of the total displayed Trading equity.Total Balance The complete amount of the Asset held in Trading.Available Balance The amount free for a new Order, Lending action, transfer, or withdrawal.Reserved Balance The amount already committed to an active or pending action.Equity The estimated current value of the Asset's Total Balance, calculated from its Index Price.Actions The Trade or Transfer actions currently available for the Asset.      Total, Available, and Equity answer different questions. Total tells you how much of an Asset Trading holds. Available tells you how much is free to use. Equity estimates the Total Balance's value using the Asset's Index Price, a volume-weighted reference built from normalized prices across leading centralized and decentralized exchanges. Use Assets in Trading An available Trading balance can support several actions: Place a spot Order. Buy or sell an Asset through an available Pair and its order book. Transfer to another Polyester account. Send an available balance to another eligible account. Lend or borrow. Supply an available Asset or use eligible collateral to borrow another Asset. Withdraw an Asset. Send an available balance to an external address through an available destination route . Only Available Balance can begin a new action. If part of the balance is Reserved, the existing Order or pending activity must release it before it can be used again. Trading and Lending Eligible Assets in Trading can contribute to account collateral and borrowing power. Polyester's risk engine can continue to recognize eligible collateral committed to open Orders, allowing the same capital to support trading and borrowing when account requirements are met. Borrowing introduces liquidation risk. If the account no longer meets its margin requirements, eligible collateral in Trading may be sold to repay its obligations.   Holding an Asset in Trading does not create debt by itself. Liquidation risk begins when collateral supports borrowing or another margin obligation. Transfer between Funding and Trading Use Transfer when an available Funding balance should support trading, Lending, borrowing, or margin, or when an unused Trading balance should return to Funding.  1 Open Transfer Keep Between My Accounts selected and review any values already shown in the form.       2 Choose the source and destination Select Funding as the source and Unified Trading as the destination to move an Asset into Trading. Reverse them to return an available Trading balance to Funding. Use the same Master Account or Subaccount on both sides. 3 Choose the Asset and amount Select an Asset held by the source account and enter an amount within its Available Balance. 4 Review and transfer Confirm the account, direction, Asset, and amount, then select Transfer once. Wait for Transfer History and both balances to show the result before using the balance or trying again. Use Withdraw when the destination is an external chain. A withdrawal from Trading reserves the amount, moves it through Funding and Zipper , and remains subject to the route's inventory, fees, minimums, policies, permissions, and security controls.  Learn the difference between funding and trading.   Funding and Trading can show the same Unified Asset, but they serve different purposes. Funding is the on-chain balance area for deposits, transfers, and withdrawals. Trading is the private, low-latency balance area used by Orders, reservations, Fills, fees, and Lending. Compare Funding Account  Trading Account Purpose Deposits, withdrawals, and transfers Trading, Lending, borrowing, and marginRecorded on Polyester Chain  PolyEngine LedgerPublicly seen Yes NoLending Not supported Supported for eligible Assets    Moving an Asset into Trading does not bridge it, change its owner, create another Zipped Asset , or move the underlying Zipped Asset out of Funding. It changes which part of the same Polyester account can use the corresponding Unified Asset balance. Funding-to-Trading transfers settle as one Polyester Chain transaction and normally appear in Trading almost immediately. Once the transfer completes, the updated Trading balance is ready to use. FAQ   Why is Available Balance lower than Total Balance?  Part of the balance is reserved for activity already in progress. Working or partially filled Orders, pending withdrawals or transfers, and an Order's fee budget can reduce Available Balance while leaving Total Balance unchanged.   Can I trade directly from my Funding Account?  No. Orders use the Unified Trading Account. Transfer the amount from Funding to Trading first, unless Deposit Routing already credited the Unified Asset balance directly to Trading.   Can I move Reserved Balance back to Funding?  No. You can only transfer the amount shown as Available Balance. A reserved amount becomes available again when the Order or pending action releases it.   When does an Order reservation return to Available Balance?  Polyester releases the unused amount when the Order reaches a final state. A cancellation can race with a Fill, so check the final Order and its Fills before reusing the balance.   Can I withdraw from Trading?  Yes, when the withdrawal flow  offers an available route for the Asset. Polyester reserves the amount in Trading, moves it through Funding and Zipper, and applies the route's current fees, minimums, policies, permissions, and security controls.   Are Trading balances shared between accounts?  No. Each Master Account and Subaccount has its own Unified Trading Account, balances, Orders, and Fills. Check the active account before trading or transferring Assets. Deposit Funds  Deposit a supported Asset from an external Network and confirm where Polyester credits it. Withdraw Funds  Withdraw an available Polyester balance to an external wallet on a supported chain. Internal Transfers  Move an available balance between Polyester accounts or balance areas.
