Choose the receiving account, Asset, and Network, then follow the current route  instructions shown by Polyester. Zipper  handles the Deposit Flow  automatically. You send the external Asset once, and Polyester tracks the transfer until the matching Unified Asset  balance is ready in Funding or Unified Trading. Make a deposit Open Deposit from the Main Account or Subaccount  that should receive the balance. Switching the active account changes the deposit details and history you see. A new deposit address may take a few seconds to appear while Polyester prepares it for that account and Network.  1 Choose the receiving account Select the Main Account or Subaccount that should own the deposited balance, then open Deposit.       2 Choose the Asset and Network Select the Asset you want to deposit and the Network from which you will send it. Polyester will show the route currently available for that combination.     Selecting USDT as the token and Ethereum as the network  3 Review and send Review the address, Asset contract, minimum, confirmations, estimated time, and any fee shown. Include the memo or destination tag when the route requires one. Copy the complete address or scan its QR code, then approve the transfer in the sending wallet.     Using MetaMask to send 121.24 USDT to the deposit address  4 Watch the in-progress deposit After you send, Polyester shows an indication in the top bar and a toast. Open either one to follow Deposit Seen while it observes the transfer and source-chain confirmations. If you miss both, open Account/Deposit to see the deposit.     Watching an in-progress USDT deposit after it is seen on chain  5 Confirm the credited balance When Credit Balance completes, check the credited amount and the account where the Unified Asset became available.  Interactive      USDT Deposited via Ethereum   Completed        121.24 USDT  Started 20s ago   Overall progress: 100% Completed just now   Steps   Deposit Seen Deposit Seen 0xc3e9…049e     Verified Deposit Verified Deposit 0x72d7…ef7e    Validated Deposit Validated Deposit 0xa827…dcaf     Minted and Transferred Minted and Transferred 0xc882…321f    Credited Balance Credited Balance 115699…5723     View on Polyester Scan    Confirming 121.24 USDT credited after the deposit completes   Open Deposit before every transfer and use the instructions shown for the selected account, Asset, and Network. A saved address or an older screenshot may no longer match the route you intend to use. What happens after you send The source transaction begins the Deposit Flow. Polyester then moves it through five stages:  Interactive            1  Deposit Seen 4m ago       2  Verified Deposit 3m ago       3  Validated Deposit 2m ago       4  Minted and Transferred 2m ago       5  Credited Balance 45s ago   Viewing a completed 121.24 USDT Deposit Flow on Polyester Scan  1 Deposit Seen Polyester detects the source transfer and starts the Deposit Flow. The deposit record then tracks confirmations against the live Network requirement for that route. 2 Verified Deposit Zipper checks that the source transaction matches the selected Asset, Network, amount, and receiving account. It then opens a deposit request for that transfer. 3 Validated Deposit Independent Zipper validators review the same evidence and the current route policy. The flow continues only after they approve the request. 4 Minted and Transferred Zipper mints the route-specific Zipped Asset  on Polyester Chain . It sends that Asset to Funding as on-chain backing. 5 Credited Balance Polyester credits the matching Unified Asset to the selected account. The balance appears in Funding or Unified Trading based on Default Deposit Destination. You can see more details on Polyester Scan .     Viewing a completed 121.24 USDT Deposit Flow on Polyester Scan  You never need to wrap the Asset yourself or hold the Zipped Asset in an external wallet. The Deposit Flow handles those steps between the source Network and your Polyester account. Confirmation requirements can change with the Network, transfer amount, and current conditions. Follow the live requirement in the deposit record instead of relying on a previous transfer. Track each deposit Every transfer has its own deposit record, even when several deposits use the same active address. Follow each record until it reaches a completed state rather than treating one completed credit as confirmation that every transfer arrived. Open Account/Deposit to view the deposits data table.     In view (Account/Deposit) data table  After completion, compare the credited amount with the deposit record and check its destination. If the balance appears in Unified Trading, you do not need to transfer it there again. Choose where new deposits go Default Deposit Destination controls where the Unified Asset becomes available after a Deposit Flow completes. The setting applies separately to each Main Account and Subaccount. Funding Account . Keep new balances ready for transfers and withdrawals, or move them to Trading later. Unified Trading Account . Make new balances available for spot trading, Lending, borrowing, and eligible collateral use. Open Settings/Security for the active account. Under Fund Movement, set Default Deposit Destination to Funding or Unified Trading. This is an authorized on-chain account setting, not a browser preference.  Interactive    Fund Movement Control deposit routing and restrict where withdrawals and transfers can go.   Default Deposit Destination Automatically credit to your selected account when you deposit   Funding  Unified Trading   Selecting Funding as the Default Deposit Destination The setting changes where the Unified Asset is credited. It does not change the external Asset, source Network, Zipped Asset backing, or Polyester account that owns the balance. If automatic routing to Unified Trading fails, Polyester leaves the completed credit in Funding. Check the deposit record and both balance areas before submitting a separate transfer. Fees and timing A deposit can involve two separate costs: Network transaction cost. The sending wallet pays the cost of broadcasting the transfer on the source Network. Polyester route fee. The Deposit page shows any fee that applies to the selected route and the expected credited amount. The estimated completion time is guidance, not a guarantee. Actual timing depends on the source Network, confirmation requirement, route health, Zipper verification, and Polyester processing. FAQ   Does every deposit appear in Funding first?  The route-specific Zipped Asset remains in Funding as on-chain backing. Default Deposit Destination determines whether the matching Unified Asset balance becomes available in Funding or Unified Trading.   Can I reuse a deposit address I saved earlier?  Open Deposit for the same account, Asset, and Network before sending. Compare the complete current address and include any memo or destination tag shown. Polyester may return the same address, but you should not assume a saved value is still the active route.   Do I need to wrap or zip the Asset first?  No. Send the supported external Asset using the current Deposit instructions. Zipper creates the route-specific Zipped Asset and Polyester credits the matching Unified Asset during the Deposit Flow.   Why can the credited amount be lower than the amount sent?  Check the deposit record for any Polyester route fee applied to the gross deposit. The source Network transaction cost is separate and is paid by the sending wallet.   How long does a deposit take?  Use the live estimated time and confirmation progress for the selected route. The requirement can change with the Network, transfer amount, and current conditions, and Zipper verification continues after the source transaction confirms.   What should I do if the deposit details were wrong?  Do not send another transfer while the first is being investigated. Keep the source transaction ID, selected account, Asset, Network, deposit address, contract, memo or destination tag, and amount. Submit one support request with that evidence. Recovery is not guaranteed.   Can I withdraw through a different Network later?  Yes, when Polyester supports an equivalent destination route for the same Unified Asset. The withdrawal still depends on that route's availability, inventory, fee, minimum, policy, permissions, and security checks. Related Topics  Unified Assets  Learn how Polyester turns chain-specific deposits into one account balance you can trade, transfer, or withdraw. Supported Assets  Deposit and withdraw Unified Assets on supported networks. Expand a row for fees, minimums, and confirmation time. Funding Account  Learn how the Funding Account keeps on-chain balances ready to deposit, transfer, trade, or withdraw. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. Withdraw Funds  Withdraw an available Polyester balance to an external wallet on a supported chain. Internal Transfers  Move an available balance between Polyester accounts or balance areas. Zipper  handles the route , validation, and external delivery, so you do not need to unwrap assets or hold gas on Polyester. Zipper handles the Withdrawal Flow  automatically. You submit once, and Polyester tracks the request until the destination transaction reaches finality . If the recipient is another Polyester account, use the Transfer page instead. Make a withdrawal Open Withdraw from the Main Account or Subaccount  that holds the balance. Switching the active account changes the balances and history you see.  1 Choose the sending account Select the Main Account or Subaccount that holds the balance, then open Withdraw.       2 Choose the Asset and source Select the Asset and whether it comes from Funding or Unified Trading.     Selecting USDT as the token and Trading as the source  3 Enter the destination and amount Select the destination Network, paste the complete address or choose an Address Book entry , and enter the amount. Include the Destination Tag when the route requires one.     Selecting Ethereum Sepolia and entering 90 USDT  4 Review and confirm Review You will receive, the route fee, Fee source, and Balance after withdrawal. Then approve the request in the connected wallet.  Check the destination before submitting Compare the complete withdrawal address, Destination Tag, Asset, and Network before you submit. Once the external transfer is broadcast, it cannot be canceled or reversed.     Using the wallet to confirm the 90 USDT withdrawal  5 Watch the in-progress withdrawal Open the withdrawal record after you submit. Follow Requested Withdrawal while Polyester validates and submits the destination transfer.     Watching an in-progress 90 USDT withdrawal  6 Confirm the completed withdrawal When Withdrawal Settled completes, check the settled amount and the destination transaction.  Interactive      USDT Withdrawn via Ethereum   Completed        90 USDT  Started 1m ago   Overall progress: 100% Completed just now   Steps   Requested Withdrawal Requested Withdrawal 0xc2c1…eff9    Validated Withdrawal Validated Withdrawal 0xd9e9…8943     Processed Withdrawal Processed Withdrawal 0xa531…457c    Submitted to Source Chain Submitted to Source Chain 0x43ed…8950    Zipper Fulfillment Zipper Fulfillment 0x4428…20c0    Withdrawal Settled Withdrawal Settled 261437…6483     View on Polyester Scan    Confirming 90 USDT withdrawn via Ethereum Sepolia   Open Withdraw before every request and use the destination, Asset, and Network shown for the selected account. A saved address or an older screenshot may no longer match the route you intend to use. What happens after you submit Submitting the request begins the Withdrawal Flow. Polyester then moves it through six stages:  Interactive            1  Requested Withdrawal 5m ago       2  Validated Withdrawal 4m ago       3  Processed Withdrawal 3m ago       4  Submitted to Source Chain 2m ago       5  Zipper Fulfillment 2m ago       6  Withdrawal Settled 45s ago   Withdrawal Flow  1 Requested Withdrawal Polyester accepts the request and locks the withdrawal amount plus the applicable fee from the selected source. 2 Validated Withdrawal Independent Zipper validators review the route, amount, destination, and account policy. The flow continues only after they approve the request. 3 Processed Withdrawal Zipper executes the approved request on Polyester Chain . It prepares the route-specific Zipped Asset  for external delivery. 4 Submitted to Source Chain Zipper submits the external transfer toward the destination Network. The withdrawal record then links that destination transaction. 5 Zipper Fulfillment Zipper follows the destination transaction until the receiving wallet can observe it. The route-specific Zipped Asset is burned after successful delivery. 6 Withdrawal Settled Polyester completes the request after the destination transaction reaches finality. The wallet receives the settled amount after any route fee. You can see more details on Polyester Scan .     Viewing a completed 90 USDT Withdrawal Flow on Polyester Scan  You never need to unwrap the Asset yourself or hold the Zipped Asset in an external wallet. The Withdrawal Flow handles those steps between your Polyester account and the destination Network. Track each withdrawal Every request has its own withdrawal record. Follow that record from submission through external delivery rather than treating one completed withdrawal as confirmation that every request arrived. Open Account/Withdraw to view the withdrawals data table.     In view (Account/Withdraw) data table  Do not submit a second withdrawal while the original request is still pending or its result is unclear. Continue following the same Flow ID and destination transaction. After completion, compare the settled amount with the withdrawal record and the destination wallet. Withdraw from Funding or Unified Trading Choose the balance area that currently holds the amount you want to withdraw. Funding Account . Withdraw any available Funding balance supported by the selected destination route. Unified Trading Account . Withdraw the available balance that is not reserved by Orders or another pending action. A withdrawal from Unified Trading can use only the amount shown as available. Open orders and other pending actions can reserve part of the balance. Polyester moves an approved Trading withdrawal through Funding and Zipper automatically; you do not need to transfer it yourself first. Fees and amounts Each destination route has a current Polyester route fee denominated in the selected Asset. Fee source changes how that fee relates to the amount you enter; it does not select a different fee. Fee source The amount you enter What leaves your balance What the wallet receives Principal Total amount to withdraw The entered amount The entered amount minus the feeBalance Amount the wallet should receive The entered amount plus the fee The entered amount    Use You will receive and Balance after withdrawal to confirm the result before submitting. When Balance is selected, your available source balance must cover the entered amount plus the fee. The Withdraw page also shows the route minimum and any current Max value. Your available balance, route inventory, minimum, fee, and account controls determine the amount that can be withdrawn. Polyester does not apply a separate global daily or per-transaction monetary cap. Address Book and Withdrawal Whitelist An Address Book entry saves an external destination for easier reuse. It does not automatically approve that address for withdrawals. If the active account requires an External Withdrawal Whitelist, select a destination with an active whitelist record for that chain. Each Main Account and Subaccount has its own Address Book and withdrawal controls. For XRP, enter the classic address in Withdrawal address and the receiver's numeric tag in Destination Tag. Polyester cannot determine that a recipient expected a tag when one is omitted. FAQ   Can I withdraw directly from Unified Trading?  Yes. Choose Unified Trading as the source when the Asset and destination route are available. Only the amount shown as available can leave; balances reserved by orders or pending actions cannot be withdrawn.   Can I withdraw on a different chain than I deposited from?  Yes. Choose another enabled destination route when it represents the same Unified Asset  and the receiving wallet supports that Asset and Network.   Why is a destination chain unavailable?  Each route needs enough inventory and must pass its current health, minimum, fee, destination, policy, and security checks. Another route for the same Unified Asset may still be available.   Is a saved Address Book entry automatically approved?  No. Saving an address and approving it for withdrawals are separate. When the active account requires an External Withdrawal Whitelist, the destination must also have an active whitelist record for the selected chain.   Can I cancel a withdrawal after submitting it?  No. Review the final destination and amount carefully before submitting. Once the external transaction is broadcast, it cannot be canceled or reversed.   What happens if a withdrawal fails before delivery?  The final withdrawal record shows the outcome. Eligible principal can return when delivery did not become irreversible, although the settled route fee may not be refunded. A withdrawal sourced from Unified Trading returns eligible principal to the same Trading Account. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. You can move assets between Funding and Unified Trading, between your Master Account  and Subaccounts , or to another Polyester user. Because both sides are Polyester accounts, an internal transfer does not use an external chain, deposit address, or Zipper  route  fee. Open the Transfer page to get started. Make an internal transfer Open Transfer from the account that holds the balance. Choose a tab, then set the source, destination, Asset, and amount.       Between My Accounts To Another Polyester User  Use this when both sides belong to you.  1 Choose From Select the sending account and Funding or Unified Trading. The form shows the available balance for that source.     Transferring 541.64 USDT from Main Funding to Futures Funding  2 Choose To Select your Master Account or a Subaccount as the destination. Then choose Funding or Unified Trading for that account. From and To each have their own account and balance area. Use the swap control if you want to reverse the direction. 3 Choose the Asset and amount Select the Asset, then enter the amount, use Max, or move the percentage slider. Stay within the available balance shown under the slider. 4 Review and confirm Compare From, To, Asset, and amount. Then approve the request in the connected wallet.     Using the wallet to confirm the internal transfer  5 Confirm the completed transfer When Ledger Settlement Confirmed completes, check the transferred amount and both balances.  Interactive      USDT Transfer    Completed        541.640622 USDT Started 15s ago  From Funding 0x4cce…b657  To Funding 0x8115…378a Overall progress: 100% Completed just now   Steps   Transfer Observed Transfer Observed 0x8ac4…5a6a    Ledger Settlement Confirmed Ledger Settlement Confirmed 179594…5363     View on Polyester Scan    Confirming 541.64 USDT transferred from Funding to Unified TradingUse this when the receiving Master Account or Subaccount belongs to someone else.  1 Choose From Select the sending account and Funding or Unified Trading. The form shows the available balance for that source.     Transferring 330.27 USDT to another Polyester user's Trading balance  2 Find the recipient Search by username, account ID, or smart-account address. Compare the resolved label, account type, and complete address with information from the recipient. 3 Choose Destination Account Set the recipient's destination to Funding or Trading. This chooses where their Unified Asset  becomes available. 4 Choose the Asset and amount Select the Asset, then enter the amount, use Max, or move the percentage slider. Stay within the available balance shown under the slider. 5 Review and confirm Compare From, To, Destination Account, Asset, and amount. Then approve the request in the connected wallet.  Confirm another user's account before submitting When transferring to another Polyester user, compare the resolved account label, account type, and complete smart-account address with information from the recipient. A completed transfer cannot be canceled or reversed by Polyester.     Using the wallet to confirm the internal transfer  6 Confirm the completed transfer When Ledger Settlement Confirmed completes, check the transferred amount and both balances.  Interactive      USDT Transfer    Completed        541.640622 USDT Started 15s ago  From Funding 0x4cce…b657  To Funding 0x8115…378a Overall progress: 100% Completed just now   Steps   Transfer Observed Transfer Observed 0x8ac4…5a6a    Ledger Settlement Confirmed Ledger Settlement Confirmed 179594…5363     View on Polyester Scan    Confirming 541.64 USDT transferred from Funding to Unified Trading What happens after you submit Submitting the request begins the Transfer Flow. Polyester then moves it through two stages:  Interactive            1  Transfer Observed 2m ago       2  Ledger Settlement Confirmed 45s ago   Transfer Flow  1 Transfer Observed Polyester records the internal movement between the selected accounts and balance areas. 2 Ledger Settlement Confirmed The Unified Asset leaves the source Available Balance and appears at the destination. There is no Zipper route fee. You can see more details on Polyester Scan .     Viewing a completed 541.64 USDT Transfer Flow on Polyester Scan  Funding and Unified Trading transfer routes Every side of an internal transfer identifies both a Polyester account and a balance area. Moving between Funding and Unified Trading changes where the balance can be used. Moving between a Master Account and Subaccount changes which account owns it. FromTo Result FundingFunding Moves an available Funding balance to the destination account's Funding balanceFundingUnified Trading Makes an available Funding balance available in the destination account's Trading balanceUnified TradingFunding Moves an available, unreserved Trading balance to the destination account's Funding balanceUnified TradingUnified Trading Moves an available Trading balance to the destination account's Trading balance    Funding transfers use the available Funding balance. Unified Trading transfers use Available Balance, so open orders and other pending actions can reduce the amount you can move. Track the transfer Transfer submitted means Polyester accepted the request. Transfer History is the primary record and shows the time, amount, asset, source, destination, Flow ID, and current status.     Viewing Transfer History after a 541.64 USDT internal transfer  Follow the same history record until it reaches a final state and both balances reflect the movement. Do not submit a second transfer while the first result is still unclear. Some internal transfers include public Polyester Chain  evidence, while others are private balance movements. A missing public Scan record does not mean the internal transfer did not occur; use Transfer History as the account record. Internal Address Book and Transfer Whitelist An Address Book entry saves another Polyester account so it is easier to find again. Saving a recipient does not automatically authorize transfers to that account. If the source account requires the Internal Transfer Whitelist, the recipient must also have an active whitelist record for that source. Each Master Account and Subaccount has its own saved entries and transfer controls. FAQ   Does the recipient need to accept an internal transfer?  No. An active recipient account receives an authorized internal transfer directly. Confirm the receiving account and balance area with the recipient before submitting.   Can I transfer to a disabled Subaccount?  No. A disabled Subaccount rejects new inbound activity until it is active again.   What can the recipient see about the sender?  The recipient's Ledger can show the sending Polyester Account ID or Subaccount ID and its public smart-account address. It does not reveal a private username or user-created account label. Unified Assets  from supported chains become available in one Trading Account, where you can trade through an interactive workspace or connect programmatically. Every Pair has its own dedicated spot order book. Polyester uses its own internal liquidity and never sources liquidity from another exchange or bridge. Order-book trading with Unified Assets Polyester uses dedicated order books rather than AMMs or liquidity pools. Orders match at the best available price; when several orders share the same price, the order submitted first is first in line. Supported forms of the same economic asset become one Unified Asset before they reach Trading. This allows liquidity from supported chains to meet in the same market instead of splitting into separate order books based on where the asset originated.  Order Book  Read prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one market. Private balances and trading activity Your Unified Trading Account  is private by default. Your individual Trading balances, open orders, fills, and trading history are visible only within the authorized Master Account  or Subaccount . Movements into and out of Trading can be visible on-chain because they cross the boundary between your public Funding Account  and private Trading balance. Once assets are inside Trading, your individual balance and trading activity are not published on-chain. Polyester still publishes the market information needed for an order-book exchange, including prices, aggregated liquidity, charts, and completed Market Trades. This public market data does not identify the account behind an order or fill.  Trading Account  Private balances, available vs reserved, and what Trading can use. An interactive trading workspace The Trading Screen brings market analysis, order entry, account activity, and balances into one customizable workspace. You can arrange and group the widgets that matter to your trading style without changing the underlying order or balance state. The workspace includes Polyester and TradingView charts, a Depth Chart, Order Book, Market Trades, Order Form, Open Orders, Order History, Triggers, and Funds. Public market information and your private account activity stay visible in their proper contexts while you trade.  Trading Screen  Arrange charts, order entry, and account activity in one workspace. Order types for different trading styles Polyester supports nine order types across immediate execution, price control, triggered protection, and algorithmic execution. Core orders: trade now or set your price. Use Market, Limit, and post-only  controls to prioritize execution, price, or adding liquidity. Triggered orders: react to market movement. Use Stop-Loss Market, Stop-Loss Limit, and Trailing Stop orders to act when a price condition is reached. Execution strategies: control how an order reaches the market. Use TWAP, Ladder, and Iceberg orders to divide, distribute, or conceal displayed quantity. Each order type has its own purpose and lifecycle. The current Pair, account, and available balance determine whether an order can be placed and how much it can use. Engineered for low latency Polyester's Order Management System, or OMS, separates account-level checks from symbol-level order processing. This design keeps account admission, market sequencing, matching, and settlement focused on their own responsibilities while communicating over low-latency paths. Admit the Order. The Account Admission Shard checks the account, available balance, authorization, and required reservation. Sequence the instruction. The Symbol Order Shard maintains the ordered lifecycle state for the selected market. Match eligible Orders. Buy and sell Orders execute against Polyester's internal order book. Settle the result. Polyester finalizes Fills, fees, balance changes, and reservation releases. The Account Admission Shard (AAS) handles account-specific admission, spend checks, and reservations. The Symbol Order Shard (SOS) maintains ordered state for each market and forwards eligible instructions to the matching engine. This separation lets account and market workloads scale independently while keeping the execution path short. The architecture is designed for rapid order entry and high-throughput market activity, including latency-sensitive market-making, automated strategies, and high-frequency trading systems.   PolyEngine  How orders are admitted, matched, and settled. APIs for traders, market makers, and agents The same trading system is available through interfaces designed for different levels of performance and operational control. Interface Best suited to REST Direct HTTP integrations, scripts, readable payloads, and operational toolsWebSocket JSON Live updates for JSON-based applicationsConnectRPC and WebSocket Protobuf Typed, high-throughput trading applications and official SDK integrationsSBE WebSocket Ultra-low-latency binary order entry and immediate acknowledgementsFIX Classic and FIX-SBE Institutional connectivity, session recovery, and existing market-making infrastructure    Read APIs are designed for high-volume access with generous rate limits, while realtime streams deliver market, order, execution, balance, and account updates without repeated polling. Integrations can combine a fast order-entry interface with REST or ConnectRPC for state reconciliation. Polyester's non-custodial account model also makes it well suited to AI agents and autonomous trading systems. An agent can operate through scoped API credentials while the account owner retains control of the account and assets.  APIs  Start with Polyester APIs, SDKs, streams, and trading interfaces. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Trading /Trading Screen   Trading Screen  07/27    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    The Polyester Trading Screen brings live market data, order entry, private account activity, and balances into one customizable workspace. Choose your chart, personalize its appearance, and arrange every panel around the way you trade. Open the Trading Screen to choose a market and arrange the workspace around the information you use most.     Trading Screen USDT/BTC pair  Public market data and private account data The Trading Screen keeps public market information and private account activity together without combining their visibility. Screen area Visibility What it shows Charts, Depth Chart, Order Book, and Market Trades Public market data Price history, aggregated liquidity, and completed market-level tradesOpen Orders, Order History, Triggers, and Funds Private account data Your attributed orders, fills, balances, reservations, and history    The Order Form connects both contexts. It uses the selected Pair's market rules and the active account's available balance and permissions. Market Trades is not your personal trade history. It shows completed public executions without identifying the accounts behind them. Use Order History and fill details for activity attributed to your account. Personalize Personalize is one of the core features of Polyester. We keep adding layout, chart, and panel options, and more will come. Feel free to send feedback or a feature request. Pick a layout, choose a chart, and arrange the panels around the way you trade. Standard and Advanced layouts Use Trading Layout in the market header to switch between Standard and Advanced.     Choose Standard or Advanced from Trading Layout        Standard Advanced  Standard keeps chart, Order Book, Order Form, and orders in a fixed arrangement. You always know where each panel is. Resize panels and switch tabs without dragging widgets around.       Standard layout features Fixed arrangement: panels stay in place so you always know where each one is Resizable panels: drag a panel edge to change its width or height Prefilled tabs: Standard already groups these widgets so you switch tabs instead of dragging: Chart and Depth: switch Polyester Chart or TradingView with Depth Chart Order Book and Trades: switch Order Book and Trades in one panel. Order Book also has Tabbed, Stacked, and Side by side Limit and Market: use the Order Form tabs for Limit, Market, and More Open Orders, Triggers, and Order History: switch Open Orders, Triggers, and Order History Funds: stays on the same screen as the formAdvanced lets each widget become a panel you can drag, resize, float, or expand. Group widgets as tabs, then move a tab from one group to another when you want more control than Standard.       Advanced layout Features Draggable: drag a panel or tab to a new place Resizable: drag edges to change width and height Floating widgets: use Float panel to pull a group out of the grid Maximize View: expand a group to fill the workspace, then restore it Move one tab to another: drag a tab into a different group to combine or split panels Widgets: Colleciton of widgets that can be added to the screen   Overview  Learn each Trading Screen widget and how to add it in Advanced. Trading chart Choose Polyester Chart, the native chart built in-house, or TradingView Chart. Both display Polyester market data, so you can use the charting experience that best fits the way you analyze a market. Polyester Chart: use Polyester's native chart for candles, volume, indicators, and drawings TradingView Chart: use TradingView Advanced Charts with its indicators, drawing tools, and chart controls Customize the chart's theme and appearance, then keep the chart beside the market data and order controls you use with it. You can also place both charts in one tab group and switch between them without rebuilding the rest of your workspace.   Polyester Chart  Learn the native chart's candles, indicators, and drawing tools.   TradingView Chart  Learn the TradingView Advanced Charts widget and its controls. Customize your workspace On Advanced, customize the display from Preset Layouts in the header. Switch a starting arrangement, then save your own layout. Creating a new preset  1 Choose a preset layout Default Trading. A balanced view of charts, liquidity, order entry, activity, and Funds Compact View. More information in a tighter arrangement Chart Focused. More room for chart analysis Orderbook Focused. More room for visible liquidity and order entry     Choose a preset layout  2 Open the widgets you need Click  in a tab header to add a widget to that group. Or click  at the top of the workspace, then drag the widget where you need it.         Widgets Overview  Learn each Trading Screen widget and how to add it in Advanced. 3 Resize and arrange the panels Drag panels into place, then adjust their width and height around the information you use most. 4 Name and save your layout Click Save next to the layout name, then enter a name in Save Layout.     Click Save      Name and save the layout  Remember Layout changes affect presentation only. They do not place, modify, cancel, or settle an order. Saved layouts stay in the current browser. They do not follow your account to another device. Clearing site data can remove saved layouts. Related Topics  Overview  See how Polyester combines order-book markets, advanced trading tools, and low-latency APIs.  Overview  Learn the Trading Screen widgets you can add, group, and rearrange in Advanced layout. Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Manage Orders  Track active orders, understand fills, modify remaining quantity, and confirm how each order ends. Quick Swap  Convert one supported asset into another and deliver it to a chosen wallet with Quick Swap. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Trading /Widgets   Overview  14d ago    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    A widget is a Trading Screen panel for one job: a chart, the book, the form, or your account activity. In Advanced, you add widgets from Add Widget, then drag, resize, float, or group them as tabs. Use Standard when you want the same widgets in a fixed arrangement. Use the pages below when you want the controls inside a specific widget. Widgets These are the Trading Screen panels you can add, group, and rearrange on Advanced. Open a widget page when you want the controls inside that panel.    Polyester Chart Read candles, volume, indicators, and drawings in Polyester's native chart. Keep it beside the book, form, and account panels you use on the same market (Learn more).         TradingView Chart Analyze markets with TradingView Advanced Charts and saved chart preferences. Both charts use Polyester market data, so you can pick the charting tools that fit how you read a market (Learn more).         Depth Chart See where visible buy and sell liquidity sits around the current market. Use the curves for shape and concentration, then the Order Book for exact prices and amounts (Learn more).         Order Book Read buy and sell prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one spot market. Use it when you need exact levels next to the chart and form (Learn more).         Market Trades Follow recent public executions for the active Pair. This tape is market-level activity, not your personal fill history (Learn more).         Order Form Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls. The form uses the selected Pair's rules and the active account's available balance (Learn more).         Open Orders Monitor working and partial fills, then act on the remaining quantity. Cancel, replace, or wait as the rest of the order works (Learn more).         Triggers Monitor conditional and staged instructions before they become orders. Use this list for instructions that are waiting on a condition, not for working orders (Learn more).         Order History Review filled, canceled, expired, and rejected outcomes for this account. Use it for activity attributed to you, not for the public tape (Learn more).         Funds Compare Unified Trading and Funding balances for the two Assets in the active Pair. Keep those balances beside the form while you size an order (Learn more).       Widgets in Advanced layout On Advanced layout, add a widget to the workspace, drag it into place, or float it over the grid. View Click Add Widget in a tab header, or open the widget catalog from the workspace toolbar. Search for the panel you want, then drop it onto the screen.  Drag Drag a panel or tab to a new place on the workspace. Drop it beside another group to split the layout, or drop it onto a group to stack it as a tab. You can also move one tab from its current group into another group when you want those widgets together. Layout changes affect presentation only. They do not place, modify, cancel, or settle an order.  Float Click Float panel to pull a group out of the grid. Move the floating group, then click Dock panel to put it back.  Related Topics  Trading Screen  Use and customize Polyester's connected workspace for market analysis, order entry, and account activity. It combines historical candles, the current candle, volume, and analysis tools for the active Pair.       What the widget shows Each candle summarizes completed trades during one interval. Value What it means Open First execution price in the intervalHigh Highest execution price in the intervalLow Lowest execution price in the intervalClose Latest or final execution price in the intervalVolume Quantity executed during the interval    The current candle can change as new trades arrive. Earlier candles represent completed intervals. Choose a chart interval Select an interval that matches the move you want to study. Short intervals reveal more immediate activity and noise. Longer intervals compress short moves and make broader price structure easier to see. The current candle service supports 1 second, 1 minute, 5 minute, 15 minute, 30 minute, 1 hour, 4 hour, 12 hour, 1 day, 1 week, and 1 calendar month intervals. A history request returns 500 candles by default and at most 10,000, with time bounds and pagination for older data. Polyester does not publish a guaranteed candle-retention period. Customize the chart's theme and appearance, then add the indicators, drawings, and chart layers that support the analysis. These controls do not place an order, reserve a balance, or create a trigger. Charts show public trades, not account activity Candles are built from public completed trades. Use Open Orders and Order History to confirm activity attributed to the selected account.  Check the latest candle after reconnecting Confirm the Pair, interval, latest candle time, and connection state. The chart should reconcile missing history after a gap before it is treated as current. Related Topics  TradingView Chart  Analyze Polyester markets with TradingView Advanced Charts and your saved chart preferences. Order Book  Read current buy and sell prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one spot market. Market Trades  Follow recent public executions for the active Pair and see where trading is taking place. Use it when you prefer TradingView Advanced Charts, indicators, drawing tools, and chart controls.       Chart settings and market context TradingView changes how the market is displayed and analyzed. It does not change how Polyester admits, matches, or settles an order. Before using the chart for a decision, confirm: the active Polyester Pair matches the chart symbol; the interval and chart style fit the question you are asking; the latest candle time is current; and saved indicators or drawings are the ones you intended to load. Available tools can vary with the embedded chart configuration. The controls visible in the current widget are the source of truth. Move from analysis to an order A chart can help you choose an intended price or condition. The Order Form defines the instruction Polyester receives. Use the Order Book for current displayed liquidity and Market Trades for recent public executions. Use account order and fill records to confirm your own result.  Saved chart settings stay local Saved chart preferences can depend on the current browser. Confirm the expected style, indicators, and drawings when opening the workspace somewhere else. Related Topics  Polyester Chart  Read candles, volume, indicators, and drawings in Polyester's native market chart. Order Book  Read current buy and sell prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one spot market. Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Trading /Widgets /Depth Chart   Depth Chart  08/10    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    The Depth Chart turns the Order Book into two cumulative curves. Use it to see how visible liquidity is distributed around the spread before choosing an order size or price.       What the widget shows Element What it means Buy depth Cumulative displayed buy quantity up to each priceSell depth Cumulative displayed sell quantity up to each priceHorizontal position How far a price is from the center of the marketVertical height How much visible quantity has accumulated by that priceCenter gap The area between the best visible buy and sell prices    Hover over a curve to inspect its price and cumulative amount. A steep section means more displayed quantity is concentrated in a smaller price range. Use it with the Order Book The Depth Chart and Order Book describe the same visible liquidity in different ways. Use the chart to understand shape and concentration. Use the Order Book when you need exact prices, amounts, and cumulative totals.  Displayed depth can change The chart is not a guaranteed quote. Orders can fill, move, or cancel before another order reaches the market, and a larger order can execute across several price levels. Confirm the chart is current Confirm the active Pair and connection state before relying on the curves. After a disconnect, wait for the widget to rebuild from a fresh Order Book snapshot rather than treating the first new update as a complete view. Related Topics  Order Book  Read current buy and sell prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one spot market. Buy orders appear as bids, sell orders appear as asks, and the difference between the best bid and best ask is the spread.       What the widget shows Field What it means Price Aggregated price level in the quote Asset Amount Visible base-Asset quantity at that levelTotal Cumulative visible quantity through that levelDepth shading Relative amount or cumulative depth, depending on the selected viewSpread Difference between the best visible bid and ask    Price buckets combine orders at the selected granularity. Pair metadata controls valid price and quantity precision, so settings from one Pair should not be reused for another. Choose a price with context Selecting a price level can copy that price into the Order Form. It does not submit an order. Review the Pair, side, amount, order type, and price before continuing. A market order can execute across several levels within its price-protection boundary. A limit order controls its worst price, but it can remain partially filled or unfilled. Use the widget settings to adjust the visible depth, price grouping, base or quote display unit, and supported row layout. Use the Depth Chart when the overall shape of liquidity matters more than an exact level. Public depth snapshots support 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, or 1,000 aggregated price levels. The service default is 50, and the current client selector reaches 500. More executable liquidity can exist beyond the rows displayed, so the widget is not the authoritative test for whether a Fill Or Kill order can complete.  Wait for a synchronized book after reconnecting If prices look crossed, quantities jump without context, or updates appear stale, refresh the market view and wait for a new snapshot before relying on later changes. Related Topics  Depth Chart  See where visible buy and sell liquidity is concentrated around the current market. Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Market Trades  Follow recent public executions for the active Pair and see where trading is taking place. Each row is a completed public execution, not a resting order or an unactivated trigger.       What the widget shows Field What it means Price Price where the trade completedAmount Executed amount in the selected base or quote Asset  unitTime Time the public execution was reportedColor Displayed buy or sell direction for the trade print    The widget can show Amount in the base or quote Asset. Its volume threshold can also emphasize larger trades without removing the underlying executions from the market record. Read recent activity Market Trades shows where price discovery is happening and whether recent activity is clustered around a level. Compare it with the Polyester Chart for history and the Order Book for liquidity that is resting now.  Public trades are not private fill history A row does not identify either participant or prove that the selected account took part. Use Order History and fill details to confirm account activity, fees, and balance changes. If the tape looks stale Confirm the active Pair, latest timestamp, and connection state. Refresh the widget after a connection gap, then verify your own order independently in Order History. Related Topics  Polyester Chart  Read candles, volume, indicators, and drawings in Polyester's native market chart. Order Book  Read current buy and sell prices, the spread, and visible liquidity for one spot market. Order History  Review filled, canceled, expired, and rejected order outcomes for the selected account. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Trading /Widgets /Order Form   Order Form  08/10    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    The Order Form turns a trading decision into a precise instruction. Its controls change with the active Pair, side, order type, account permissions, and current product availability.       Changing the form prepares a future submission. It does not modify an open order unless the form was opened through an explicit modify action for that order. Review every submission Check Why it matters Pair Identifies the base and quote Assets  and current market stateSide Determines whether the order buys or sells the base Asset Order type Defines how price and execution should behaveAmount Sets the requested quantity in the displayed unitPrice or protection Sets a limit, trigger, or market-order protection when requiredTime in force and modifiers Controls how the order can work, rest, or avoid taking liquidityAvailable Balance Shows what the selected account can use for a new eligible orderEstimate and fee Previews the expected balance effect without guaranteeing execution    Pair metadata provides the price tick, quantity step or lot size, minimum quantity, minimum notional, amount scales, market state, and separate default market-order protection for Buy and Sell. It does not publish a maximum order size. The Order Form applies these Pair rules and surfaces validation when a value does not fit them. A submission can also be rejected by the available balance, account policy, market state, or an unsupported modifier. API users can read the Pair rules from the public spot configuration. A Subaccount  policy can limit maximum order notional. This is an account restriction, not a global maximum order size for the Pair. For a market order, the Pair's per-side slippage value is the default. The public order contract can override it with maximum slippage in basis points or an absolute tick delta when the selected interface exposes that choice. Self-trade prevention defaults to Expire Maker  when it is omitted. The current order contract also accepts Expire Taker  or Expire Both per order. Read the selected value before submitting instead of assuming a preference carries across forms.  Review the instruction in front of you Confirm the Pair, account, side, amount, and effective price controls after changing any option. The public Pair catalog does not publish advanced-order capability flags, so a control shown in another Pair, saved layout, or example cannot prove that a strategy is enabled end to end. After you submit Submitting begins an order lifecycle. An acknowledgement does not mean the order is working, filled, or financially settled. Use Open Orders for working quantity, Order Triggers for conditional parents, and Order History for ended outcomes. Related Topics  Open Orders  Monitor working and partially filled orders, then act on their remaining quantity. Order Triggers  Monitor conditional and staged instructions before and after they create executable orders. Order History  Review filled, canceled, expired, and rejected order outcomes for the selected account. A partially filled order can remain open for its unfilled quantity when its instructions allow it.       What the widget shows Use the Pair and side filters to narrow the table. The available columns include status, type, quantity, filled progress, average price, limit price, trade value, time in force, modifiers, and order identifiers. Read these values together: Quantity is the amount originally submitted. Filled shows how much has already executed. Remaining quantity is what can still fill or be canceled. Status shows the current order state in the account view. Select a row to view details or use the actions currently available for that order, such as modify or cancel. Cancel or modify safely  A request can race with a fill An order can fill before cancellation, fill partially while its remainder cancels, or reach another final state before a modify request arrives. Wait for the resulting order and balance state before assuming exposure is gone. A successful request does not make its outcome immediate. Preserve the order ID and follow the row until the private account view shows the final result. Reconcile after a connection gap Refresh Open Orders, recent fills, Order Triggers, and Funds. Resume trading only after those private account views agree. Ended orders move to Order History. Related Topics  Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Order Triggers  Monitor conditional and staged instructions before and after they create executable orders. Order History  Review filled, canceled, expired, and rejected order outcomes for the selected account. A trigger has its own state before it creates or manages an executable child order.       The widget organizes Stop, Trailing, TWAP, and Ladder records. Availability depends on the Pair and account. The Stop-Loss Market, Stop-Loss Limit, Trailing Stop, TWAP, and Ladder guides explain how each instruction works. What the widget shows View or field What it means All Every trigger returned by the selected filtersStop and Trailing Conditional instructions tied to a price condition or trailing distanceTWAP A staged instruction divided across a scheduleLadder A staged instruction distributed across price levelsStatus and progress Current parent state before, during, or after child execution    The table can also show Pair, side, trigger type, amount, condition, progress, parent order, and type-specific details. Available capabilities determine which tabs and fields contain live records. Trigger definitions and compacted state are stored and restored by server-side services. Conditions and strategies continue to be evaluated after the browser closes. Reconnect and refresh the record because persistence does not guarantee that a later child will pass admission or fill. Trigger family When balance is reserved Standalone stop, take-profit, trailing At trigger creationStandalone TWAP When each slice is admittedStandalone LINEAR Ladder Each immediately admitted child reserves independentlyAttached stop, take-profit, trailing Zero at setup; the risk instruction arms after its parent fills    Trigger, child order, and fill records Record What it tracks Trigger Condition, configuration, progress, and parent statusChild order Market or limit instruction created or managed by the triggerFill Completed match produced by an executable child order    An active trigger may be absent from Open Orders because it has not created a working child order yet. Follow its condition and parent status in Order Triggers. Canceling a trigger and canceling a child order are different actions. Use only the action available for the record and state you intend to stop. A child rejection is a terminal trigger failure, not a pause-until-balance-recovers state. The trigger releases its eligible hold and does not rearm automatically. If delivery was uncertain rather than explicitly rejected, Polyester can reconcile a retry under the same child identity instead of creating duplicate economic intent. Trigger family Modification while eligible and waiting Stop-loss or take-profit Trigger priceTrailing stop Distance, activation price, and maximum slippageTWAP or Ladder Not modifiable; cancel and recreate    Quantity, side, strategy family, and child template cannot be changed. The trigger modification path also does not support changing a limit child's price, even when an API request schema contains that field.  Activation does not guarantee a fill A price condition can activate a trigger, but its child order still needs to pass admission and find eligible liquidity under its own instructions. Related Topics  Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Open Orders  Monitor working and partially filled orders, then act on their remaining quantity. Order History  Review filled, canceled, expired, and rejected order outcomes for the selected account. Use it to review ended outcomes and connect an order with its fills, instructions, and final state.       What the widget shows The table can be filtered by Pair, side, and status. Its available columns include order time, Pair, side, type, status, quantity, filled amount, average price, limit price, time in force, and order identifiers. Status What it means Filled No order quantity remains after completed matchesCanceled The remaining eligible quantity was canceledExpired The instruction ended under its time or product ruleRejected The order did not become active as intended    Status alone is not the whole result. An order can fill partially before its remainder is canceled, so compare the original quantity, filled amount, and final state together. Trace an order Open the row details and keep the order ID or client order ID when one is available. Compare the submitted instructions, fills, final status, fees, and resulting balance changes.  Acknowledgement is not the final outcome A successful submission response means the request reached the trading system. Order History, fill details, and balances show what happened afterward. After a connection gap, the read view can take a moment to reconcile. Refresh the row and preserve its identifiers before escalating an apparent mismatch. Related Topics  Open Orders  Monitor working and partially filled orders, then act on their remaining quantity. Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Manage Orders  Track active orders, understand fills, modify remaining quantity, and confirm how each order ends. It shows the base and quote Assets  in both Unified Trading and Funding for the selected Master Account  or Subaccount .       What the widget shows Balance area What it means Unified Trading Balance held for trading. Open orders and other active work can reserve part of it.Funding On-chain balance available to withdraw, transfer to another account, or move into Trading.    The widget follows the active Pair, so it is a focused balance view rather than a complete portfolio. Changing the Pair changes which two Assets appear. Read a Trading balance Open a Unified Trading amount's balance detail to compare its three values. Value What it means Total Balance Posted Trading balance before active reservations are subtractedReserved Balance Amount set aside for orders, triggers, or other pending spendsAvailable Balance Amount that can support a new eligible order or transfer    An accepted order can reduce Available Balance before any fill occurs. A reservation is a hold, not proof that the Asset has been spent. Trigger families do not all reserve at the same moment: Trigger or strategy Reservation timing Standalone stop-loss or take-profit Reserves capital when the trigger is createdStandalone trailing stop Reserves capital when the trigger is createdStandalone TWAP No upfront trigger hold; each slice reserves when admittedStandalone LINEAR Ladder No parent hold; all children are admitted immediately and reserve individuallyAttached take-profit, stop-loss, or trailing risk Starts with zero reserve and arms after the parent fills    Reserved Balance follows the lifecycle of each order or trigger rather than applying one timing rule to every strategy. Add or move funds Use 'Deposit' to open the deposit page with the relevant Asset selected. Use 'Transfer' to move an available balance between eligible Polyester balance areas or accounts. The widget does not combine balances between accounts. Confirm the active Master Account or Subaccount before moving funds or placing an order. The Trading Account page explains the complete balance and reservation model. Related Topics  Order Form  Choose a side, order type, amount, price, and execution controls before submitting an order. Trading Account  Learn how the Trading Account manages available and reserved balances for trading, Lending, transfers, and withdrawals. Deposit Funds  Deposit a supported Asset from an external Network and confirm where Polyester credits it. What it does A market order prioritizes an immediate execution attempt. It takes eligible liquidity from the best available price outward until the requested quantity fills or no more liquidity is available within its protection boundary. The final average price can differ from the price shown when you submit because the order may fill across several Order Book levels. How it works Polyester converts a Market order into an immediate-or-cancel order at the accepted price-protection boundary. It matches against eligible liquidity up to that boundary, then cancels any unfilled quantity. Completed fills remain final. A canceled remainder does not become an open order.  Market does not mean any price Price protection limits how far the order can move through the book. A Market order can fill completely, fill partially, or receive no fill when eligible liquidity is unavailable within that boundary. When to use it Use it when trading now matters most. Choose a Market order when attempting to enter or exit immediately matters more than receiving one exact price. Avoid it when you need a firm price boundary. Choose a Limit order when you will not buy above or sell below a specific price, especially when visible liquidity is thin. Review the Order Book, estimated price impact, minimum received, and current price-protection setting before submitting a larger Market order. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to buy 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, and entering the market now matters more to you than receiving one exact price. You choose a Market order. You submit a Market buy for 0.01 BTC. The best eligible ask fills 0.006 BTC at 100,000 USDT. The next eligible ask fills the remaining 0.004 BTC at 100,050 USDT. The order completes because both prices are within its price-protection boundary. Result: You buy 0.01 BTC for 1,000.20 USDT before fees, at an average price of 100,020 USDT. These are example prices and available quantities. Actual execution depends on live liquidity and the order's price-protection setting. What to watch Available prices can change between review and execution. A larger order can move through several price levels. Price protection can leave part or all of the order unfilled. Each completed fill receives its own maker  or taker  treatment and fee. Use a Limit Order when a specific price boundary matters more than trading immediately. Related Topics  Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A limit order gives you control over the worst price the order may accept. A Limit buy can execute at its limit price or lower, while a Limit sell can execute at its limit price or higher. If eligible liquidity is not available, the order can remain open, fill partially, or end without a fill according to its time-in-force instruction. How it works Side Price boundary Example Buy The order cannot pay more than the limit price A buy at 99,000 USDT can fill at 99,000 USDT or lowerSell The order cannot accept less than the limit price A sell at 101,000 USDT can fill at 101,000 USDT or higher    A Limit order can rest in the Order Book, but it can also execute immediately when its price crosses available liquidity. Add post-only  when it must add liquidity instead of executing immediately as a taker .  A limit price does not guarantee a fill The market may never reach your price, or only part of the requested quantity may become available there. When to use it Use it when your price boundary matters most. Choose a Limit order when you will buy only at or below a maximum price, or sell only at or above a minimum price. Avoid it when you need to trade immediately. Choose a Market order when attempting execution now matters more than waiting for one price or better. Choose the limit price, time-in-force, and post-only setting based on whether the order may wait, take liquidity immediately, or must remain maker-only. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to buy 0.01 BTC, but only if the price falls to 99,000 USDT or lower. Because that maximum price matters more to you than buying immediately, you choose a Limit order. You submit a Limit buy for 0.01 BTC at 99,000 USDT. The best available ask is still above 99,000 USDT, so the order waits in the Order Book. Bitcoin falls and 0.006 BTC becomes available at 99,000 USDT, partially filling the order. The remaining 0.004 BTC later fills at 98,950 USDT, which is better than your limit price. Result: You buy 0.01 BTC for 989.80 USDT before fees, at an average price of 98,980 USDT. The order never pays more than 99,000 USDT per BTC. These are example prices and available quantities. If the market never reaches the limit, the order may remain open or end without filling. What to watch A Limit order is not guaranteed to fill. Partial fills can leave quantity open in the Order Book. A crossing Limit order can execute immediately as a taker. Time-in-force determines what happens to unfilled quantity. Use a Market Order when trading immediately matters more than one fixed price. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does Time-in-force controls whether unfilled quantity waits, cancels, or prevents the order from executing at all. Post-only prevents a limit order from taking liquidity. These are instructions applied to eligible orders, not separate markets. How it works Instruction Immediate behavior Unfilled quantity GTC Eligible quantity can fill The remainder stays active until filled, canceled, or ended by another market or order lifecycle actionIOC Eligible quantity fills immediately The remainder is canceledFOK The complete quantity must fill immediately The entire order is canceled if a full fill is unavailablePost-only A crossing order is rejected No taker execution occurs    In the current spot model, post-only applies to an eligible limit GTC order. Market execution is IOC-style rather than a resting time-in-force choice. When to use each instruction Instruction Use it when Avoid it when GTC Unfilled quantity may wait for future liquidity Any resting remainder would create unwanted exposureIOC Available quantity should fill now without leaving a remainder The complete amount must fill or the order should do nothingFOK The complete amount must fill immediately or not at all A partial fill would still be usefulPost-only The order must add liquidity as a maker  Immediate execution matters or the price may cross the current market    A limit price by itself does not guarantee maker status. Polyester rejects a post-only order that would cross the book. It does not reprice the order to keep it resting, and post-only cannot be combined with a market order. FOK evaluates all executable matching-engine liquidity within the order's price boundary after self-trade prevention. The visible Order Book can show only part of that liquidity, so its displayed rows are useful context but not the authoritative FOK test. GTC has no implemented maximum lifetime or hidden expiry timestamp. Pair disablement, delisting, cancellation, or another explicit lifecycle action can still terminate the order, but those events are not a GTC time-to-live.  Available combinations depend on the Pair The active Pair determines which instructions and combinations are available. Use the controls shown in the current Order Form or supported by the approved API Reference. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to place a 0.01 BTC Limit buy at that price, but only 0.006 BTC is available immediately. You choose the instruction based on whether a partial fill is useful, whether the remainder can wait, or whether the entire order must fill at once. You choose post-only when your goal is to add liquidity instead of executing immediately. Here is what each instruction does: GTC can fill 0.006 BTC and leave the remaining 0.004 BTC open on the Order Book. IOC can fill 0.006 BTC and cancel the remaining 0.004 BTC. FOK cancels the entire order because the full 0.01 BTC cannot fill immediately. Post-only rejects the order if its 100,000 USDT limit price would immediately match a resting ask. Result: The price and quantity stay the same, but the instruction changes what happens to the order and any unfilled quantity. These are example prices and available quantities. FOK evaluates all eligible matching-engine liquidity, which can differ from the rows currently visible in the Order Book. What to watch Maker or taker treatment is determined per fill. A partially resting order can have both immediate and later fills when post-only is not used. Self-trade prevention can end an otherwise eligible match. A post-only rejection means the submitted price would have removed liquidity at admission. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance.
