What it would do In the general market concept, an iceberg order exposes only part of a larger limit instruction in the public Order Book. The undisplayed remainder stays hidden under defined replenishment rules. It is designed for a trader who wants limit-price control without displaying the full intended quantity at once. Repeated displayed fills can still reveal the larger execution over time.  Iceberg is not available The current public order and trigger contracts have no Iceberg request. The public Pair catalog also has no advanced-order capability flag that enables it. How the concept works Quantity or rule What it controls Total quantity The complete amount managed by the instructionDisplay quantity The maximum amount shown publicly at one timeHidden quantity The undisplayed remainderReplenishment When another displayed portion enters the book after fillsPriority Whether replenished quantity keeps or receives a new time priority    These fields describe the concept only. Polyester has not published reservation, replenishment, queue-priority, cancellation, or lifecycle rules for an implemented Iceberg order. When it would fit Use it when displayed size should stay smaller. The concept fits a larger limit order that should reveal only part of its intended quantity at once. Avoid it when the instruction must work on Polyester today. Iceberg is not currently available, and repeated replenishment can still reveal the larger intent over time. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to sell 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, without displaying the full order at once. You would choose an Iceberg order with a 0.002 BTC display quantity so only one portion is visible at a time. The first 0.002 BTC appears in the public Order Book. After that portion fills, the next 0.002 BTC becomes visible under the order's priority rules. The order continues replenishing in 0.002 BTC portions until the full 0.01 BTC fills or the order ends. Result: No more than 0.002 BTC is displayed at once, though repeated fills can still reveal that a larger order exists. This is a conceptual example. Polyester does not currently accept Iceberg orders through the application or public API. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A time-weighted average price strategy divides a target quantity into child orders released across a configured period. TWAP reduces dependence on one moment of liquidity. It does not guarantee the market's TWAP benchmark, a better price, or a complete fill.  TWAP availability depends on configuration A visible form or request field does not establish end-to-end support. Use TWAP when the current product flow exposes the strategy and its lifecycle for the active Pair and account. How it works Setting What it controls Total quantity The complete amount the strategy attempts to tradeDuration How long the release schedule runsSlice interval The time between child-order attemptsChild type Market-IOC or supported limit-GTC behaviorLimit price The execution boundary when limit children are used    Each child must independently satisfy current Pair metadata, including quantity, price, and minimum-order rules. TWAP creates no upfront trigger-level reservation. Each slice requests and holds the balance it needs when that child is admitted. A later slice can therefore fail even when the parent strategy was accepted. The strategy definition and compacted state are persisted and evaluated server-side. Closing the browser does not stop its schedule, so return to Order Triggers and the child-order views to reconcile progress. The first explicit child rejection fails the parent and stops future slices. Children admitted before that failure remain real orders: their completed fills stay final, and any still-working child must be monitored or canceled under its own lifecycle. An uncertain transport attempt can be retried under the same slice identity. That reconciliation is different from skipping or retrying a child that admission explicitly rejected. When to use it Use it when execution should be spread through time. TWAP fits a target quantity that should be divided into scheduled attempts instead of entering the market all at once. Avoid it when immediate completion or one price matters. Choose another order when the entire quantity should execute now or when every fill must respect one fixed limit. Monitor the parent for schedule progress and the child orders for actual fills, rejections, and remaining exposure. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to buy 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, without submitting the entire order at once. You choose TWAP to spread the order across 10 minutes. TWAP divides the order into ten 0.001 BTC child orders. Polyester attempts one child order each minute. Each child passes admission and reserves balance when its turn arrives. If the sixth child is rejected, the remaining scheduled children stop. The first five children and any completed fills remain valid. Result: If all ten child orders complete, you trade 0.01 BTC over the 10-minute schedule. Your average price depends on the price of each fill. This is an example schedule. TWAP does not guarantee a benchmark price, a complete fill, or lower fees. What to watch Market conditions can change between slices. A child can partially fill, receive no fill, or fail admission. A valid parent does not make every child valid. Canceling the parent can race with a child already being released. Fees apply to completed child fills, not the planned schedule. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A ladder distributes a target quantity across several limit-price levels. It expresses a scaled entry or exit without manually creating each child order. Each level becomes an independent limit order with its own position, fills, fees, and final state.  Ladder availability depends on configuration A visible form or request field does not establish end-to-end support. Use Ladder when the current product flow exposes the strategy and its lifecycle for the active Pair and account. How it works Setting What it controls Minimum price One boundary of the ladder rangeMaximum price The other boundary of the ladder rangeLevels The number of limit children distributed across the rangeTotal quantity The amount allocated across all levels    The current client builds linearly distributed limit-GTC levels. Every rounded child must independently satisfy the Pair's price increment, quantity increment, and minimum-order rules. Only the LINEAR distribution is supported by the current public create-trigger contract. Geometric, weighted, or another nonlinear distribution is not available. Internal representations of those choices do not make them callable. The parent Ladder creates no trigger-level reservation. All LINEAR child orders are admitted immediately, and each resting child reserves its own balance. The compacted strategy state persists server-side after the browser closes. Children are admitted in sequence. The first explicit rejection, transport failure, or system error stops further children and marks the parent failed. Ladder does not retry that failed level. Children accepted before that point remain live or filled and are not rolled back automatically. When to use it Use it when entry or exit should span a price range. Ladder fits a plan that intentionally distributes quantity across several limit-price levels. Avoid it when one price or immediate execution matters. Choose one Limit or Market order when separate children would add unnecessary exposure, reservations, or monitoring. Review the generated children before submission. One level can fill while other levels remain active, so the result can be only part of the intended ladder. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You want to buy 0.01 BTC across several price levels instead of relying on one entry price. You choose a five-level LINEAR Ladder with 0.002 BTC at each level. Polyester creates Limit buys at 98,000, 99,000, 100,000, 101,000, and 102,000 USDT. Each 0.002 BTC child order is admitted and reserves balance independently. One price level can fill while the other child orders remain open. If a child is rejected, Polyester stops submitting later children without canceling or reversing the children already accepted. Result: The five planned child orders total 0.01 BTC and exactly 1,000 USDT across the example price range. These are example prices. Rounding, Pair minimums, available balance, fills, and fees apply separately to every child order. What to watch A wide range can leave some children far from the market. Open children reserve balance independently. Partial execution changes the remaining exposure across the range. Canceling the parent can race with a match at one level. A ladder does not guarantee that every level fills. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A stop-loss market trigger watches for a downside condition, then attempts to submit a market-style child order. It prioritizes an execution attempt after activation rather than setting one fixed execution price. How it works Watch: Last Price is compared with the configured condition. Activate: the condition is met and Polyester attempts to admit the child order. Execute: the market-IOC child takes eligible liquidity within configured price protection. Reconcile: child orders, fills, and balances establish the final outcome. The trigger and child have separate states. An accepted trigger does not prove that the later child is admitted, filled, or settled.  This is not a guaranteed exit The child can fill across several prices, fill only partially, or receive no fill within current protection and liquidity. When to use it Use it when an execution attempt matters most. Stop-Loss Market fits a downside condition where attempting to reduce exposure matters more than one fixed execution price. Avoid it when a precise exit price must be protected. Choose Stop-Loss Limit when selling below a defined price would be worse than leaving some or all of the position open. Confirm the active market, eligible side, quantity, trigger condition, price source, and price-protection control shown by the current form. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You hold 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, and want to reduce your exposure if the price falls to 95,000 USDT. Because attempting to exit matters more to you than receiving one exact price, you choose Stop-Loss Market. A Last Price trade at 95,000 USDT activates the stop. The best eligible bid can buy 0.006 BTC at 94,900 USDT, so the Market child fills that amount first. The next eligible bid can buy the remaining 0.004 BTC at 94,850 USDT, completing the order. Result: You sell the full 0.01 BTC for 948.80 USDT before fees, at an average price of 94,880 USDT. This is example liquidity. A real child order can fill partially or receive no fill when eligible bids do not exist within price protection. What to watch A gap can move available prices before the child is admitted. Price protection can produce a partial fill or no fill. Balance, policy, or market state can reject the child. Canceling after activation can race with execution. Verify the trigger in Order Triggers, then verify fills in Order History. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A stop-loss limit trigger activates after a downside condition and attempts to submit a limit child at a separate configured price. It adds price control after activation, but that control can prevent the child from completing. How it works Price Purpose Trigger price Determines when the condition activatesLimit price Defines the worst price the child may accept    After activation, the child follows normal limit-order behavior. It can execute immediately, fill in parts, rest in Open Orders, or remain completely unfilled.  Activation does not guarantee a fill If the market moves beyond the limit before the child can match, the limit order can remain open while the market continues away from it. When to use it Use it when the child needs a firm price boundary. Stop-Loss Limit fits a downside condition where the trader will not accept execution beyond a chosen limit price. Avoid it when reducing exposure matters more than price. Choose Stop-Loss Market when a limit child remaining unfilled would create more risk than price movement during execution. Confirm both prices, the eligible side, quantity, price source, time-in-force, precision, and available balance before submitting. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You hold 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, and want to reduce your exposure if the price falls to 95,000 USDT, but you will not sell below 94,500 USDT. Because that minimum price matters more than guaranteeing a fill, you choose Stop-Loss Limit. A Last Price trade at or below 95,000 USDT activates the stop. Polyester submits a Limit sell for 0.01 BTC at 94,500 USDT. The market gaps to 94,000 USDT, where all available bids are below your limit price. The child order does not accept those lower bids and remains open. Result: Your 0.01 BTC remains unsold until eligible liquidity reaches 94,500 USDT or higher, or you cancel the child order. These are example prices. A child order can also fill partially before its remaining quantity rests. What to watch A fast move can pass through the limit before the child works. A restrictive limit can leave exposure open. Partial fills can leave a working remainder. Canceling the trigger does not cancel a child that already exists. Monitor the parent in Order Triggers and the child separately. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Trailing Stop  Follow a favorable price extreme and activate a child order after price reverses by a configured distance. What it does A trailing stop follows a favorable price extreme at a configured distance. When price reverses through the current trigger, Polyester attempts to submit the configured child order. Unlike a fixed stop, the trigger can become more protective as the market moves favorably. How it works Setting What it controls Trailing distance The supported percentage or quote amount between the favorable extreme and triggerFavorable extreme The highest observed price for the current standalone trailing sell modelActivation price An optional condition that starts trailing only after price reaches itSlippage cap Price protection for the market-style child after activation    The trigger moves with a new favorable extreme. It holds its most protective level when price reverses, then activates when the condition is met.  Current standalone behavior The current public create-trigger path supports standalone Trailing Stop only on the Sell side and uses a market-IOC child. It rejects a standalone Buy trailing stop, including through the API. An attached Buy trailing child can arise only as opposite-side risk after a Sell parent fills. A standalone trailing stop reserves capital when it is created. An attached trailing-risk instruction begins with zero reservation and arms after its parent fills. Both are persisted and evaluated server-side, so closing the browser does not cancel them. When to use it Use it when protection should follow a favorable move. Trailing Stop fits a position that should keep gaining room while price rises, then react after a defined reversal. Avoid it when a fixed trigger is more appropriate. Choose a fixed stop when the exit condition should not move or when ordinary volatility could activate the selected trail too early. Choose a distance that matches the trading plan. A smaller distance reacts sooner, while a larger distance allows more movement before activation. Example Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at 100,000 USDT. You hold 0.01 BTC, worth about 1,000 USDT, and want your protection to follow the price higher without manually moving a fixed stop. You choose a Sell trailing stop with a 5% distance so it activates after a 5% reversal from the highest observed price. At 100,000 USDT, the trigger begins at 95,000 USDT, which is 5% below the current high. BTC rises to 110,000 USDT, so the trigger moves up to 104,500 USDT. BTC then falls to 104,500 USDT, activating the Market IOC child for 0.01 BTC. Result: The trigger follows the market higher, then attempts to sell after price reverses by 5% from the new high. These are example prices. The trailing distance controls activation, not the final fill price. What to watch The trailing distance controls activation, not the final fill price. A small distance can activate during ordinary market movement. A large distance can allow a larger reversal before activation. A gap can change execution after the trigger fires. Balance, policy, or market state can block the child at activation. Related Topics  Market Order  Attempt immediate execution against available Order Book liquidity within price protection. Limit Order  Buy at a chosen maximum price or sell at a chosen minimum price. Time-in-Force & Post-Only  Control what happens to unfilled limit quantity and whether an order may remove liquidity immediately. Iceberg  Understand the Iceberg order concept and its current availability on Polyester. TWAP  Spread a target quantity across scheduled child orders while monitoring execution, timing, and completion risk. Ladder  Distribute a target quantity across planned limit-price levels and monitor each child order independently. Stop-Loss Market  Attempt market-style execution after a downside condition while accounting for gaps, protection, and partial fills. Stop-Loss Limit  Activate a limit child after a downside condition while keeping trigger price and execution boundary distinct. These views show its current state, completed fills, active quantity, and final result. Your orders and attributed fills remain private to your account. Confirm the active account whenever an expected order does not appear. Order views Each order moves between connected views. View Use it for Open Orders Monitoring orders with quantity still active and opening modify or cancel actionsOrder History Reviewing filled, canceled, expired, and rejected outcomesTriggers Monitoring stop, trailing, TWAP, and ladder instructions before and after they create ordersOrder Details Connecting the selected order with its instructions, identifiers, fills, fees, and Transfers    Open Orders and Order History can follow the active Pair. Change or clear their filters when you need to find activity from another market in the same account.        Open Orders Order History Triggers                  Select a row to open Order Details. The panel connects the order's instructions, fill progress, trades, fees, and identifiers.       Completed fills also appear in Trades, with the Order ID that connects each fill to its order.       Order states State What it means What remains possible Pending The request was accepted but is not yet confirmed as working or ended Wait for the next stateWorking Remaining quantity is active under the order's instructions Match, modify, or cancelPartially Filled One or more fills completed while quantity remains active Completed fills stay final; the remainder can keep working, modify, or cancelPending Cancel Polyester received a cancellation request, but the order can still match Wait for a final state or updated progressFilled The full effective quantity matched Review fills, Average Price, fees, and balance changesCanceled or Expired No quantity remains active, although partial fills can remain final Review the terminal reason and released reservationRejected The order never became Working Correct the rejection reason before submitting again    A submission confirmation means Polyester received the request, not that the order is already Working. Orders continue server-side after you close the browser, sign out, or lose a connection. Modify an open order The quantity entered in Modify Order becomes the new total for the order, not the new remaining quantity. If the new total is equal to or below the amount already filled, Polyester treats the change as a request to cancel the remaining quantity. Behavior What it does Order identity Amend Only Applies the change only when the existing order can be amended safely Keeps the existing Order IDAmend or Replace Amends when possible and otherwise replaces the active order The final Order ID can changeReplace Only Cancels the active order and submits a replacement Creates a new Order ID    An in-place amend is limited to a Limit order that keeps its price and does not increase its total quantity. Changing the price, increasing total quantity, or selecting Replace Only creates a new order at the back of the applicable price queue. A replacement protects the new order first. Available Balance can briefly reflect both sides of a safe replacement transition. Confirm the final order and reservation before using the expected released balance. Cancel orders Cancellation applies only to quantity that remains active. It cannot reverse a completed fill.  Cancellation can race with a fill An order can still match while its cancellation is processing. The final order state and Trades determine how much filled and how much canceled. Cancel all open orders Cancel All Orders previews how many open orders it will target before confirmation.  Table filters do not limit Cancel All Cancel All applies to every open order in the selected account, not only the Pair or Side visible in the filtered table. Review the preview count, then confirm each final outcome because individual orders can still fill or fail to cancel. An order can also end when its time-in-force instruction cancels a remainder, self-trade prevention ends it, a replacement takes over, or another lifecycle action makes it terminal. Rejected orders A rejected order never became Working. Use its displayed reason to identify the failed requirement. Balance and policy: Confirm the account has enough Available Balance and permission to place the order. Pair rules: Check the current quantity, price, minimum, and precision requirements. Order instructions: Confirm the side, order type, time-in-force, and post-only combination is supported. Market state: Confirm the Pair currently accepts the requested action. Use the current Order Form and rejection reason instead of copying values from an older order. You select what to send, what to receive, and where the output should go. Polyester handles the deposit, conversion through its order books, and delivery on the destination chain. You do not need to move funds into a regular Polyester Trading Account or place an order yourself. Quick Swap presents the complete route  and quote before you send the input asset.       Swap and deliver an asset One Quick Swap connects the input transfer, protected order-book conversion, and output delivery.  1 Choose what you want to send and receive Select the input asset and chain, then choose the output asset and destination chain. 2 Enter the amount and destination Add the amount you want to convert and the wallet address that should receive the output. 3 Review the quote Check the exchange rate, protected output, itemized fees, destination, and expiration before continuing. 4 Send the input asset Use the deposit instructions assigned to this swap so Polyester can identify the transfer. 5 Follow the conversion and delivery Track the input transfer, order-book conversion, and final delivery from the same swap record. How Quick Swap works Each Quick Swap is one connected request. Polyester assigns deposit instructions to that request, identifies the incoming transfer, and makes the input balance available only for the quoted conversion. The conversion executes against liquidity in Polyester's dedicated order book for the selected Pair. Quick Swap does not use an AMM, bridge pool, or liquidity from another exchange. Price protection in the quote limits the result you agree to accept. After the conversion settles, Polyester sends the output asset through the selected destination route. The swap is complete when the output reaches its final delivery state, not merely when the input transfer confirms or the trade fills. Review your quote The quote brings the important choices and costs together before you send funds: You send shows the input asset, source chain, and exact amount. You receive shows the output asset, destination chain, and protected output. Rate and price protection show how the conversion is priced and the minimum acceptable result. Fees itemize the trading, network, and service or partner charges included in the swap. Destination shows the complete receiving address and any required memo or tag. Expiration shows how long the quote and its deposit instructions remain valid. The displayed output is a quote until the conversion executes. Market movement can change the final result within the accepted protection; it cannot make the completed output lower than the quote's protected amount.  Use the instructions for the current swap Send only the selected asset and chain to the deposit instructions shown for that Quick Swap. Confirm the complete destination and any memo or tag before sending, because an external transfer cannot be reversed by Polyester. Quick Swap settings Quick Swap settings belong to the individual quote, so the choices remain visible together when you review the swap. Assets, chains, and amount Choose the asset and chain you are sending from, the asset and chain you want to receive, and the amount to convert. Available combinations and amount limits come from the current routes and order-book liquidity. Price protection Price protection defines the lowest output the swap can accept as the market order executes. Stronger protection narrows the acceptable result, while a wider range gives the order more room to complete as the market moves. Destination and recovery The destination identifies where the converted asset should arrive. When a separate recovery address is required, it applies to the original input asset and source chain; it does not replace the output destination. Quote expiration The expiration keeps the route, price protection, and fees tied to current conditions. Start the transfer while the quote is active. If it expires before you send, request a new quote instead of reusing the old instructions. Track your swap The swap record keeps the input transaction, conversion, fees, output transaction, and final result together under one Quick Swap ID. Use it to follow progress after leaving the page or closing the browser. An input transaction can be confirmed while the conversion or delivery is still processing. Continue following the same record until it shows the final output amount and destination result. Your fee rate depends on your VIP tier and whether the fill is classified as maker  or taker . For eligible buy orders, you can also choose which asset pays the fee. There is no fee to place or cancel an order that does not fill. Spot trading fee schedule VIP tier Maker fee Taker fee   VIP 0 0.100% 0.150%  VIP 1 0.080% 0.135%  VIP 2 0.065% 0.120%  VIP 3 0.050% 0.105%  VIP 4 0.040% 0.090%  VIP 5 0.030% 0.080%  VIP 6 0.020% 0.070%  VIP 7 0.015% 0.060%  VIP 8 0.0125% 0.055%  VIP 9 0.010% 0.050%  VIP 10 0.005% 0.045%    Fees are calculated from the value of each completed fill. If an order fills in several parts, the applicable fee is calculated separately for each fill.  Your VIP tier determines your rate This table shows each tier's base rate. Symbol-specific adjustments, rewards, and referral discounts
can lower your effective rate. Authenticated API clients can call GET /v1/spot/fee-rates for exact
rates by symbol. See VIP Tiers to learn how your tier is
determined and how to progress to the next level. Maker and taker fees Role When it applies Maker Your order rests on the order book before another order fills against it.Taker Your order fills immediately against liquidity already resting on the order book.    A limit order can be both: any quantity that fills immediately pays the taker rate, while quantity that rests and fills later pays the maker rate. Choose how your fee is paid Most exchanges decide the fee asset for you. On Polyester, an eligible buy order lets you choose Quote or Received from the Fee Source selector in the Order Form. Your choice appears again when you review the order. Quote pays the fee with the quote asset  you are spending. When buying BTC/USDT, the fee is paid in USDT. Received deducts the fee from the base asset  you receive. When buying BTC/USDT, the fee is paid in BTC. The percentage rate does not change. The fee is calculated in the selected asset: Fee source Calculation Effect on a buy order Quote Fill value in the quote asset × fee rate You spend slightly more quote asset and receive the full base quantity.Received Base quantity received × fee rate You spend the entered quote amount and receive slightly less base asset.    Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at $100,000 and you buy $1,000 of BTC at a 0.08% fee rate. With Quote, the fee is 0.80 USDT. You spend 1,000.80 USDT and receive 0.01 BTC. With Received, the fee is 0.000008 BTC. You spend 1,000 USDT and receive 0.009992 BTC after the fee. Sell-order fees are deducted from the quote asset received from the sale. For example, selling 0.01 BTC for 1,000 USDT at a 0.08% rate returns 999.20 USDT after the 0.80 USDT fee.  Fee Source is available on eligible buy orders Quote is the default. The Received option appears only when the selected market and order support paying with the base asset you receive. Referral discounts and rewards Referral codes affect positive trading fees in two different ways: Who receives the benefit Benefit What it applies to Referred trader 4% lower trading fees Positive maker or taker fees on eligible fillsReferrer 15% of the referred user's paid trading fees The fee remaining after the referred trader's discount    The referral benefit is calculated from the trading fee, not the order's full value. Let's say a referred trader completes a $1,000 fill at a 0.08% fee rate: The standard trading fee is 0.80 USDT. The 4% referral discount saves the trader 0.032 USDT. The referred trader pays 0.768 USDT. The referrer earns 15% of that paid fee, or 0.1152 USDT. Referral discounts and rewards apply only when a positive trading fee is charged. They do not
create a negative fee or maker rebate. See Referrals for referral eligibility, links, rewards, and account-level reporting. You do not need both. Polyester applies the higher result to your Master Account  and all of its Subaccounts . 14-day average spot volume: Polyester averages the USD value of completed spot fills over 14 days. 60-day average account equity: Polyester averages eligible balances over 60 days. VIP tier requirements Qualify by meeting either the volume requirement or the equity requirement for a tier. VIP tier 30-day settled spot volume 30-day average account equity   VIP 0 Default Default  VIP 1 $100,000 $50,000  VIP 2 $500,000 $100,000  VIP 3 $1,000,000 $250,000  VIP 4 $5,000,000 $500,000  VIP 5 $10,000,000 $1,000,000  VIP 6 $25,000,000 $2,500,000  VIP 7 $50,000,000 $5,000,000  VIP 8 $100,000,000 $10,000,000  VIP 9 $250,000,000 $25,000,000  VIP 10 $500,000,000 $100,000,000     The higher qualifying tier wins Volume and equity are evaluated separately. They are not added together, and you never need to meet both thresholds. See Trading Fees for the maker  and taker  rate at every tier. How your tier is calculated Spot trading volume Polyester adds the USD value of your settled spot fills across the rolling 30-day window. Open,
canceled, unfilled, and failed-settlement quantities do not count. 30-day settled spot volume = settled spot fill value over the rolling 30-day window Maker and taker fills both count. Activity from the Master Account and every Subaccount beneath it is combined into the same volume total. Account equity Polyester measures the USD value of your eligible account equity across the Master Account and all
of its Subaccounts, then averages hourly values across the rolling 30-day window. 30-day average account equity = total hourly account equity values / 720 Funding and Trading balances count toward the same account-level equity total. Moving an asset between your own accounts does not create additional equity, and a large new deposit must remain in the account long enough to raise the rolling average. Examples Qualify through trading volume. Your settled 30-day spot volume is $6 million, which qualifies
for VIP 4. Your 30-day average account equity is $200,000, which qualifies for VIP 2. Polyester
applies VIP 4 because the volume path gives you the higher tier. Qualify through account equity. Your settled 30-day spot volume is $600,000, which qualifies
for VIP 2. Your 30-day average account equity is $1.2 million, which qualifies for VIP 5.
Polyester applies VIP 5 even though your trading volume is below the VIP 5 requirement. Use the higher tier without combining paths. If your volume qualifies for VIP 5 and your
equity qualifies for VIP 4, your effective tier is VIP 5. The two results do not combine into
VIP 6. When your tier changes Polyester evaluates complete qualification data hourly. Your tier can move up or down as new
activity enters each rolling window and older activity leaves it. Account-equity promotions require
the full threshold, while an existing account-equity tier is retained down to 95% of its threshold
to avoid frequent changes near a boundary. A new tier applies to future fills; it does not recalculate fees on trades that have already
settled. Authenticated API clients can call GET /v1/vip/status to inspect the current component
tiers, metrics, and next-tier thresholds. GET /v1/vip/tiers returns the active public catalog. You do not need to hold the destination chain's native gas asset for Polyester to complete the transaction.  Example: withdraw USDT on Ethereum   When you withdraw    USDT on    Ethereum , Polyester pays the Ethereum gas fee in    ETH and charges you the displayed withdrawal fee in USDT. This lets you withdraw USDT without also keeping ETH in your Polyester balance. Fees can change as network gas costs and asset prices change. Always use the current fee shown for the exact asset and chain you select. A deposit fee is deducted from the amount credited, while a withdrawal fee is included in the final withdrawal review. The fee charged by Polyester is separate from any gas fee your external wallet charges when you send a deposit to Polyester. Current fees Search by token or chain to compare network fees, minimum amounts, and estimated confirmation time.  The same fee applies to deposits and withdrawals The Network fee shown for each asset and chain is the fee Polyester charges in both directions. There is no separate deposit rate or withdrawal rate for the same route . Your friend receives 4% off eligible trading fees, while you earn 15% of the trading fees they pay. They save, and you earn. The Referrals page gives you everything you need to create custom links, understand where new traders come from, follow every reward, and automatically convert earnings into the asset you want to hold.       How referrals work Create a link from the Referrals page and share it wherever you connect with traders. Polyester handles the attribution, applies your friend's discount, and records your share whenever they pay an eligible trading fee.  1 Create a referral link Use Create new referral link, give it a recognizable name based on where you plan to share it, and copy the URL.             2 Invite a friend Share the link directly or publish it for your audience. When someone creates an account through it, Polyester attributes that account to you. 3 Your friend saves on fees Your friend receives 4% off every eligible positive spot trading fee. 4 You earn a fee share You receive 15% of the discounted fee your friend pays. Each reward appears in your Reward Ledger, ready to track, convert, or claim. Create multiple referral links Create and name separate links for social posts, communities, campaigns, or individual invitations. Every link uses your referral ID, while its name makes the source easy to recognize. Switch between links from the Referral Link selector. At    VIP 1, you can set a custom code for a link. You can only set that code once, and it cannot be changed afterward.       When a custom code is unlocked, the selected link shows that you can set one.       Referral Analytics attributes users, trading volume, and rewards to the link each trader used. This lets you compare audiences without creating separate referral accounts. Granular reward tracking The Reward Ledger records the link, eligible fee event, reward asset, amount, and status behind each earning. Rewards first appear in the asset used to pay the trading fee, giving you a complete history from the original trade to the amount you receive. See Referral Rewards for the complete discount and reward calculation. Dynamic reward payouts Choose the asset you want to receive and how often rewards should be converted. Polyester can keep rewards in their original assets or convert available rewards into one selected payout asset at the interval you set. For example, you can automatically convert USDT rewards into SOL instead of managing each reward asset separately. Each payout conversion remains visible in the Reward Ledger. Related Topics  Rewards  See how referral rewards are calculated, collected, converted, and paid to your Trading Account. Analytics  Track referred users, trading volume, and rewards across every referral link and date range. When a friend joins through your referral, they receive 4% off each eligible positive trading fee, and you earn 15% of the discounted fee they pay. The Referrals page shows your earnings by asset and records every reward in a detailed ledger. Collect rewards manually or on an automatic schedule, then keep the original assets or convert them into the payout asset you choose. How your reward is calculated The calculation begins with the maker  or taker  fee charged on an eligible fill. Polyester first applies the referred trader's 4% discount, then calculates your 15% reward from the fee they actually pay. Let's say Bitcoin is currently trading at $100,000, and your friend completes a $1,000 BTC/USDT trade at a 0.08% fee rate: The standard trading fee is 0.80 USDT. The 4% referral discount saves your friend 0.032 USDT. Your friend pays 0.768 USDT after the discount. You earn 15% of the paid fee, or 0.1152 USDT. The reward appears in your Reward Ledger as 0.1152 USDT. The fee share is based on the trading fee, not the value of the trade, deposit, withdrawal, or account balance.  Referral rewards apply only to positive fees A fill with a 0.00% maker fee does not create a referral reward. Maker rebates are separate: a negative maker rate rewards the trader directly and is not discounted or shared with a referrer. How rewards are credited Your reward is first recorded in the asset used to pay the trading fee. This keeps every ledger entry connected to the actual fee that produced it, even when your referred traders pay fees in several different assets. The Reward Ledger gives each amount a clear history, including: the referral link that produced it; the eligible fee event; the original reward asset and amount; any automatic conversion; and its available or claimed status.       Claim your rewards The Referrals page groups available rewards by asset. To collect them manually, review the balance, choose Claim Rewards, and confirm the payout to your Trading Account. You can keep each reward in its original asset or convert it into another asset as part of the claim.       Completed claims remain in the Reward Ledger, giving you one history from the original trading fee through conversion and payout.  Collect rewards automatically Turn on automatic collection to send available rewards to your Trading Account without returning to select Claim. Choose the payout interval in minutes and the asset you want to receive. When the selected payout asset differs from the assets you earned, Polyester converts the rewards as part of each automatic payout. Choose your payout asset Reward conversion happens when rewards are collected. For a manual claim, choose the destination asset in the claim flow. For automatic collection, save one preferred payout asset in your automatic payout settings. For example, if you earn USDT but want to accumulate SOL, choose SOL before confirming a manual claim or set SOL as the asset for automatic payouts. Polyester converts the available USDT at the current market price, deposits the resulting SOL into your Trading Account, and records both sides of the conversion in the Reward Ledger. If you keep the original reward assets, Polyester deposits them without conversion. See Trading Fees for the complete spot fee schedule and maker rebate tiers. See Analytics to compare earnings across links and referred users. Related Topics  Overview  Invite friends to Polyester, earn a share of their trading fees, and track every referral from one dashboard. Analytics  Track referred users, trading volume, and rewards across every referral link and date range. See how your audience grows, compare the performance of every link, and understand which traders, assets, and periods contribute to your rewards. Open Referrals and select Analytics to explore the complete picture or narrow it to the link and date range you care about. Track performance over time The summary and chart track referred users, eligible trading volume, and rewards across the same selected period. This makes it easy to see how changes in trading activity affect what you earn. View all links for your complete referral performance, or select one link to focus the chart on a specific audience or campaign.       Compare referral links Every link uses your referral ID, but its name keeps the source recognizable. You might create one link for a community, another for a social profile, and another for a specific campaign. Open All Referral Links to compare referred users, volume, and lifetime fees by link.       This lets you compare distribution channels without creating separate referral accounts. Rename or stop sharing a link when a campaign ends; its historical performance remains available for comparison. Review referred users The Referred Users view connects each referred account to the link they used. It shows when the relationship began, the trader's attributed activity, and the rewards their eligible fees produced.       Use it to understand whether a link attracted one highly active trader or a larger group of occasional traders without losing the link-level view. Trace rewards and conversions Open the Reward Ledger when you want the records behind an analytics total. Each entry identifies the referral link, eligible fee event, original reward asset, amount, and status. Conversion history connects the asset originally earned to the payout asset you selected. Together, these records let you move from a performance trend to the exact rewards behind it without maintaining a separate spreadsheet. See Referral Rewards to understand how each reward is calculated, collected, and converted. Related Topics  Overview  Invite friends to Polyester, earn a share of their trading fees, and track every referral from one dashboard. It shows your current account equity, Funding and Trading balances, asset allocation, open orders, and recent transactions.       Dashboard at a glance Total equity Total Equity estimates the current value of the assets in your Funding and Trading Accounts. It can change when asset prices move, even when you have not deposited, withdrawn, or traded. Funding and Trading The Dashboard shows how much value is held in each part of your account: Funding Account  holds assets available for deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers. Unified Trading Account  holds assets available for trading, lending, borrowing, and margin. Open Funding Account or Trading Account when you need the complete balance details. Assets The Assets view combines your Funding and Trading balances by asset. It shows the quantity you hold, its estimated value, and its share of your account equity. The combined balance is not always the amount available for a new action. Open orders, withdrawals, and transfers can reserve part of a Trading balance. Open orders Open Orders shows orders that are still working or partially filled. Open Orders or Manage Orders to change or cancel an order and see its complete fill history. Recent transactions Recent Transactions shows your latest deposits, withdrawals, and transfers with their current status. Select a transaction when you want to see its complete progress and identifying details. Open Ledger for the complete balance history. Quick actions Use Deposit, Withdraw, or Transfer to start moving an asset. These actions open the relevant page with your account context ready, but nothing moves until you review and submit the request.  Hide balances before sharing your screen Use the amount-visibility control to hide account values in shared spaces. This changes only what is displayed; it does not change your balances. Related Topics  Sign-In & Ownership  Understand how your wallet, Google account, or email connects you to your Polyester account. Overview  See every balance change in your account and connect it to the trade, transfer, or fee that created it. The method you choose becomes the owner credential that brings you back to the same Polyester account. Every Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own Safe smart account  on Polyester Chain . Your owner credential authorizes that account; your Safe holds the account identity and on-chain activity. Choose your sign-in method        Non-custodial wallet Google Email  Connect MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, WalletConnect, or another supported wallet. Your wallet signs a message to prove ownership without sharing its private key or paying gas. The wallet provider remains responsible for its backup and recovery. Returning with the same wallet address reconnects you to the same owner path.Google creates a Turnkey-backed embedded owner wallet  connected to your Google identity. Sign in with the same Google account whenever you return.Email creates a Turnkey-backed embedded owner wallet connected to your email address. A verification code proves access to that mailbox during sign-in.  Use the same identity when you return A different wallet address, Google account, or email address can open a different Polyester account. If your expected balances are missing, sign out and use the identity that originally created the account before depositing or trading. Your owner credential and smart account Your owner credential approves account access and protected actions. It is always a non-custodial wallet, whether you connect an existing wallet or create an embedded owner wallet with Google or email. Your Safe smart account is the Polyester account that appears on Polyester Chain. It has its own address and does not have one account-wide private key to export. The owner credential signs for it. Signing in is free. The Safe is deployed automatically with your first eligible on-chain action, such as your first deposit, if it has not already been deployed. Sessions and MFA After sign-in, the browser keeps a Polyester session so you can use your account without signing another wallet message on every page. Sensitive actions can still ask for MFA  or a fresh verification. Signing out ends the Polyester session in that browser. It does not sign you out of your wallet, Google account, or email provider. Export an embedded owner wallet If you use Google or email, you can export the embedded owner's seed phrase or private key from the Security page. Polyester shows it only when you request an export and is never notified of the exported value.              Keep exported private keys safe An exported seed phrase or private key can control your account. Store it securely and never send it to support, paste it into a chat, or save it in an unprotected file. External wallets use their own provider's export and recovery tools. Recover access For a connected wallet, use the wallet provider's recovery process. For Google, recover the Google account connected to your embedded owner wallet. For email, recover access through your email provider. If an MFA method is unavailable, use another enrolled method or an unused recovery code. Polyester support never needs your seed phrase, private key, email verification code, MFA code, recovery code, or API private key. Related Topics  MFA & Recovery  Add a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes available if you lose a method. Sessions & Alerts  Manage account sessions, understand security alerts, and respond to unfamiliar activity. Address Book & Whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. API Keys  Create API keys, choose what they can access, and keep their private signing keys safe. You can use a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes as a backup. Open Security to see your methods, add another one, or replace a method you no longer use. Choose an MFA method       Passkey Authenticator app  A passkey uses Face ID, Touch ID, a device PIN, or a compatible hardware security key. It is quick to use and resistant to phishing. Check whether your passkey syncs across trusted devices or stays only on the device where you created it.      An authenticator app generates a new six-digit code at regular intervals. Scan the setup QR code once, then enter the current code to finish enrollment. Protect the setup QR code and secret. Anyone who copies either can generate valid codes.       Set up MFA  1 Open Security Go to Security and find Multi-Factor Authentication. 2 Add your first method Choose a passkey or authenticator app and complete the device or code prompt.       3 Name the method Use a label that helps you recognize the device or authenticator without including a secret. 4 Save your recovery codes Store the codes somewhere protected and separate from your primary device. 5 Add a backup method Enroll another method so one lost device does not lock you out of protected actions. Recovery codes Recovery codes let you complete an MFA challenge when your usual method is unavailable. Each code works once. Keep them out of email, chat, screenshots, support tickets, source code, and browser autofill. Remove a code from your saved set after using it. Regenerating codes replaces the entire previous set.  New recovery codes replace the old set Do not close the new-code window until the replacement codes are stored safely. Every code from the previous set stops working after regeneration. Manage your methods The Security page shows when each method was added and last used. Rename a method when a clearer label would help, or remove a method you no longer control. You cannot remove your final MFA method. Add and test its replacement first, then remove the old method. When Polyester asks for MFA Polyester automatically requests MFA when an action needs more protection. Some actions accept a recent MFA check, while higher-risk changes ask for a fresh verification tied to that request. Examples include changing security settings, managing API keys , changing whitelists, exporting an embedded owner wallet , or moving funds under an MFA requirement. If verification fails Try another enrolled method if one is available. For authenticator codes, check that your device time is correct and enter the newest code. Use one unused recovery code when your regular methods are unavailable. If the prompt is unfamiliar, stop and review Sessions & Alerts. Polyester support never needs your authenticator secret, current code, passkey credential, or recovery code. Related Topics  Sign-In & Ownership  Understand how your wallet, Google account, or email connects you to your Polyester account. Sessions & Alerts  Manage account sessions, understand security alerts, and respond to unfamiliar activity. Address Book & Whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. API Keys  Create API keys, choose what they can access, and keep their private signing keys safe. Security alerts help you spot important account changes and activity that may need your attention. Your sessions A signed-in session lets that browser use your account until you sign out or the session ends. Polyester can still ask for MFA  before a sensitive action. Signing out ends the session on the browser you are using. If another device is lost or unfamiliar, secure the wallet, Google account, or email identity that owns your Polyester account, then end any sessions available from Security. API keys  are separate from browser sessions. Signing out does not disable them. Security alerts An alert tells you that something important happened, such as a new API key, MFA change, whitelist update, order, or transfer. Open the related account page for the complete details behind the alert. Device, IP address, and location descriptions can be approximate. Focus on the account, action, time, and related identifier when deciding whether the activity belongs to you. For unfamiliar activity, check the matching area: API Keys for key creation, permission changes, and recent use. Security for MFA methods and recovery-code changes. Address Book for destinations and whitelist changes. Orders and Trades for trading activity. Transfers and Ledger for deposits, withdrawals, and internal movement. If your account may be compromised  1 Secure your sign-in identity Use your wallet, Google, or email provider's official recovery tools. Change or strengthen access there if the owner identity may be exposed. 2 End unfamiliar access Sign out on devices you control and end unfamiliar sessions shown in Security. 3 Revoke exposed credentials Disable unfamiliar API keys, remove unknown Subaccount  members, and reduce permissions you did not approve. 4 Check security and balances Review MFA methods, recovery codes, whitelists, open orders, balances, and pending transfers. Avoid sending funds to a destination you have not independently verified. 5 Save useful evidence and contact support Keep event times, IDs, and screenshots that do not expose secrets. Send them through Support after immediate access risks are contained. Recover access Recover a connected wallet through its wallet provider. Recover Google or email access through the appropriate provider. Use another enrolled MFA method or an unused recovery code when one factor is unavailable. Revoke and replace an API key if its private key is lost or exposed.  Never send secrets as evidence Polyester support never needs your seed phrase, private key, email verification code, MFA code, recovery code, embedded-wallet export, or API private key. Related Topics  Sign-In & Ownership  Understand how your wallet, Google account, or email connects you to your Polyester account. MFA & Recovery  Add a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes available if you lose a method. Address Book & Whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. API Keys  Create API keys, choose what they can access, and keep their private signing keys safe. Whitelists add another layer of protection by limiting where your account can send funds. Each Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own Address Book and whitelist settings. Save external and internal destinations       External Internal  Save a wallet or contract address on a supported external chain. Each entry includes its chain, complete address, label, and any optional notes or tags you add. An Ethereum address and a Solana address are different destinations, even when they belong to the same person.      Save another Polyester account for transfers inside Polyester. The entry connects a friendly label to the account identity used by the transfer page.       Favorites, recent destinations, tags, and chain filters help you find an entry. They do not change its security permissions. Add a destination  1 Choose the account Select the Master Account or Subaccount that should save the entry. 2 Choose External or Internal External is for an address on another chain. Internal is for another Polyester account. 3 Enter and verify the destination For an external entry, choose the chain and paste the complete address. For an internal entry, select the intended Polyester account. Compare it with a trusted source before continuing.             4 Name and save it Add a clear label and optional tags or notes, then save the entry.  Check the complete destination Lookalike addresses can share the same beginning and ending characters. Compare the full address and chain before saving, whitelisting, or sending funds. How whitelists protect your account Open Withdraw. Polyester checks the External Withdrawal Whitelist first. If the destination is allowed, or the whitelist is off, MFA  is next when it is enrolled. Then you approve in the wallet.   Whitelist On Off     Whitelist is on. Entering an address or picking one from the address book that is not
		whitelisted blocks the withdrawal. A whitelisted address book entry continues to MFA, then
		wallet, then proceeds.           Withdraw  Enter address  0x8A7F…a3C2B Address book  0x3E9B…F4Daa  Whitelisted destinationAddress book  0x1A2C…f5a2c  Not whitelisted  MFA Wallet                    Whitelist on. Only an approved address book entry can continue. Polyester provides two separate controls: External Withdrawal Whitelist limits withdrawals to approved external addresses. Internal Transfer Whitelist limits internal transfers to approved Polyester accounts. Saving an Address Book entry  does not automatically whitelist it. Add it to the appropriate whitelist when you want it approved for a protected movement. Whitelist settings apply only to the selected Master Account or Subaccount. Turn them on separately for every account you want protected. Change a whitelist Open Security or the relevant Address Book destination. Choose the account and the External or Internal whitelist. Add or remove the intended destination, or turn the requirement on or off. Complete the requested MFA, GuardSigner , and wallet approval. Wait for the destination's whitelist status to update before moving funds. Adding or removing an approved destination and turning a whitelist off are sensitive actions. Polyester uses fresh verification and GuardSigner to protect them.       GuardSigner GuardSigner is an additional security signer for protected Funding Account  changes. It is not a login method or an MFA replacement. Security shows whether GuardSigner is ready. Complete its setup or initialization before changing a protected whitelist. If Security reports a recovery problem, stop the whitelist change and use the recovery instructions shown there.               Never export or share GuardSigner private material. Use a saved destination When you withdraw or transfer, select a saved entry and check the asset, chain, complete destination, and whitelist status shown in the review. A saved label makes the destination easier to recognize, but the complete address or account remains the destination that receives the funds. You choose whether the key can view balances, trade, or move funds, and you can disable or revoke it at any time. Open API Keys to create a key and manage its access.       For request signing, authentication headers, replay protection, and implementation examples, use Ed25519 API Keys in the Developer Docs. How an API key works Polyester API keys use an Ed25519 keypair: The private key stays with your software and signs each request. The public key lets Polyester verify the signature. The Key ID tells Polyester which public key and permissions apply. The account limits the key to one Master Account or Subaccount. The permissions control which actions the key can perform. Polyester never stores or redisplays the private key.  Keep the private key secret Store it in a secret manager. Never paste it into support, chat, source code, screenshots, logs, analytics, or an untrusted browser form. Revoke the key immediately if it may have been exposed. Choose how to create the key       Generate in browser Bring your own key  Your browser creates the public and private key. Save the private key securely before completing creation; it is shown only once.Create the Ed25519 keypair in your own security system and provide only the public key to Polyester. The private key never leaves your system. Create an API key  1 Choose the account Select the Master Account or Subaccount the software should use. 2 Name the key Use a label that identifies the application and environment, such as 'Reporting production' or 'Market maker  testnet'. 3 Create or provide the keypair Generate it in the browser or enter a public key you created elsewhere. Save the private key before continuing.       4 Choose its access Enable only the data and actions the application needs. Add an expiry and IP whitelist when appropriate. 5 Save the Key ID Store the Key ID with the private key and application configuration, then test one low-risk request. Choose permissions and limits Spot Trading can allow market data access, order access, or order placement for all or selected markets. Balances lets the key view private account balances. Outgoing Internal Transfers can allow internal transfer access and an optional daily limit. External Withdrawals can allow withdrawal access and an optional daily limit. IP whitelist limits requests to specified IP addresses or network ranges. The most restrictive account, Subaccount, API-key, whitelist, and endpoint rule always applies.        API keys do not open MFA prompts A software request cannot complete an interactive MFA  challenge. Protect write access with a narrow account, limited permissions, an expiry, a stable IP whitelist when available, and a separate key for each application. Manage and replace keys The API Keys page shows each key's account, permissions, creation time, last use, status, and expiry. Disable pauses a key and can be reversed. Revoke permanently stops the key. Replace a key by creating and testing a new one before revoking the old one. If a key is no longer needed or its private key may be exposed, revoke it instead of leaving it active. Developer guides Use the Developer Docs for request signing and API integration: Ed25519 API Keys API Key IP Allowlists API Key Replay Policy REST Guide Related Topics  Sign-In & Ownership  Understand how your wallet, Google account, or email connects you to your Polyester account. MFA & Recovery  Add a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes available if you lose a method. Sessions & Alerts  Manage account sessions, understand security alerts, and respond to unfamiliar activity. Address Book & Whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. It includes deposits, withdrawals, transfers, trades, fees, rebates, and amounts reserved or released by active requests. Ledger activity is private to your account. Public explorers show on-chain transactions, while the Ledger shows how those events affected your Polyester balance.       Find the activity you need Use All for the complete history, Transfers for deposits, withdrawals, and internal movement, or Trades for executions, fees, and rebates. Search by asset, Flow ID, source, destination, or activity type. Turn on Group transactions to combine entries created by the same action. Turn it off when you want to see every debit, credit, fee, or rebate separately. What each entry shows Field What it tells you Time When the balance change was recordedType The action, such as Deposit, Withdraw, Transfer, Buy, Sell, Fee, or RebateAmount How much of the asset was added or removedAsset The balance that changedBalance After Your balance immediately after that entrySource and Destination Where the value came from and where it wentFlow ID The deposit, withdrawal, or transfer connected to the entry    Select an entry with a Flow ID to open the related transaction and see its complete progress. Why one action can create several entries One trade or transfer can affect more than one balance: A spot buy removes the quote asset , adds the base asset , and records the fee or rebate. A spot sell removes the base asset, adds the quote asset, and records the fee or rebate. A Funding-to-Trading transfer removes the amount from Funding and adds it to Trading. An internal transfer records the amount leaving one account and entering another. A withdrawal can reserve the amount before the final debit is completed. Grouped transactions keep those connected entries together. Available and reserved balances An open order, transfer, or withdrawal can reserve part of your Trading balance. The reserved amount still belongs to your account, but it is not available for another action. When the request completes, Polyester uses the required amount. When it is canceled or fails, Polyester releases the unused amount. A partially filled order keeps its completed trades and releases only the unused remainder.  Several requests can reserve one asset Your available balance can be lower because of multiple open orders, transfers, or withdrawals. Check all active activity before assigning the difference to one order. Ledger and statements The Ledger shows individual balance changes. Account Statements groups those records into a report for a selected period. Related Topics  Account Statements  Create a report of your balances, trades, fees, and account activity for a selected period. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Account /Ledger /Account Statements   Account Statements  08/10    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    Account Statements turn your account activity into a downloadable report for a selected period. Use them for recordkeeping, accounting, or reviewing how your balances changed. Statements are created separately for each Master Account  or Subaccount , so the report matches the account you selected. Create a statement  1 Choose the account Select the Master Account or Subaccount you want included. 2 Choose the reporting period Set the start date, end date, and timezone for the report. 3 Choose the format Select the available PDF or data export based on how you plan to use the statement. 4 Generate and download Generate the statement, then save the finished file to a protected location. What a statement includes Your statement identifies the account, reporting period, timezone, and generation time. It can include: opening and closing balances; deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers; orders, fills, fees, and rebates; the asset and quantity for each entry; and ledger, flow, order, fill, or transaction references. The exact sections depend on the activity in the selected account and period. Match a statement to your account Use the opening and closing balances to understand the period as a whole. For more detail, match statement rows to your Ledger, orders, trades, or transaction history using their IDs and timestamps.  A statement covers a fixed period A downloaded statement does not update after it is generated. Use your current Dashboard and account pages for live balances and active orders. Protect downloaded statements Statements can contain account IDs, smart account  addresses, balances, trading history, and transfer details. Store them in an encrypted or access-controlled location. Share only the account, period, and fields the recipient needs. Check the recipient and delivery method before sending a file. Remove unrelated personal information before sharing when appropriate. Never add private keys, MFA  codes, recovery codes, or API private keys to an exported report. Related Topics  Overview  See every balance change in your account and connect it to the trade, transfer, or fee that created it. Interactive     Enable audio Turn Enable audio off when you want Polyester to stay silent. Your individual volume choices remain saved for the next time you turn audio on. Set the overall volume Master volume controls the overall level for every Polyester sound. Start here, then fine-tune the categories underneath it. Adjust each category Notifications controls sounds for account and product alerts. UI sounds controls feedback from buttons and other interface actions. Voice alerts controls supported spoken updates. Use the play button beside a category to hear its current level. Choose a sound pack Sound packs change the style of supported Polyester sounds without changing which alerts you receive. Choose a pack and use the preview before keeping it. If nothing plays, check Enable audio, Master volume, the category level, your device output, and whether the browser tab is muted. Choose the updates you care about and where you want to receive them. Open Notifications to review alerts. Open Notification Settings to manage your choices.       Choose where notifications appear In-app notifications appear while you are using Polyester. Browser notifications can appear outside the active Polyester tab. Push notifications appear on supported devices. Browser and push notifications also need permission from your browser or device. Choose which updates you receive Turn notification groups on or off for: orders and trades; deposits and withdrawals; transfers; security activity; and platform updates. Your security settings and activity records remain available even when a notification group is turned off. Choose how alerts look and sound Set where alerts appear on screen, whether Polyester shows an unread badge, how long temporary alerts remain visible, and whether they play a sound.       Sound volume is controlled separately under Sounds. If an alert does not arrive Check that the notification group and delivery channel are on. For browser or push alerts, also check the browser permission, device notification settings, and focus or do-not-disturb mode. Each Subaccount has its own deposit addresses, balances, orders, members, permissions, and account history, so activity in one stays separate from the others. Open Subaccounts to create a new Subaccount or switch between the accounts you can access.       What each Subaccount keeps separate Every Subaccount has its own: Funding and Trading balances; orders and fills; members and roles; permissions; API keys ; and activity and financial records. Someone who can use one Subaccount does not automatically gain access to your Master Account or another Subaccount. When to create a Subaccount Create a Subaccount when you want a clear boundary between different types of activity. For example, you can keep a trading strategy separate, give a team access to only the assets they manage, or use a dedicated account for an automated trading system. Use as many Subaccounts as you need, but give each one a clear purpose. Subaccounts sit directly beneath the Master Account and cannot contain other Subaccounts. Move assets between accounts Balances do not move between your Master Account and Subaccounts automatically. Use an Internal Transfer to move available assets between your accounts without withdrawing them from Polyester. Each account still keeps its own Funding and Trading balances after the transfer. Control who can do what A member's role defines their general responsibility, while the Subaccount's permissions define what is available inside that account. API keys use the same access controls and are scoped to the account where you create them. See Members & Roles for people, Permissions & Policies for account limits, and API Keys for programmatic access.  One Master Account, separate account spaces Your Master Account manages the Subaccounts beneath it, but each Subaccount keeps its balances, trading activity, and access separate. Related Topics  Manage Subaccounts  Create, switch, fund, freeze, leave, or delete a Subaccount. Members & Roles  Invite people to a Subaccount and choose what each role can do. Permissions & Policies  Choose which trading, balance, transfer, and withdrawal actions a Subaccount supports. Audit Logs  See membership, permission, API-key, and account-setting changes for a Subaccount.
