From one place, you can create accounts, switch between them, move assets, manage access, and update each account's status.       Pending invitations appear on the same page. Accept or decline them before they become Subaccounts you can use. Create a Subaccount  1 Open Subaccounts Open the Subaccounts page from your Master Account  and select Create Subaccount. 2 Choose a label Enter a Label that describes the account's purpose, such as a strategy, team, or automated workload.       3 Create it Select Create Subaccount. Polyester gives the new account its own account ID and smart account  address. 4 Set it up Add permissions, members, API keys , and assets based on how you plan to use the account. You can also save the Subaccount to your Address Book for faster internal transfers, or select Skip for now.       Switch between accounts Select Switch to make a Subaccount your active account. Polyester then shows that account's balances, orders, settings, and available actions across the product. The account selector always shows which account you are currently using.       Add or move assets Use Internal Transfers to move assets between your Master Account and Subaccounts or between two Subaccounts. You can also deposit directly into a Subaccount when it is available as the destination on the Deposit page. Freeze, leave, or delete a Subaccount An Owner can freeze a Subaccount to stop new activity and reactivate it later. A member can leave a shared Subaccount when they no longer need access. An Owner can delete a Subaccount that is no longer needed. Before deleting an account, move its available balances and finish managing any open orders. Its completed trading, transfer, and account history remains available after deletion.  Leaving and deleting are different Leaving removes your access to someone else's Subaccount. Deleting retires a Subaccount you own. Related Topics  Overview  Use Subaccounts to separate balances, trading, people, and access under one Master Account. Members & Roles  Invite people to a Subaccount and choose what each role can do. Permissions & Policies  Choose which trading, balance, transfer, and withdrawal actions a Subaccount supports. Audit Logs  See membership, permission, API-key, and account-setting changes for a Subaccount. Each person receives a role that applies only to that Subaccount. Open the Subaccount and select Members to invite someone, update their role, or remove their access. Invite a member  1 Choose Invite Member Open the Subaccount's Members tab and select Invite Member. 2 Find the person Search by username, wallet address, or account ID and select the correct Polyester account.       3 Choose a role Give the person the role that matches what they need to do.       4 Send the invitation Select Invite member. Polyester may ask you to verify with your passkey before sending the invitation. The invitation remains pending until the person accepts it. Access begins after acceptance.       Choose the right role Role Best for Access Owner The person responsible for the Subaccount Full account and access managementAdmin Someone who manages day-to-day account setup Trading, transfers, members, API keys , and most settingsTreasury Someone responsible for assets Balances, internal transfers, and withdrawalsTrader Someone responsible for trading Balances and spot tradingViewer Someone who only needs visibility Read-only account access    The Subaccount's permissions can narrow what any role is allowed to do. See Permissions & Policies for those account-wide controls. Require MFA for members The Owner can turn on Require MFA  for the Subaccount. Members who have not set up MFA are prompted to add it before using protected account actions. This setting applies to members of the selected Subaccount. Each person manages their own MFA from their Polyester account. Update or remove access Change a member's role when their responsibilities change, or remove them when they no longer need the Subaccount. Removing a member ends their access but does not change completed trades or transfers.  API keys are managed separately A member role does not create or control an API key. Manage programmatic access from the shared API Keys page. Related Topics  Overview  Use Subaccounts to separate balances, trading, people, and access under one Master Account. Manage Subaccounts  Create, switch, fund, freeze, leave, or delete a Subaccount. Permissions & Policies  Choose which trading, balance, transfer, and withdrawal actions a Subaccount supports. Audit Logs  See membership, permission, API-key, and account-setting changes for a Subaccount. They apply across the account and work together with member roles and API-key settings. Open a Subaccount and select Permissions to manage its trading, balance, transfer, withdrawal, and safety controls. How permissions work A member's role describes their general responsibility. The Subaccount policy is a shared ceiling. A role or API-key policy can narrow access further, but it cannot exceed the Subaccount policy. If no policy is attached, the role or API-key policy decides the available access. If a policy is attached with no actions enabled, all policy-controlled actions are denied. For example, a Trader can place orders only when both the Trader role and the Subaccount policy allow the market. Each action is independent. Enabling a trading, transfer, or management action does not automatically enable the related read action. What you can control Use the policy to choose: whether the account can view balances or trade; which spot markets it can use; the maximum size of one order; the maximum number of open orders; whether it can make internal transfers; whether it can make external withdrawals; whether it can manage address-book or whitelist settings; whether new trading activity is halted; and whether the policy is locked against changes. Trading halt rejects new orders and order or trigger changes that can resume trading. Existing orders and triggers can still be canceled or paused. Set the policy  1 Open Permissions Choose the Subaccount you want to manage and open its Permissions tab. 2 Choose the available actions Set the trading, balance, transfer, and withdrawal access that fits the account's purpose. 3 Add useful limits Choose the spot markets, per-order size, open-order limit, and trading-halt setting that should apply across the Subaccount. 4 Review and save Review the complete policy and save your changes. Polyester may ask for MFA  before applying a protected change. Permissions and whitelists Transfer permission allows a member or API key  to request a transfer. A whitelist separately controls which destinations are approved. Both checks must pass when the transfer route  requires a whitelisted destination. Manage destinations from Address Book & Whitelists. Lock the policy The Owner can lock a policy after it is configured. A locked policy continues to apply, but only the Owner can unlock it before making changes.  Roles and permissions have different jobs Roles describe what a person can manage. Permissions describe what the Subaccount allows. Both must allow an action before it is available. Related Topics  Overview  Use Subaccounts to separate balances, trading, people, and access under one Master Account. Manage Subaccounts  Create, switch, fund, freeze, leave, or delete a Subaccount. Members & Roles  Invite people to a Subaccount and choose what each role can do. Audit Logs  See membership, permission, API-key, and account-setting changes for a Subaccount. Whitelists add another layer of protection by limiting where your account can send funds. Each Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own Address Book and whitelist settings. Save external and internal destinations       External Internal  Save a wallet or contract address on a supported external chain. Each entry includes its chain, complete address, label, and any optional notes or tags you add. An Ethereum address and a Solana address are different destinations, even when they belong to the same person.      Save another Polyester account for transfers inside Polyester. The entry connects a friendly label to the account identity used by the transfer page.       Favorites, recent destinations, tags, and chain filters help you find an entry. They do not change its security permissions. Add a destination  1 Choose the account Select the Master Account or Subaccount that should save the entry. 2 Choose External or Internal External is for an address on another chain. Internal is for another Polyester account. 3 Enter and verify the destination For an external entry, choose the chain and paste the complete address. For an internal entry, select the intended Polyester account. Compare it with a trusted source before continuing.             4 Name and save it Add a clear label and optional tags or notes, then save the entry.  Check the complete destination Lookalike addresses can share the same beginning and ending characters. Compare the full address and chain before saving, whitelisting, or sending funds. How whitelists protect your account Open Withdraw. Polyester checks the External Withdrawal Whitelist first. If the destination is allowed, or the whitelist is off, MFA  is next when it is enrolled. Then you approve in the wallet.   Whitelist On Off     Whitelist is on. Entering an address or picking one from the address book that is not
		whitelisted blocks the withdrawal. A whitelisted address book entry continues to MFA, then
		wallet, then proceeds.           Withdraw  Enter address  0x8A7F…a3C2B Address book  0x3E9B…F4Daa  Whitelisted destinationAddress book  0x1A2C…f5a2c  Not whitelisted  MFA Wallet                    Whitelist on. Only an approved address book entry can continue. Polyester provides two separate controls: External Withdrawal Whitelist limits withdrawals to approved external addresses. Internal Transfer Whitelist limits internal transfers to approved Polyester accounts. Saving an Address Book entry  does not automatically whitelist it. Add it to the appropriate whitelist when you want it approved for a protected movement. Whitelist settings apply only to the selected Master Account or Subaccount. Turn them on separately for every account you want protected. Change a whitelist Open Security or the relevant Address Book destination. Choose the account and the External or Internal whitelist. Add or remove the intended destination, or turn the requirement on or off. Complete the requested MFA, GuardSigner , and wallet approval. Wait for the destination's whitelist status to update before moving funds. Adding or removing an approved destination and turning a whitelist off are sensitive actions. Polyester uses fresh verification and GuardSigner to protect them.       GuardSigner GuardSigner is an additional security signer for protected Funding Account  changes. It is not a login method or an MFA replacement. Security shows whether GuardSigner is ready. Complete its setup or initialization before changing a protected whitelist. If Security reports a recovery problem, stop the whitelist change and use the recovery instructions shown there.               Never export or share GuardSigner private material. Use a saved destination When you withdraw or transfer, select a saved entry and check the asset, chain, complete destination, and whitelist status shown in the review. A saved label makes the destination easier to recognize, but the complete address or account remains the destination that receives the funds. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Subaccounts /Audit Logs   Audit Logs  06/30    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    Audit Logs give you a clear history of access and setting changes for a Subaccount . Open the Subaccount and select Activity to see who made each change and when it happened. What appears in Activity Activity includes changes such as: creating, renaming, freezing, or deleting a Subaccount; sending or responding to member invitations; changing a member's role or access; creating, updating, or removing an API key ; updating or locking permissions; and changing the member MFA  requirement. Read an activity entry Each entry shows the time, the type of item that changed, the action, where the change came from, and the account that made it. When available, Polyester also shows the source IP address. The newest entries appear first. Select Load more to continue through earlier activity. Trading and balance history Activity focuses on access and account settings. Other records remain in the part of Polyester where they belong: Manage Orders shows orders and fills. Overview shows balance entries. Deposit, withdrawal, and transfer pages show the progress of fund movements. Polyester Scan  shows public Polyester Chain  activity.  A focused account history Audit Logs keep membership, permission, credential, and account-setting changes together without mixing them with trading or balance records. Related Topics  Overview  Use Subaccounts to separate balances, trading, people, and access under one Master Account. Manage Subaccounts  Create, switch, fund, freeze, leave, or delete a Subaccount. Members & Roles  Invite people to a Subaccount and choose what each role can do. Permissions & Policies  Choose which trading, balance, transfer, and withdrawal actions a Subaccount supports. You choose whether the key can view balances, trade, or move funds, and you can disable or revoke it at any time. Open API Keys to create a key and manage its access.       For request signing, authentication headers, replay protection, and implementation examples, use Ed25519 API Keys in the Developer Docs. How an API key works Polyester API keys use an Ed25519 keypair: The private key stays with your software and signs each request. The public key lets Polyester verify the signature. The Key ID tells Polyester which public key and permissions apply. The account limits the key to one Master Account or Subaccount. The permissions control which actions the key can perform. Polyester never stores or redisplays the private key.  Keep the private key secret Store it in a secret manager. Never paste it into support, chat, source code, screenshots, logs, analytics, or an untrusted browser form. Revoke the key immediately if it may have been exposed. Choose how to create the key       Generate in browser Bring your own key  Your browser creates the public and private key. Save the private key securely before completing creation; it is shown only once.Create the Ed25519 keypair in your own security system and provide only the public key to Polyester. The private key never leaves your system. Create an API key  1 Choose the account Select the Master Account or Subaccount the software should use. 2 Name the key Use a label that identifies the application and environment, such as 'Reporting production' or 'Market maker  testnet'. 3 Create or provide the keypair Generate it in the browser or enter a public key you created elsewhere. Save the private key before continuing.       4 Choose its access Enable only the data and actions the application needs. Add an expiry and IP whitelist when appropriate. 5 Save the Key ID Store the Key ID with the private key and application configuration, then test one low-risk request. Choose permissions and limits Spot Trading can allow market data access, order access, or order placement for all or selected markets. Balances lets the key view private account balances. Outgoing Internal Transfers can allow internal transfer access and an optional daily limit. External Withdrawals can allow withdrawal access and an optional daily limit. IP whitelist limits requests to specified IP addresses or network ranges. The most restrictive account, Subaccount, API-key, whitelist, and endpoint rule always applies.        API keys do not open MFA prompts A software request cannot complete an interactive MFA  challenge. Protect write access with a narrow account, limited permissions, an expiry, a stable IP whitelist when available, and a separate key for each application. Manage and replace keys The API Keys page shows each key's account, permissions, creation time, last use, status, and expiry. Disable pauses a key and can be reversed. Revoke permanently stops the key. Replace a key by creating and testing a new one before revoking the old one. If a key is no longer needed or its private key may be exposed, revoke it instead of leaving it active. Developer guides Use the Developer Docs for request signing and API integration: Ed25519 API Keys API Key IP Allowlists API Key Replay Policy REST Guide Related Topics  Sign-In & Ownership  Understand how your wallet, Google account, or email connects you to your Polyester account. MFA & Recovery  Add a passkey or authenticator app and keep recovery codes available if you lose a method. Sessions & Alerts  Manage account sessions, understand security alerts, and respond to unfamiliar activity. Address Book & Whitelists  Save trusted destinations and control where withdrawals and internal transfers can be sent. When you submit an order, PolyEngine checks that it can be placed, protects the balance it may use, matches it against the order book, and records every completed trade in your account.  PolyEngine works off-chain, so your orders do not need to wait for a Polyester Chain  block. Your balances, orders, fills, and trading activity also remain private to your account. PolyEngine is built for high-performance, institutional-grade trading. It supports significant order throughput with end-to-end latency below one millisecond, making it suitable for high-frequency trading, market making, API-driven strategies, and fast interactive trading. How your order moves You submit an order. Your instruction includes the account, market, side, order type, amount, and any price or execution settings. Admission checks the order. PolyEngine checks your permissions, the market rules, and your available Trading balance. It reserves the amount the order may spend. Matching finds eligible orders. Buy and sell orders meet on the market's order book using price and time priority. Settlement records each fill. PolyEngine updates the base asset , quote asset , fee or rebate, and reserved balance for both sides of the trade. Your account updates. Open Orders, Order History, Trades, Trading balances, and Ledger entries reflect the result. An order may move through several of these stages almost instantly. Its Order ID connects the instruction, fills, and financial records. Dedicated order books Every trading pair has its own order book. PolyEngine matches buyers and sellers directly; it does not use an AMM or pull assets from a shared liquidity pool. Assets deposited from different supported chains trade through their unified asset . For example, USDT deposited through two supported chains enters the same USDT market instead of creating a separate order book for each chain. Public markets, private accounts The Order Book and Market Trades show the market's combined activity. They do not show who owns an order, a user's balance, or the fee attached to a private fill. Your open orders, order history, fills, fees, rebates, reservations, and Trading balances are available only inside your account. Funds entering or leaving your Trading Account can create visible on-chain activity, but your trading activity inside PolyEngine remains private. Explore each stage Admission explains the checks that happen before your order can work. Matching explains order-book priority, maker  and taker  fills, partial fills, and self-trade prevention. Settlement explains how fills, fees, rebates, and reservations update your account.  Accepted does not mean filled An accepted order has passed PolyEngine's initial checks. It may fill immediately, rest on the order book, fill in parts, or end without a fill based on your order settings and available liquidity. Related Topics  Admission  See how PolyEngine checks your order and protects the balance it may use. Matching  See how your eligible order receives priority and becomes one or more fills. Settlement  See how each fill updates your assets, fees, rebates, and reserved balance. PolyEngine  reviews your instruction and account together before the order can enter the market. If the order is accepted, PolyEngine gives it an Order ID and reserves the balance it may spend. If it is not accepted, the order does not begin working and Polyester shows the reason.  What Admission checks PolyEngine checks: that your active account can trade the selected pair; that the market and order type are available; that the price and amount follow the market's minimums and increments; that time in force, post-only , and self-trade prevention work with the order; that the order stays within its price or slippage protection; which asset will pay the trading fee; and that your Trading Account has enough available balance. The current market rules always apply. A price or amount copied from an older order may no longer fit the pair's current minimums or increments. How your balance is protected Admission reserves only the balance the order may need. A sell order reserves the base asset  you want to sell. A buy order reserves the quote asset  required for the purchase and any applicable fee protection. The reservation is not a fee or a second charge. It simply prevents another order, transfer, or withdrawal from spending the same balance while your order is active. As your order progresses: completed fills use the amount required for the trade; an unfilled portion keeps the balance it still needs reserved; and cancellation or completion releases any amount the order no longer needs. See Trading Account for more about available and reserved balances. Market orders still have price protection A market order tries to trade immediately, but it does not accept any price. PolyEngine uses the pair's active price-protection settings, so the order can fill completely, fill partly, or end without a fill when eligible liquidity is unavailable within that range. The selected market state also matters. A market can allow normal trading, accept only post-only orders, allow cancellations only, or stop accepting new orders. What acceptance means Acceptance means your order passed Admission and received an Order ID. The order can then move to Matching. It does not guarantee that the order will fill. The result still depends on its price, time in force, available liquidity, and other order settings.  One balance cannot fund two active actions Your available balance excludes amounts already reserved by open orders and other pending activity. This keeps every accepted order fully backed by the balance it may spend. Related Topics  Overview  See how PolyEngine checks, matches, and settles your spot orders. Matching  See how your eligible order receives priority and becomes one or more fills. Settlement  See how each fill updates your assets, fees, rebates, and reserved balance. It begins after Admission accepts your order and reserves the balance it may use. Each trading pair has its own order book. Deposits from different supported chains trade through the same unified asset , so the source chain does not create a separate market. Price comes first, then time PolyEngine  gives priority in two steps: Best price first. Buyers receive the lowest eligible sell price, while sellers receive the highest eligible buy price. Earlier order first. When several orders share the same price, the order that arrived earlier receives priority. Your limit price is the worst price you accept, not necessarily the price you receive. A buy can fill at its limit price or lower, and a sell can fill at its limit price or higher. Maker and taker fills The order already resting on the book is the maker . The incoming order that trades against it is the taker . The applicable maker fee, maker rebate, or taker fee is calculated for each fill. Maker or taker status belongs to the fill, not permanently to the order. A limit order can take liquidity immediately and later provide liquidity with its remaining amount. Post-only  prevents that mixed result by rejecting a limit order that would immediately trade as a taker. See Trading Fees for fee and rebate rates. Partial fills and remaining amounts One order can trade against several orders or prices. Each match creates a separate fill, and Polyester combines those fills to show your total filled amount and average execution price. What happens to the unfilled amount depends on the instruction: Instruction What happens to the unfilled amount Good Til Canceled (GTC) It remains on the order book until it fills or you cancel it.Immediate Or Cancel (IOC) It is canceled after all immediately available matches complete.Fill Or Kill (FOK) The entire order fills immediately or no part of it fills.Market It trades immediately within price protection, then cancels any remainder.    FOK checks the eligible liquidity across the complete order book, not only the rows currently visible in the Order Book widget. Prevent self-trading Self-trade prevention applies when two orders from the same Polyester Account ID would otherwise match: Expire Maker cancels the resting order. Expire Taker cancels the incoming order. Expire Both cancels both orders. When you do not choose a mode, Polyester uses Expire Maker. Different Subaccounts  have different account IDs, so orders from two Subaccounts can match normally even when they belong to the same Master Account . Canceling a working order A working order remains active if you close your browser, sign out, or lose your connection. It continues following its price, priority, and time-in-force instructions until it fills, is canceled, or otherwise ends. A fill can complete while your cancellation is being processed. Any completed fill remains final, while only the amount still open is canceled.  Every fill moves to Settlement Matching creates the price, amount, maker and taker roles, and order references for each fill. Settlement then applies the asset, fee, rebate, and balance changes to your account. Related Topics  Overview  See how PolyEngine checks, matches, and settles your spot orders. Admission  See how PolyEngine checks your order and protects the balance it may use. Settlement  See how each fill updates your assets, fees, rebates, and reserved balance. It records the assets exchanged, your fee or rebate, and the amount used or released from your order's reservation. Settlement uses Polyester's private ledger. Your spot fill does not require a separate Polyester Chain  transaction, and its account-level details remain private. What changes after a fill Every trading pair contains a base asset  and a quote asset . Settlement applies the following movement: Your side You spend You receive Buy Quote asset Base assetSell Base asset Quote asset    Each fill is settled on its own. If your order fills in several parts, each fill has its own price, amount, maker  or taker  role, and fee result. Your order and balance views then combine those fills into the complete result. How trading fees are paid Seller fees come from the quote asset received by the trade. When the pair and your account settings allow it, a buyer can choose between: Quote, which pays the fee from the quote asset; or Received, which deducts the fee from the base asset received. Your fee source does not change the execution price or whether the fill is maker or taker. Maker rebates are credited as part of the same fill. See Trading Fees for the current rates, VIP tiers, fee-source options, and maker rebates. What happens to reserved balance Admission reserves the amount your order may spend. Settlement turns the required part of that reservation into the completed trade: a full fill uses the required amount and releases any extra protection; a partial fill uses the completed portion and keeps the remaining order amount reserved; canceling after a partial fill releases only the unused remainder; and an order with no fills releases its unused reservation when it ends. The reservation itself is never an additional fee.  Canceling does not reverse a completed fill Cancellation applies only to the amount that remains open. Assets, fees, and rebates from completed fills stay in your account. Where you see the result Open Order Details to see the instruction and every fill. The Trades view shows each execution, while Transfers and your Ledger show the connected asset, fee, rebate, and reservation entries. Market Trades shows that an execution occurred for the pair, but it does not reveal your account, balance, fee source, or private settlement details. Related Topics  Overview  See how PolyEngine checks, matches, and settles your spot orders. Admission  See how PolyEngine checks your order and protects the balance it may use. Matching  See how your eligible order receives priority and becomes one or more fills. It powers deposits and withdrawals by validating each transfer, representing the asset on Polyester Chain, and crediting the matching unified balance to your account. Zipper is designed to support native assets from virtually any blockchain architecture. The resulting assets are issued on Polyester Chain for use across the Polyester Exchange, lending markets, and the broader Polyester ecosystem. This lets you deposit through one supported chain and later withdraw through another compatible chain without managing wrapped tokens or an external bridge yourself. How deposits work You send a supported asset to the deposit address assigned to your account for the selected chain. Zipper waits for the external transfer to reach the required confirmations. Zipper validators independently confirm the chain, asset, amount, and receiving account through a three-quarter quorum. Polyester creates the route-specific Zipped Asset , or zAsset, on Polyester Chain. Your account receives the matching Unified Asset , or uAsset, in Funding or Trading based on your deposit settings. Each Master Account  and Subaccount  has its own deposit addresses, so Zipper can credit the correct account automatically. How withdrawals work You choose a Unified Asset, destination chain, amount, and address. Zipper selects the exact supported route  and reserves the amount and route fee. Validators approve the request, and the Cubist-protected vault  prepares the external transaction. Polyester burns the route-specific Zipped Asset before the matching external backing can leave the vault. The custody system releases the external asset and Zipper follows the transfer through destination finality . You can withdraw an available balance from Funding or Trading through the supported withdrawal flow . Zipped Assets and Unified Assets A Zipped Asset identifies one exact source chain and asset on Polyester Chain. Bitcoin becomes Zipped Bitcoin, or zBTC. USDT deposited from Ethereum, Solana, and Base creates three separate Polyester Chain ERC-20 Zipped Assets, each backed one-to-one by the exact USDT held on its originating chain. A Unified Asset brings compatible Zipped Assets together as one account-facing balance. This is the asset you see in Funding, transfer to Trading, and use across Polyester. Only routes that Polyester explicitly connects share a Unified Asset. Matching ticker symbols alone do not make two assets equivalent. Routes, fees, and availability Every route defines its chain, asset contract, minimum amount, confirmation requirement, custody path, and fee. The configured route fee is an absolute amount in the asset being deposited or withdrawn, not a percentage. The same base route fee applies to deposits and withdrawals on that route. Fees are calculated to cover the source chain's gas costs while keeping the amount charged to you as low as possible. They can change as chain costs and asset values change. Availability can differ by chain because every supported asset and source chain has its own external supply. Explore Zipper Asset Lifecycle explains the complete deposit and withdrawal journey. Vaults explains deposit addresses, external custody, source-chain supply, and withdrawal liquidity. Security explains validator quorum, Blockaid and OFAC screening, Cubist TEE vaults, finality, and duplicate prevention.  The complete route defines the asset Zipper uses the selected chain and exact asset contract, not only the ticker symbol. Native, wrapped, and externally bridged versions remain separate unless Polyester explicitly supports and maps them. Related Topics  Asset Lifecycle  Follow your asset from an external deposit to a Polyester balance and back to an external chain. Vaults  See how Zipper deposit addresses, custody vaults, and route inventory support deposits and withdrawals. Security  See how Zipper protects deposits, withdrawals, custody, and Zipped Asset supply. It links the external transaction, the request on Polyester Chain , and the final change to your account balance. Deposit lifecycle Open the Deposit page and choose the account, asset, and source chain. Polyester shows the deposit address, supported asset contract, minimum amount, route  fee, and estimated time for that route. Send the asset. Transfer the displayed asset on the selected chain to the deposit address assigned to your account. Reach confirmation. The source chain confirms the transaction according to the route's finality  requirement. Validate the deposit. Blockaid screens the transaction, and Zipper validators confirm the transaction, route, amount, and account attribution through a three-quarter quorum. Create the Zipped Asset . Polyester mints the Zipped Asset connected to that exact external route. Credit your account. Funding maps the Zipped Asset to its Unified Asset  and credits Funding or Trading based on your default deposit destination. The amount credited is the deposit amount after the route fee.  Use the route shown on the Deposit page Send the displayed asset on the selected chain and meet its minimum. The deposit address belongs to the active Master Account  or Subaccount  and the selected route. Inside Polyester Once credited, your Unified Asset can move between Funding and Trading or between eligible Polyester accounts. These internal movements do not create another Zipper request or charge another Zipper route fee. The Zipped Asset continues to identify the external route that backs the Unified Asset, but you do not need to convert or manage the Zipped Asset yourself. Withdrawal lifecycle Open the Withdraw page from the account that owns the balance. Choose the Unified Asset, destination chain, amount, address, and destination tag when one is required. Resolve the route. Polyester connects your Unified Asset and destination chain to one enabled Zipped Asset route. Reserve the balance. Your account reserves the withdrawal amount and applicable route fee. Validate the request. Blockaid screens the destination and transaction risk. Zipper checks the route, amount, destination, account permissions, whitelist, fee protection, and vault  liquidity before validators reach a three-quarter quorum. Approve and burn. Cubist's C2F policy and the required MFA  approvals authorize vault signing. Polyester then burns the route-specific Zipped Asset before its native backing can be released. Deliver and finalize. The executor verifies the recipient and amount, broadcasts the signed external transaction, and follows it through destination finality. The withdrawal moves through Pending, Processing, Fulfilling, and Distributed as it advances. If a request ends before external delivery, any eligible principal is returned to your account. Follow the transfer Your transaction history shows the account-facing progress of the deposit or withdrawal. Each request also receives a request or Flow ID that connects it to the relevant external transaction and Zipped Asset mint or burn. Asset Flows shows the public Polyester Chain side of that lifecycle. Related Topics  Overview  See how Zipper moves supported assets between external chains and your Polyester account. Vaults  See how Zipper deposit addresses, custody vaults, and route inventory support deposits and withdrawals. Security  See how Zipper protects deposits, withdrawals, custody, and Zipped Asset supply. Every supported asset on every source chain has its own vault, supply, and redemption path, limiting exposure between different assets and networks. Your deposit address identifies the account and route  receiving a transfer. It is not the same thing as a custody vault. Deposit addresses and vaults Each Master Account  and Subaccount  receives deposit addresses for its supported routes. These addresses let Zipper connect an external transfer to the correct Polyester account. After a deposit is credited, Polyester can move the external asset from the deposit address into a controlled vault. This movement is called a sweep. A sweep organizes custody; it is not another deposit and does not create another account credit or Zipped Asset mint. Vaults can also be separated by chain, asset, signing policy, or operational purpose. This does not change the Unified Asset  shown in your account.  Deposit addresses come from Polyester Use the address shown on the Deposit page for your selected account, asset, and chain. A vault or custody address visible in an explorer is not assigned to your account. Asset and source-chain isolation The same ticker can have several independent custody paths. USDT from Ethereum, USDT from Solana, and USDT from Base each use a separate external vault and a separate Zipped Asset supply on Polyester Chain . Each Zipped Asset is backed one-to-one by the exact native asset held on its originating chain. Activity affecting one asset or source chain remains separated from the vault, supply, and withdrawal path of the others. Route inventory Route inventory is the amount of an external asset available through a specific chain route. Zipper uses that inventory to fulfill withdrawals on the route you select. A route's withdrawal capacity can change based on: available and already reserved inventory; deposits and withdrawals still in progress; the route minimum and fee; chain health and finality ; route or custody status; and signer availability. Your Unified Asset balance can be larger than the amount currently available on one destination chain. Another compatible route may still be available. Zipped Asset supply and vault inventory Zipped Asset supply shows how much of a route is represented on Polyester Chain. Vault inventory shows how much external asset is held, reserved, or moving through that route's custody path. They are connected, but they do not always change at the same moment. Confirmations, pending withdrawals, custody sweeps, fees, and in-flight transactions can temporarily place assets at different stages of the route. How backing is used External assets held as Zipped Asset backing stay inside the Zipper custody purpose. Polyester does not lend them for yield, deploy them into other protocols, rehypothecate them, or send them through another external bridge. Controlled sweeps and approved withdrawals can move backing between custody addresses because those movements continue serving the same deposit and withdrawal system. The mint-and-burn design maintains verifiable one-to-one backing and prevents the same deposit from creating duplicate Zipped Asset supply. For withdrawals, the Zipped Asset burns before the corresponding native backing can leave its source-chain vault. Balancing withdrawal liquidity across source chains The supply available for an asset can differ greatly from one source chain to another. One chain may receive more deposits, while another may process more withdrawals. This can leave a source chain with less of that asset available for future withdrawals. Polyester reviews these supplies daily. When one source chain needs more withdrawal liquidity, Polyester uses Polyester-owned operational funds to make a series of deposits on that chain. Polyester then withdraws the same total amount through a source chain with surplus liquidity.  Example: USDT on Ethereum and Solana Suppose there is 100 million USDT available through Ethereum but only 2 million USDT available through Solana. Polyester can repeatedly deposit its own USDT through Solana and withdraw the same total amount through Ethereum. This increases the USDT supply available for Solana withdrawals while reducing the Ethereum surplus by an equal amount. Every movement follows the normal Zipper lifecycle, including validation, deposit minting, withdrawal burning before release, external delivery, and finality. The custody and contract design does not provide an operational path for Polyester to move Zipped Asset backing directly between vaults or chains. Polyester must use its own funds through the standard lifecycle instead. This separation protects user backing and does not change your Unified Asset balance. Vault balances, deposits, Zipped Asset mints and burns, withdrawals, and circulating supplies can be independently viewed through Polyester Scan . See Asset Lifecycle for deposits and withdrawals and Security for the controls around vault signing and request approval. Related Topics  Overview  See how Zipper moves supported assets between external chains and your Polyester account. Asset Lifecycle  Follow your asset from an external deposit to a Polyester balance and back to an external chain. Security  See how Zipper protects deposits, withdrawals, custody, and Zipped Asset supply. Each request is tied to an exact route , independently validated, recorded through one lifecycle, and allowed to create only one financial result. Polyester works with Cubist to protect the signing keys used by Zipper's external-chain vaults . Cubist's CubeSigner keeps these keys inside hardware-isolated trusted execution environments, or TEEs, and applies policy checks before a vault can sign a transaction. Security throughout the lifecycle Zipper protects an asset movement in seven stages: Exact route. The chain, asset contract, minimum, fee, and destination format must match a supported route. Blockaid screening. Blockaid screens deposits and withdrawals for OFAC sanctions exposure, illicit activity, and wallet or transaction risk. External finality . A deposit reaches the required source-chain confirmations before minting, and Zipper follows a withdrawal through destination finality after release. Independent validation. Zipper validators check the transaction, amount, route, destination, policy, and vault liquidity through a three-quarter quorum. One request state. The request ID connects validation, execution, fees, external transactions, and the final result. Cubist TEE vault signing. An approved withdrawal must pass CubeSigner's C2F policy and required MFA  approvals before its transaction can be signed. Supply and account updates. Deposits mint only after approval. Withdrawals burn the Zipped Asset  before the matching native backing leaves its vault. These layers keep one deposit from minting twice and one withdrawal from producing duplicate external payments. Independent Zipper validator quorum Zipper uses approximately 12 independent validators, with the validator set designed to expand over time. Each validator monitors supported blockchains through its own local RPC infrastructure and reviews deposit and withdrawal evidence independently. A request needs a three-quarter validator quorum before it can continue. For deposits, validators confirm the source transaction, account attribution, asset, amount, confirmations, and screening result before a Zipped Asset can mint. For withdrawals, they review the policy, destination risk, amount, fee, and available vault liquidity. Polyester Chain  validators produce and validate blocks for Polyester Chain. They secure chain consensus but do not independently approve a Zipper deposit or withdrawal. Keeping these roles separate means one system does not control observation, approval, custody signing, chain consensus, and account accounting by itself. How Cubist protects Zipper vaults Cubist is Polyester's security partner for Zipper vault key management. Its CubeSigner system combines a trusted execution environment with an HSM-backed hardware root of trust. Vault keys are generated, stored, and used for signing inside this protected boundary. Raw private keys are never exposed to Zipper validators, Polyester operators, or Zipper application services. The signing process works as follows: Zipper validates the withdrawal and creates an exact transaction intent containing the chain, asset, amount, and destination. The approved intent is sent to CubeSigner as a signing request. Zipper does not retrieve or handle the raw vault private key. Cubist's C2F policy checks the exact transaction against the security rules attached to that vault key, including required MFA and approval conditions. The key can sign only when the policy approves the request. The signing operation happens inside the protected TEE/HSM boundary. CubeSigner returns the signature, while the private key remains protected inside the vault infrastructure. This means access to a Polyester application server is not enough to move vault assets. A withdrawal still needs Zipper approval, an exact transaction intent, and Cubist's independent policy-enforced signature. Cubist's role is focused on secure key storage and transaction signing. Zipper continues to own route validation, request state, validator approval, destination commitment, finality, and the Zipped Asset burn connected to the withdrawal. Deposit protection Before a deposit creates a Zipped Asset, Zipper confirms: the exact chain and asset contract; the receiving address and Polyester account; the amount, minimum, and route fee; the source transaction and required confirmations; the Blockaid sanctions and transaction-risk screening result; that the source event has not already been used; and that a three-quarter validator quorum approved the request. Only an approved request can mint its route-specific Zipped Asset and credit the matching Unified Asset  to your account. Blockaid and OFAC screening Every deposit and withdrawal is screened through Blockaid before processing. Blockaid evaluates the source or destination for OFAC sanctions exposure, illicit activity, and other wallet or transaction risks. The screening result becomes part of Zipper's validation and policy decision. This applies to deposits arriving at your assigned address and withdrawals leaving a Zipper vault, adding an independent transaction-risk layer before assets are minted or released. Withdrawal protection Withdrawal security begins with on-chain checks for the request parameters, fee, destination, and your available funds. Before a withdrawal leaves custody, Zipper confirms: that your account can use the available balance; the destination chain, address, and destination tag when required; the principal, fee, and maximum fee you approved; your permissions, MFA, and withdrawal-whitelist settings; the Blockaid destination-risk screening result; the route's status and available vault liquidity; a three-quarter Zipper validator quorum; and the Cubist C2F policy and MFA approvals required for signing. After approval, the executor verifies the recipient and amount. Polyester burns the route-specific Zipped Asset before the corresponding native asset can leave the source-chain vault. The signed transaction is then broadcast and followed through destination finality. Your account controls Your Master Account  or Subaccount  permissions determine who can request a withdrawal. MFA adds fresh verification to protected actions, while the Withdrawal Whitelist limits which external destinations can receive assets. API keys  follow the same account and route controls and can be narrowed further for one application. Custody and backing External backing remains inside policy-controlled Zipper custody. Application services coordinate requests but do not have unrestricted authority to move vault assets. Approved sweeps can organize assets between controlled custody addresses, and approved withdrawals can deliver them externally. Zipper does not lend, rehypothecate, or deploy the backing into other protocols. Every circulating Zipped Asset remains backed one-to-one by its corresponding native asset. Separate vaults, supplies, and redemption paths for every supported asset and source chain limit exposure between assets and networks. See Vaults for the full custody and source-chain supply model. The Audits page lists published security reports and their scope. Public transparency Vault balances, deposits, Zipped Asset mints and burns, withdrawals, and circulating supplies can be independently viewed through Polyester Scan .  Public evidence, private account details External transactions and Zipped Asset mints or burns are public. Your permissions, balances, whitelists, and complete account-attributed deposit or withdrawal records remain private to your account. Related Topics  Overview  See how Zipper moves supported assets between external chains and your Polyester account. Asset Lifecycle  Follow your asset from an external deposit to a Polyester balance and back to an external chain. Vaults  See how Zipper deposit addresses, custody vaults, and route inventory support deposits and withdrawals. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Polyester Chain   Overview  06/30    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    Polyester Chain  is the EVM-compatible blockchain that supports Polyester accounts and protocol activity. It is built with Cosmos EVM and CometBFT, giving Polyester a dedicated chain for smart accounts , asset movement, account controls, and public contract records. You interact with Polyester Chain through the Polyester product. Polyester Scan  is the browser that organizes and displays the Chain's public blocks, transactions, accounts, tokens, and contracts. What runs on Polyester Chain Polyester Chain hosts the contracts and public records behind: Safe smart accounts for every Master Account  and Subaccount ; Funding Account  asset movements; assets moving into and out of Trading; Zipper  requests and Zipped Asset  mints and burns; internal transfers and withdrawal activity; destination whitelists and other account controls; and ERC-4337 gas sponsorship. These contracts give Polyester one shared on-chain layer for account identity, supported asset movement, and public protocol activity. How an action reaches the Chain Polyester prepares the supported action for your active smart account. Your owner credential authorizes the action. A bundler submits it through the ERC-4337 infrastructure. The relevant Polyester protocol contract executes the action. CometBFT validators include the result in Polyester Chain's block history. Polyester Scan organizes the public transaction, contract, and event information. Polyester sponsors gas for current user-facing Chain actions, so you do not need to hold BALL  to use the product. Public Chain activity and private trading Polyester Chain records public activity such as smart-account calls, protocol transactions, contract events, and Zipped Asset supply changes. Your specific orders, fills, fees, reserved Trading balance, members, permissions, sessions, and complete financial ledger remain private to your account. Spot trades execute through PolyEngine  and do not create a separate public Chain transaction for every fill.  Public activity does not expose your trading account Polyester Scan can show assets entering or leaving your account on-chain. It does not reveal your private Trading balance, open orders, fills, or account-attributed trading history. Browse activity with Polyester Scan Use Polyester Scan to browse Polyester Chain blocks, transactions, smart accounts, contracts, tokens, transfers, and Zipper flows. Scan is a read-only browser. It organizes Chain data but does not execute transactions or change contract state. Explore Polyester Chain Smart Account explains the Safe that represents your Polyester account. Gas Abstraction  explains how Polyester sponsors Chain gas. Validators explains CometBFT consensus and the other approval roles used across Polyester. Related Topics  Smart Account  Understand the Safe smart account that represents your Polyester account. Gas Abstraction  See how Polyester sponsors gas for your supported Polyester Chain actions. Validators  See how Polyester Chain validators secure blocks and how other approval roles remain separate. The Safe address is your account's on-chain identity. Your external or embedded owner wallet  is the non-custodial credential that authorizes it. Your owner wallet and Safe have different addresses and different jobs. The owner approves actions; the Safe executes them. Owner wallet and smart account Your owner wallet can be: an external non-custodial wallet; or an embedded non-custodial wallet created through an available Google or email sign-in. The owner wallet holds the credential used to authorize your Safe. Polyester does not become the owner because it sponsors gas, operates a bundler, or keeps you signed in. The Safe has no single private key or recovery phrase of its own. If you export an embedded wallet key, you are exporting the owner credential, not a separate Safe private key. How your smart account takes action Polyester prepares the call for your active Safe and the relevant protocol contract. Your owner credential authorizes the action. Polyester packages it as an ERC-4337 UserOperation. The Safe validates the authorization and executes the call. Polyester Chain records the resulting transaction and contract events. Your application session, MFA , permissions, and destination controls can add protection before an action reaches the Safe. They do not replace the owner credential. Your address can exist before deployment Polyester can calculate your Safe address before the account contract is deployed. This is called a counterfactual smart account. The address can already support account setup, deposit-address attribution, and product records. The first eligible on-chain action deploys the Safe and executes the requested call together. Creating your account, signing in, receiving a deposit, or trading through PolyEngine  does not necessarily deploy the Safe. A Funding transfer, withdrawal, whitelist change, or another signed on-chain action can become its first deployment.  Your first Chain action can deploy the Safe Deployment does not create a new account or change its address. It places the already predicted Safe contract on Polyester Chain. Master Accounts and Subaccounts Your Master Account and every Subaccount have separate Safe addresses. They can share the same owner wallet while keeping their balances, permissions, members, and activity separate. Switching accounts changes which Safe is active. It does not merge the accounts or move assets between them. Your Safe and your balances The Safe is your account identity and authorization layer, but not every balance appears as tokens held directly at the Safe address. Funding contracts hold route-specific Zipped Assets  and record your Unified Asset  movements. Trading balances, orders, fills, fees, and reservations remain in Polyester's private Trading system. Zipper  vaults  separately hold native external assets that back Zipped Assets. See Sign-In & Ownership for owner credentials and Gas Abstraction  for sponsored smart-account actions. Related Topics  Overview  See how Polyester Chain supports your account, assets, and public on-chain activity. Gas Abstraction  See how Polyester sponsors gas for your supported Polyester Chain actions. Validators  See how Polyester Chain validators secure blocks and how other approval roles remain separate. Polyester pays the underlying Chain gas through ERC-4337 smart-account infrastructure. The action still executes on-chain and uses gas. Sponsorship simply means Polyester pays that cost for you. How sponsorship works Polyester prepares the supported action for your active Safe smart account . The smart-account client packages it as a UserOperation. A bundler prepares and submits the operation. A paymaster sponsors the BALL required for the eligible action. Your owner credential authorizes the operation. ERC-4337 EntryPoint validates it, and your Safe executes the protocol call. The paymaster pays gas but does not authorize the action or own your Safe. Your owner credential and the Safe's rules remain the authorization boundary. What Polyester sponsors Sponsorship covers the Polyester Chain gas used by current user-facing product actions, including eligible Funding movements, withdrawals, internal transfers, deposit-routing changes, and account-control updates. It can also cover the first eligible action for a counterfactual Safe. In that case, the same UserOperation deploys the Safe and executes the action. You do not need to acquire BALL for these supported product flows. Costs outside Chain sponsorship Cost Covered by Polyester Chain gas sponsorship? Supported Polyester Chain product gas YesGas paid by your external wallet when sending a deposit NoZipper  deposit or withdrawal fee NoSpot trading fee NoActivity performed later on an external destination chain No    Zipper fees are charged for moving assets between chains, while trading fees apply to completed fills. They are separate from the BALL used to execute a Polyester Chain contract call.  Sponsored gas is not the same as no fees Polyester pays the BALL required for supported Chain actions. External-chain gas, Zipper fees, and trading fees remain separate. Gas sponsorship and account ownership The bundler and paymaster help submit your action, but neither becomes an owner of your account. They cannot replace your owner credential, bypass your Safe, or ignore your account permissions and security controls. See Smart Account for the owner and Safe relationship and Deposit & Withdrawal Fees for charges outside Chain sponsorship. Related Topics  Overview  See how Polyester Chain supports your account, assets, and public on-chain activity. Smart Account  Understand the Safe smart account that represents your Polyester account. Validators  See how Polyester Chain validators secure blocks and how other approval roles remain separate. Key Concepts   Create Your Account   Secure Your Account   First Deposit & Trade   Funds   Unified Assets   Supported Assets   Funding Account   Trading Account   Deposit Funds   Withdraw Funds   Internal Transfers   Trading   Overview   Trading Screen   Widgets   Overview   Polyester Chart   TradingView Chart   Depth Chart   Order Book   Market Trades   Order Form   Open Orders   Order Triggers   Order History   Funds   Order Types   Market Order   Limit Order   Time-in-Force & Post-Only   Iceberg   TWAP   Ladder   Stop-Loss Market   Stop-Loss Limit   Trailing Stop   Manage Orders   Quick Swap   Fees & VIP   Trading Fees   VIP Tiers   Deposit & Withdrawal Fees   Referrals   Overview   Rewards   Analytics   Account   Dashboard   Access & Security   Sign-In & Ownership   MFA & Recovery   Sessions & Alerts   Address Book & Whitelists   API Keys   Ledger   Overview   Account Statements   Preferences   Overview   Appearance   Language & Region   Sounds   Notifications   Balances   Footer   Subaccounts   Overview   Manage Subaccounts   Members & Roles   Permissions & Policies   Address Book & Whitelists   Audit Logs   API Keys   PolyEngine   Overview   Admission   Matching   Settlement   Zipper    Overview    Asset Lifecycle    Vaults   Security    Polyester Chain   Overview   Smart Account   Gas Abstraction   Validators   Polyester Scan   Overview   zAssets & uAssets   Asset Flows   Chain Activity   Tokens & Chains   Contracts & Tools   Reference   Confirmation Requirements   Polyester Contracts   Audits   Official Links   Glossary   LLMs.txt   Help & Support   FAQs   Feature Requests   Submit a Support Ticket            User Docs /Polyester Chain /Validators   Validators  08/10    Copy as Markdown   View as Markdown    Open in    Polyester Chain  validators use CometBFT consensus to agree on the order of transactions and the resulting public Chain state. They secure Polyester Chain blocks, contract execution, receipts, and event logs. Polyester also uses other validators, approvers, and signers for specific product actions. Those roles have separate responsibilities and do not replace Chain consensus. How Chain consensus works A transaction or sponsored UserOperation reaches Polyester Chain. A validator proposes an ordered block. The validator set executes and evaluates the block under the Chain's CometBFT rules. Consensus commits the block and its resulting EVM state. Polyester Scan  organizes the public block, transactions, receipts, and events. Consensus gives every Polyester Chain contract the same ordered view of public state. Separate approval roles Role Responsibility Polyester Chain validators Secure CometBFT blocks, transaction ordering, and canonical Chain state.Zipper  validators Approve supported external deposits and withdrawals.Trading withdrawal approvers Approve the exact intent for an eligible withdrawal from Trading.Guard Signer Adds approval to protected Funding and account-control changes.Cubist vault  signing Applies TEE-backed signing policies before external vault assets can move.Safe owner Authorizes actions for the user's smart account .    An approval in one layer does not grant authority in another. For example, a Zipper validator approves a cross-chain request but does not produce Polyester Chain blocks or control a user's Safe.  Zipper quorum and Chain consensus are different Zipper validators review deposit and withdrawal requests. Polyester Chain validators secure blocks through CometBFT. Each system has its own responsibility and approval rules. Layered protection Polyester combines several security boundaries: your owner credential and Safe rules authorize smart-account actions; protocol contracts enforce their account, balance, and asset rules; Polyester Chain validators secure the resulting public state; Zipper validators and Cubist protect cross-chain asset movement; Guard approvals protect selected account-control changes; and PolyEngine  keeps private trading execution and settlement separate from public Chain consensus. No single signer controls every layer. View public consensus activity Use Polyester Scan to browse blocks, transactions, receipts, contracts, token activity, and Zipper events recorded on Polyester Chain. Scan displays the public result of consensus. It does not participate in consensus, approve transactions, or change Chain state. See Zipper Security for request validation and vault signing, and Smart Account for account authorization. Related Topics  Overview  See how Polyester Chain supports your account, assets, and public on-chain activity. Smart Account  Understand the Safe smart account that represents your Polyester account. It organizes blocks, transactions, accounts, tokens, contracts, and Zipper  flows in one searchable place. You do not need to connect an account to browse. Scan is read-only, so viewing a record never changes your account or submits a transaction.       What you can explore Area What it shows Chain activity Blocks, transactions, addresses, contract calls, logs, and token transfersAssets Tokens, route-specific Zipped Assets , Unified Assets , and supported chainsAsset flows The complete journey of a deposit, withdrawal, or internal transferContracts Verified source code, public contract data, and available read or write methods    The home page also shows live activity and network summaries. Open any row to see the complete record and its related links. Find a record Use the global search when you already have an identifier. Scan can search by: address; transaction hash; block number or hash; token name, symbol, or contract; Unified Asset; chain; or Flow ID. An exact address, hash, contract, or Flow ID gives the most direct result. A broader search can show several result types together, which is useful when one symbol represents more than one asset route .  The full asset identity matters Two assets can share the same name or symbol. The source chain and contract address identify the exact asset and route shown in Scan. Public activity and private account data Scan displays public Polyester Chain records and approved public Zipper flow information. This includes assets entering or leaving an account, public smart-account actions, contract events, and Zipped Asset supply changes. Your Trading balance, orders, fills, account permissions, sessions, and complete financial ledger remain private. Scan does not expose that information simply because the related account has a public blockchain address. Explore Polyester Scan zAssets & uAssets explains how route-specific Zipped Assets connect to one Unified Asset balance. Asset Flows follows deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers from start to finish. Chain Activity covers blocks, transactions, addresses, and public execution details. Tokens & Chains helps you browse supported asset routes and their source chains. Contracts & Tools covers verified contracts, filters, exports, statistics, gas, and APIs. Related Topics  zAssets & uAssets  See how route-specific Zipped Assets connect to one Unified Asset balance. Asset Flows  Follow deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers from start to finish in Polyester Scan. Chain Activity  Browse Polyester Chain blocks, transactions, addresses, and public execution details. Tokens & Chains  Browse assets, token transfers, and the source chains connected to Polyester. Contracts & Tools  Explore verified contracts and use Polyester Scan's filters, exports, statistics, gas, and API tools. A Zipped Asset , or zAsset, represents one asset from one source chain. A Unified Asset , or uAsset, brings compatible Zipped Assets together as one account-facing balance. For example, USDT deposited from Ethereum and USDT deposited from Solana create separate Zipped Assets. When both routes  map to Unified USDT, you see one USDT balance in your Polyester account. Browse Unified Assets The Unified Assets directory lists each Unified Asset with its supported chains, Unified Asset ID, Ledger ID, decimals, and combined Zipped Asset supply.       Expand a row to see every route behind that asset. Each route includes its source chain, Polyester contract, and source-chain contract. Native assets show Native instead of a source contract address. On a Unified Asset page, you can use: Flows to see related deposits, withdrawals, and transfers; Zipped Assets to compare the routes that contribute to the balance; Info to see IDs, decimals, and route metadata; and Holders when holder information is available.       Browse a Zipped Asset Open a Zipped Asset from the Tokens directory, a transfer, a Flow, or a Unified Asset page. Its detail page connects the route's source chain and source asset to the corresponding contract on Polyester Chain .       It can also show transfers, holders, flows, supply, and contract information. The supply shown here belongs to this individual source-chain route. A Verified badge means Scan recognizes the asset from Polyester's configured catalog.  One symbol can represent several routes USDT from Ethereum and USDT from Solana can use the same symbol while remaining separate Zipped Assets. Their source chains and contract addresses show which route each one represents. Use Asset Flows to follow a specific movement, or Tokens & Chains to explore the routes available in Scan. Related Topics  Overview  Explore public Polyester Chain activity, assets, contracts, and cross-chain flows. Asset Flows  Follow deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers from start to finish in Polyester Scan. Chain Activity  Browse Polyester Chain blocks, transactions, addresses, and public execution details. Tokens & Chains  Browse assets, token transfers, and the source chains connected to Polyester. Contracts & Tools  Explore verified contracts and use Polyester Scan's filters, exports, statistics, gas, and API tools. Instead of making you follow several separate records, Polyester Scan  brings the movement, status, amounts, and linked transactions into one journey. The three Flow types Flow What it follows Deposit An asset moving from an external chain into your Polyester accountWithdrawal An asset moving from Polyester to an address on a supported external chainInternal transfer An asset moving between supported Polyester accounts or balance areas    A Flow is not one blockchain transaction. It can link an external transaction, one or more Polyester Chain  transactions, validator activity, and a private ledger settlement into one understandable record. Find a Flow Open the Flows directory to browse recent activity. You can filter by Flow type, account, chain, transaction, asset, or status.       Each row shows the direction, asset, linked records, elapsed time, current stage, and overall status. Open a row to see its complete Summary and Journey. Read the Summary and Journey The Summary shows what moved and where it went. It includes the asset, principal amount, fee, final amount, source, destination, account, and available transaction links. The Journey shows how the movement progressed. Depending on the Flow, it can include: source-chain confirmations; Zipper  validator approval; a Zipped Asset  mint or burn; a Funding or Trading balance update; and destination-chain delivery. Deposit and withdrawal Flows  contain more stages because they cross networks. An internal transfer usually contains only the observed transfer and its ledger settlement.        Deposit Withdrawal Internal transfer                  Understand the status Status Meaning Pending The Flow is still moving through its required stagesCompleted The expected final stage has finishedFailed or Dropped Processing ended without the intended completionRefunded The Flow ended through its supported refund path    The progress bar shows how far the Flow has moved through its lifecycle. A terminal Flow can show 100% whether it completed, failed, or refunded, so the written status remains the clearest result.  A Flow can contain different kinds of records A linked hexadecimal hash usually opens a blockchain transaction. A ledger settlement reference records a Polyester balance step and is clearly labeled as not being a Polyester Chain transaction. Follow the linked records Transaction links take you to the public record for that stage. External-chain links open the relevant network explorer, while Polyester Chain links remain in Polyester Scan. You can also open the related account, Zipped Asset, Unified Asset , or source chain directly from the Flow. This makes the Flow the easiest starting point when you want to understand the complete journey of one asset movement. Related Topics  Overview  Explore public Polyester Chain activity, assets, contracts, and cross-chain flows. zAssets & uAssets  See how route-specific Zipped Assets connect to one Unified Asset balance. Chain Activity  Browse Polyester Chain blocks, transactions, addresses, and public execution details. Tokens & Chains  Browse assets, token transfers, and the source chains connected to Polyester. Contracts & Tools  Explore verified contracts and use Polyester Scan's filters, exports, statistics, gas, and API tools. You can browse recent blocks and transactions or open a specific hash, block, or address to see its details. Browse chain records Page What you can see Transactions Confirmed transactions, methods, blocks, addresses, amounts, and feesPending Transactions Transactions waiting to be included in a blockInternal Transactions Contract calls and internal value movements created during executionBlocks Block production, included transactions, gas, fees, and producer informationAccounts Public addresses and their indexed Polyester Chain activity    The main lists update as new records arrive. When useful, Download Page Data exports the rows currently shown in the table.       Transactions Blocks             Read a transaction The Overview gives you the transaction's result and main details. A Success status means the Chain execution completed without reverting. Failed means it reverted, while Pending means it has not yet reached a final Chain result. Use the tabs when you want more detail: Tab What it shows Token Transfers ERC-20 transfers, mints, and burnsInternal Txns Calls or value movements created inside the transactionLogs Events emitted by the contracts involvedState Indexed before-and-after changes created by execution    If the transaction belongs to a deposit, withdrawal, or transfer Flow, Scan also shows a Flow summary with links to the other lifecycle stages. Read a block A block groups transactions that were included together. Its Overview can show the block height, time, transaction count, producer, gas use, base fee, burned fees, and the hashes that connect it to the surrounding Chain history. Additional tabs provide the transactions and internal calls within the block. Consensus, MEV, and blob information appears when the active Chain supplies it. Read an address An address page adapts to the type of address you open: a regular wallet address shows its public balance and activity; a Safe smart account  adds smart-account and Flow information; and a contract can add source code, contract methods, proxy information, and trusted Polyester labels. All of these pages show public Polyester Chain activity. They do not reveal the person behind an address or the private contents of a Polyester account.  Internal transaction and internal transfer mean different things An internal transaction is a contract call or value movement created during Chain execution. A Polyester internal transfer moves an asset between supported account or balance areas and can be followed as an Asset Flow. Use Asset Flows when you want the complete deposit, withdrawal, or transfer journey rather than one Chain transaction. Related Topics  Overview  Explore public Polyester Chain activity, assets, contracts, and cross-chain flows. zAssets & uAssets  See how route-specific Zipped Assets connect to one Unified Asset balance. Asset Flows  Follow deposits, withdrawals, and internal transfers from start to finish in Polyester Scan. Tokens & Chains  Browse assets, token transfers, and the source chains connected to Polyester. Contracts & Tools  Explore verified contracts and use Polyester Scan's filters, exports, statistics, gas, and API tools.
